# Lab notebook {#sec-notebook}

::: {.callout-important title="Scientific agenda, not engineering log"}
This notebook records research questions, rival hypotheses, decisive evidence,
corrections, belief changes, and program decisions. It does not specify jobs,
model configurations, optimization schedules, or implementation plans.

The complete experimental chronology remains in
`results/notebook_full_chronology_through_2026-07-29.qmd`. The more detailed
ledger that preceded this scope correction is preserved verbatim in
`results/research_ledger_detailed_snapshot_2026-07-29.qmd`. Those archives are
provenance, not the active research argument.
:::

“Registered” means the deciding pattern was written before the result was
seen. “Exploratory” means useful for forming a hypothesis but not confirming
one. “Invalid” means the instrument could not answer the stated question.
Corrections to earlier interpretations are marked **EDIT**.

Iterations 1--6 predate the notebook and are summarized in @sec-learned-bie,
@sec-parametric, and @sec-3d-results.

## Current research agenda {#sec-nb-current-agenda}

**EDIT (2026-07-31): this agenda is superseded.** The four transfer-cause
questions below are retired by the program decision at
@sec-nb-model-quality-agenda: the program returns to model quality —
accuracy, graceful degradation, discretization indifference, and
simplicity, on one frozen scorecard — and stops designing transfer
instruments. The text below is retained as the record of the superseded
agenda.

The long-term goal is an accurate surrogate that remains useful when boundary
conditions, geometry, discretization, or PDE parameters change. The evidence
does not yet identify such an architecture. It supports four questions, in
this order:

| Research question | Present evidence | Evidence that would decide it |
|---|---|---|
| Which source--target relations create reusable knowledge? | Recent work already shows geometry transfer and target-data savings in several settings, while this program's first untouched vehicle-family transfer failed. | Evidence that crosses geometry similarity with boundary-response compatibility and controls boundary-drive coverage, rather than crediting “pretraining” as one undifferentiated cause. |
| Is any benefit specific to physical structure? | Boundary-aware structure has produced large gains on controlled problems, but several plausible physical additions were neutral or harmful. | A matched structured model repeatedly improves transfer or scaling where a steel-manned generic model does not. |
| How broad is the reusable principle? | Ordered propagation and licensed boundary structure work in more than one controlled setting, but not yet across distinct propagation classes at realistic breadth. | The same high-level principle improves a second, different class without changing the claim after seeing results. |
| Does a general program repay its complexity? | No cost-weighted evidence exists yet. | Repeated target-data or compute savings exceed the cost of pretraining, added structure, and maintenance. |

**EDIT (2026-07-29):** the first version made the existence of geometry
transfer the open question. The literature audit in
@sec-nb-literature-transfer-cause found that this was too broad: transfer and
data savings already occur in credible settings. The open question is which
relationship causes the saving and whether boundary-aware structure adds to
strong generic pretraining.

**EDIT (2026-07-29):** “geometry, physics, or diversity” was still an
incomplete task taxonomy. For a boundary-driven problem, the boundary operator,
the observable, and the distribution of boundary drives help determine the
response that can be learned. The refined hypothesis is developed in
@sec-nb-boundary-response-hypothesis and corrected into a prospective
relation vector in @sec-nb-prospective-relation-vector. The smallest
identifiable causal contrast is derived in @sec-nb-two-mode-transfer-test,
with its distance control corrected in @sec-nb-spectral-crossover and its
statistical scope corrected in @sec-nb-rich-transfer-task. The first concrete
preregistration is @sec-nb-broadband-prereg.

**EDIT (2026-07-29):** the rectangle analysis narrows the first question
again. It contrasts aspect-ratio alignment with screening alignment, not broad
morphology with broad physics. An exact adaptation null
(@sec-nb-adaptation-null) and the target response-tangent metric
(@sec-nb-response-tangent-metric) now provide the leading account: source
usefulness may follow response-space direction, while smooth boundary spectra
can make the nominal causal factors nearly indistinguishable.
The first prospective three-regime contrast is frozen in
@sec-nb-response-direction-sweep; it holds target information and source
distance fixed while rotating the exact response directions.
@sec-nb-two-route-response-test adds a matched excitation-support route at
fixed screening, so a route-specific residual can now falsify the
response-direction account.

**EDIT (2026-07-29):** @sec-nb-one-field-demixing withdraws the rectangle as
a target-simulation-efficiency experiment. Sixteen equal-energy response
modes do not require sixteen target fields: separability lets one full field
reveal every modal profile. The distance and response-direction analyses
remain useful, but only as analytic task geometry until the empirical test is
moved to a nonseparable setting. @sec-nb-nonseparable-response-gate supplies
the first replacement that passes this analytic gate.
@sec-nb-target-saturation rejects its first learning instrument before any
source-transfer result is inspected.

**EDIT (2026-07-29):** @sec-nb-spectral-priors-close closes the replacement
spectral-instrument branch as well. A smooth frequency prior could not
represent the response accurately, while an exact uncoupled carrier left
unseen mode conversion largely unidentified until full directional coverage.
The first research question now moves to a geometry-bearing adaptation curve
on fresh SHIFT-SUV cases; no further compact-state variant is on the active
agenda.

Four rival program hypotheses remain live:

1. **Boundary-response reuse.** Sharing the physical structure of the map from
   boundary data to the requested field makes source experience
   disproportionately valuable.
2. **Geometry-scaffold reuse.** Similar morphology is valuable even when the
   boundary-response law changes.
3. **Diversity-driven reuse.** Broad source diversity is more important than
   close similarity; a capable generic model extracts the useful regularities.
4. **Specialist families.** The relevant PDE and geometry families share too
   little for either approach to yield dependable reuse.

The architectural question cuts across the first two hypotheses: does
boundary-aware structure provide an incremental advantage after the strongest
generic pretraining effect is accounted for?

## 2026-07-03 to 2026-07-05 — Controlled studies established conditional structure {#sec-nb-controlled-program}

These studies asked which representational restrictions survive controlled
changes in boundary data, dimension, and PDE family. Their collective result
is conditional rather than architectural: some physical structure is useful,
but no component is universally beneficial.

### Boundary-to-query propagation escaped a finite-moment wall {#sec-nb-iter7}

A learned boundary-to-query kernel transmitted modes that a fixed finite set
of global moments could not represent. This established an information-path
advantage, not a universal decoder.

### Nonlinear drive dependence was necessary on Liouville {#sec-nb-iter8}

Every drive-linear model remained on the predicted superposition wall, while
a zero-preserving nonlinear read-in crossed it across seeds. Smooth learned
kernel members did not provide a reliable additional gain.

### The screened-kernel failure was not a physical verdict {#sec-nb-iter9}

The generic model varied smoothly with screening, but the historical
specialist collapsed near the Laplace limit.

**EDIT (2026-07-29):** that specialist used an inconsistent normalization,
omitted a material self interaction, and became numerically unstable. The
measurements remain observations; the claimed inherent failure of screened
kernels is withdrawn.

### Dimensional transfer held; the first 3D explanation did not {#sec-nb-iter10}

The same core representation ran in three dimensions. The apparent benefit of
extra smooth members was later traced to their compensation for a harmful
polynomial dictionary, not to a dimension-dependent reversal.

### A smaller singular dictionary beat broader alternatives {#sec-nb-iter11}

On controlled Laplace tests, singular-only structure matched or beat larger
physical and learned dictionaries on interpolation and frequency transfer.
Recognizable extra terms did not justify their complexity.

### The dictionary result generalized with a nonlinear exception {#sec-nb-iter12}

The smaller dictionary remained strong in 3D and screened settings but failed
on nonlinear Liouville. The scientific lesson is to add flexibility only
after the simpler licensed span measurably fails.

### Scalar state was sufficient only on the easiest family {#sec-nb-iter14}

Scalar propagation matched the typed model on 2D Laplace but degraded on
screened and 3D problems. Richer state is conditionally necessary, not
automatically useful.

### Generic attention did not close the controlled gap {#sec-nb-iter15}

A matched generic attention baseline was worse in the streaming regime and
violated a similarity contract. Because that was not its native regime, the
claim remained provisional.

### The gap persisted on a fixed solver-labeled dataset {#sec-nb-iter17}

Matched-size and larger generic controls remained worse on the fixed dataset,
including trace-frequency transfer. This supports a boundary-aware inductive
bias within the declared family.

### A classical kernel term could still be harmful {#sec-nb-iter16}

An added single-layer member failed its predicted topology benefit and harmed
frequency transfer. A physically meaningful basis function is not helpful
when its use is unconstrained by the governing boundary relation.

### Nonlocal boundary processing was conditional {#sec-nb-iter18}

Removing boundary self-attention was neutral on all-Dirichlet problems. The
null result was expected from their near-local trace structure and was not
generalized beyond that scope.

### Mixed boundary conditions justified one nonlocal layer {#sec-nb-iter19}

On mixed-condition problems, one boundary-attention layer earned a measurable
gain. Additional depth did not establish a broader scaling law.

### Refinement transferred, but dense interaction cost remained {#sec-nb-iter20}

Predictions improved under boundary refinement without retraining. The result
supports discretization transfer while leaving the cost of dense pairwise
interaction unresolved.

### Potential flow exposed a missing representation type {#sec-nb-iter21}

The first potential-flow target lay outside the model's parity and output
class. The failure was representational, not evidence that boundary
propagation itself had failed.

### Making the target representable removed the wall {#sec-nb-iter22}

Once the declared output class could express the solution, the large error
wall disappeared. This separated information transport from output
expressivity.

### A pseudoscalar extension passed its prediction {#sec-nb-iter23}

Adding the missing parity type recovered the intended rotational response.
The result licenses parity-aware state when the observable demands it.

### An intrinsic length gauge remained a hypothesis {#sec-nb-iter24}

Similarity arguments favored an intrinsic geometric scale, but later
industrial tests showed that a theoretically natural normalization is not
automatically a drop-in improvement.

### Nonlinear output degree had to be representable {#sec-nb-iter25}

Euler--Bernoulli tests confirmed that an output class lacking the required
quadratic dependence cannot learn it through more optimization.

### Exact contracts helped only when correctly specified {#sec-nb-iter26}

Hard constraints improved fidelity when they matched the admitted PDE
problem. Later validity failures showed that an incorrect “exact” contract
can be worse than a flexible approximation.

### Far-field decay required separate evidence {#sec-nb-iter27}

Near-field accuracy did not guarantee the correct asymptotic response.
Far-field behavior must be scored as its own scientific claim.

### Licensed decay improved the tail but did not solve the family {#sec-nb-iter30}

A decay-aware form helped the intended asymptotic regime, yet did not justify
hard-coding the same law on viscous industrial flows.

### One full-width head was the parsimonious default {#sec-nb-iter31}

Splitting capacity across several heads did not provide a consistent advantage
over one full-width head in the controlled suite.

### The cross-suite result was noninferiority, not superiority {#sec-nb-iter32}

The simpler head matched the tested families without material loss. The
evidence does not establish that it is universally better.

### Rotational Euler exposed an operator-parameter failure {#sec-nb-iter33}

Interpolation remained strong while extrapolation across a physical parameter
failed, separating family fit from operator transfer.

### Two nonlinear blowups shared an expressivity defect {#sec-nb-iter34}

Apparently different failures were traced to the same missing output degree,
weakening explanations based on optimizer instability.

### Declaring quadratic degree was the constructive repair {#sec-nb-iter35}

The minimal degree-aware extension crossed the registered bar. It earned a
specific representational capability, not a general nonlinear module.

### Solver-labeled Navier--Stokes exposed the next limit {#sec-nb-iter36}

The controlled surrogate reached a regime where solution quality and model
error could no longer be interpreted independently of the steady solver's
physical validity.

### The low-Reynolds band corrected the first explanation {#sec-nb-iter37}

Performance did not vary monotonically with Reynolds number. The earlier
single-direction difficulty story was withdrawn.

### Parity, capacity, and read-in class were separated {#sec-nb-iter38}

The factorial comparison showed that these mechanisms could not be credited
to one another. The remaining claims are component- and family-specific.

## 2026-07-05 to 2026-07-27 — Industrial studies found fit, then failed transfer {#sec-nb-industrial-program}

The industrial branch established that the surrogate can fit demanding CFD
families and compete with generic baselines in distribution. It did not
establish transfer to a new vehicle family.

### The program pivoted to AirFRANS and DrivAerML {#sec-nb-industrial-pivot}

The research moved from controlled PDEs to solver-labeled airfoil and vehicle
flows to test whether the earlier principles held on realistic geometry and
viscous responses.

### Parity transferred; a declared far-field law did not {#sec-nb-airfrans-v1}

Parity-aware state improved AirFRANS, while a hard point-singularity decay law
hurt. The industrial response did not obey the borrowed asymptotic contract.

### Learned capacity beat a declared viscous scale {#sec-nb-h4-verdict}

A flexible capacity control decisively outperformed the proposed
viscous-length feature. Physical familiarity did not make that feature a
useful representation.

### Log-radial geometry features helped with an instability caveat {#sec-nb-v-verdicts}

Log-radial pair features improved AirFRANS, but some runs were unstable. The
effect was promising within-family evidence, not a transfer result.

### Angle-of-attack extrapolation supported the parity explanation {#sec-nb-extrapolation}

The parity-aware improvement persisted beyond the training angle range,
strengthening the scoped mechanism claim.

### Trace information gave only a small uncertain benefit {#sec-nb-t1-verdict}

The first trace-mode comparison suggested a modest gain whose uncertainty did
not justify a broad architectural conclusion.

### A lower learning rate traded anomalies for accuracy {#sec-nb-tail-verdict}

Reducing late-training instability also reduced the best achieved accuracy.
The result was an optimization trade-off, not a scientific advance.

### Large-batch behavior revealed optimization sensitivity {#sec-nb-b22-verdict}

Changing batch and update structure materially changed the fitted model. This
limits claims drawn from unmatched training budgets.

### Reynolds difficulty was U-shaped {#sec-nb-e1-curve}

Both ends of the tested Reynolds range were harder than the middle, refuting a
simple monotone extrapolation story.

### The steady-solver study had a practical Reynolds ceiling {#sec-nb-re-ceiling-final}

Beyond roughly Reynolds 5000, solver and modeling limitations became too
entangled for clean surrogate conclusions.

### DrivAerML exposed a scale-sensitive drive path {#sec-nb-drivaer-smoke}

The vehicle benchmark revealed sensitivity to the chosen physical scale. This
motivated, but did not validate, intrinsic normalization.

### The first global baseline comparison was inconclusive {#sec-nb-hground-verdict}

Coverage and protocol differences prevented the initial DrivAerML comparison
from isolating architecture.

### Rival explanations for the generic-model gap were registered {#sec-nb-geot-gap}

The gap could have arisen from loss weighting, optimizer settings, input
information, or architecture. These were kept separate before follow-up.

### No single field or optimizer explained the gap {#sec-nb-geot-gap-verdict}

The controlled follow-up rejected simple field-weighting and optimizer
stories. A residual architecture or information difference remained.

### Configuration inspection excluded an optimizer explanation {#sec-nb-t3-launch}

The compared training configurations did not support attributing the gap to a
hidden optimizer advantage.

### Trace mode was treated as a scientific intervention {#sec-nb-trace-mode}

The trace pathway was evaluated as a candidate information channel, not
bundled into a larger model without explicit attribution.

### Trace information helped, but less than predicted {#sec-nb-trace-verdict}

The effect was real but missed its registered magnitude. It therefore narrowed
rather than confirmed the original mechanism claim.

### The trace factorial isolated a dominant channel {#sec-nb-trace-factorial-verdict}

Most of the benefit came from one pathway; the broader story that every trace
component was necessary was withdrawn.

### Depth helped more than rank {#sec-nb-t2-verdict}

A controlled capacity ladder favored additional processing depth over a
larger low-rank state. This remained an in-distribution result.

### Three plausible local corrections were null {#sec-nb-probes-verdict}

None of the tested local-corrector hypotheses materially improved the base
model. The nulls prevented post-hoc credit assignment.

### Several supported changes stacked in distribution {#sec-nb-flagship-verdict}

The combined model improved DrivAerML fit. Composition of in-distribution
gains did not itself predict cross-family transfer.

### Learned kernel members had conditional value {#sec-nb-factorial-verdict}

The factorial rejected both “exact kernels suffice” and “structure never
helps.” The benefit depended on the surrounding representation.

### Scale and iteration effects were separated {#sec-nb-hc2}

The study asked whether improvement came from more parameters or merely more
optimization steps.

### Parameters, not extra iterations, carried most of the gain {#sec-nb-hc2-verdict}

The matched comparison favored model scale as the main source of improvement.

### Scaling was registered against the rival's budget {#sec-nb-scalelaw}

The relevant question was whether the surrogate retained an advantage at
comparable parameter scale, not whether a small baseline could be beaten.

### Scaling improved predictably but with flattening returns {#sec-nb-scalelaw-verdict}

Larger models reduced error, while marginal gains diminished. The result
supported scaling within-family, not unbounded benefit.

### The gap remained at the generic model's parameter budget {#sec-nb-x2l8-verdict}

The structured model retained a matched-budget advantage on DrivAerML. That
advantage later failed to imply differential family-shift robustness.

### More source support helped strongly {#sec-nb-sr-verdict}

Increasing geometric sampling resolution materially improved fit. Coverage,
query resolution, and scoring measure could not yet be cleanly separated.

### Batch size changed the optimization outcome {#sec-nb-mn-verdict}

The large-batch control confirmed that nominal compute alone does not make two
training protocols scientifically equivalent.

### Within-family geometry shifts were declared separately {#sec-nb-ood-protocol}

The OOD protocol isolated geometry axes inside the vehicle family rather than
mixing them with a new family.

### Initial zero-shot results were limited by tiny clean subsets {#sec-nb-ood-zeroshot}

No sharp within-family cliff appeared, but the sample support was too small
for a strong architecture claim.

### The generic baseline showed no clear robustness separation {#sec-nb-geot-ood-zeroshot}

Both models degraded similarly on the initial zero-shot split.

### A corrected vector metric exposed wall-shear failure {#sec-nb-corrected-zeroshot}

**EDIT:** the earlier magnitude-only score hid directional wall-shear error.
Under the corrected vector metric, both models lost important information.

### Absolute within-family transfer remained viable {#sec-nb-ood-deep-verdict}

With stronger models, absolute performance on the declared within-family
shifts remained useful.

### The structured robustness advantage was modest {#sec-nb-deep-differential}

The differential benefit was far smaller than the in-distribution accuracy
gap and did not support a universal transfer claim.

### External review forced three material corrections {#sec-nb-review}

The review identified metric, attribution, and scope problems. Correcting them
weakened the headline without erasing the underlying measurements.

### Exact kernels did not explain the industrial flagship {#sec-nb-factorial-verdict-industrial}

The industrial factorial showed that exact dictionary members were not the
dominant source of the flagship gain.

### Dictionary choice did not change the robustness slope {#sec-nb-rider-verdict}

Exact and learned variants degraded similarly under the within-family shift.
Their difference was mainly absolute fit or efficiency, not robustness.

### The five-seed wall-shear result remained provisional {#sec-nb-seal-verdict}

Replication narrowed uncertainty but did not resolve the limited target
support or metric-scope caveats.

### A cross-family transfer test was sealed before evaluation {#sec-nb-crossfamily-prereg}

Untouched vehicle-family data were reserved to test whether the trained model
carried useful knowledge beyond its source family.

### Cross-family transfer failed decisively {#sec-nb-crossfam-verdict}

The model's error rose far beyond its within-family scale on the untouched
vehicle family. This is the program's strongest negative result and the main
reason a universal architecture remains unearned.

### Synthetic mechanisms were stronger than the industrial claim {#sec-nb-checkin-2}

The program check-in separated convincing controlled mechanisms from weak
industrial generalization. It ended the practice of treating in-distribution
fit as transfer evidence.

### Intrinsic-gauge calibration violated the intended protocol {#sec-nb-gauge-calib}

The first gauge follow-up used target information in a way that prevented a
clean transfer interpretation.

### The repaired train-only recalibration reproduced the constant {#sec-nb-gauge-recalibration}

Rerunning the calibration through the exact 435-case train sampler gives
C = 26.48436 against the contaminated 26.47659 -- a 0.029% change. The
protocol violation was real; its numerical effect on the constant was
immaterial, so the dependent retrains stand as measurements while their
protocol label stays historical
([artifact](../results/intrinsic_gauge_recalibration_2026-07-27/intrinsic_gauge_calibration_train_only_2026-07-27.json)).

### The intrinsic gauge was not a drop-in transformation {#sec-nb-gauge-accept-verdict}

When evaluated fairly, the theoretically natural scale did not preserve the
source model's behavior.

### Transfer-v2 required retraining before target inspection {#sec-nb-transfer-v2-prereg}

The revised question separated a trained intrinsic representation
from post-hoc coordinate changes.

### Measure matching did not explain the transfer failure {#sec-nb-measmech-verdict}

The registered causal prediction failed. Matching the proposed geometric
measure did not recover transfer.

### Initialization weakened the normalization mechanism story {#sec-nb-measnorm-caveat}

The normalization effect was visible before learning, suggesting that part of
the observed behavior belonged to parameterization rather than learned
physics.

### Subsampling was a biased operator; the model's contract held {#sec-nb-hdi-summary}

Under boundary refinement the discretization-invariance contract
held, while random subsampling changed the represented operator: its bias is
a far-field completeness effect of the missing surface, which no reweighting
of the retained cells can repair. "Random subsampling" also named two
different operators across experiments (production cyclic contiguous blocks
versus simple-random diagnostics). Full record: archived chronology,
`sec-nb-hdi-verdict`.

### A missing measure-scale invariance was found and fixed exactly {#sec-nb-hms-summary}

The model was measurably sensitive to the nuisance magnitude of the source
measure. The repair (`measure_normalization`) composes one normalizing factor
into the public measure weights, restoring the invariance by construction;
the unifying claim that this one mechanism explained the transfer failures
was then demoted by its own falsifier. Full record: archived chronology,
`sec-nb-hms-prereg`.

### Accuracy was resolution-specific: a sharp minimum at the training resolution {#sec-nb-hcc-summary}

Varying nothing but sampling resolution around one trained checkpoint showed
pattern error minimized sharply at the training resolution and degrading
catastrophically above it. Within-family accuracy was therefore partly a
coverage-specific compensation, not resolution-transferable operator quality
(@sec-drivaerml-coverage). Full record: archived chronology,
`sec-nb-hcc-verdict`.

### The declared-degree wave answered its secondary question, not its primary {#sec-nb-wave-summary}

Six pre-registered arms (declared drive degrees and invariance fixes) all
failed the resolution-bounding criterion; the size of that failure became the
finding, and the homogeneous (degree-one) arm won the cross-family criterion
reproducibly. Diagnostic tracing located the amplification in the member MLP
and Gram-invariant formation rather than the predicted stage. Full record:
archived chronology, `sec-nb-wave-verdict`.

### The seed outranked the architecture at cross-family scale {#sec-nb-hseed-summary}

Five seeds of one arm spanned a 2491x range of cross-family error against a
pre-registered 3x reproducibility bar; an earlier 1.23x advantage was an
n=2 mirage, and a planned third experiment broke the seed
ranking. Any future cross-family comparison without seed replication is
uninterpretable -- including the current adaptation branch, whose pilot is
one training seed per cell by declared limitation. Full record: archived
chronology, `sec-nb-homog-seeds-verdict` and `sec-nb-seed-transfer-caveat`.

### Coverage augmentation was not accepted as architecture evidence {#sec-nb-hca-launch}

Adding broader source coverage could repair deployment performance, but such a
repair would test data coverage rather than intrinsic transfer.

### Singularity subtraction replicated with a smaller effect {#sec-nb-subtraction-replication}

The correction remained useful, but earlier gains were overstated by roughly
four to ten times. It supports singularity-aware numerical treatment, not a
complete industrial-transfer explanation.

### The industrial branch stopped widening {#sec-program-review}

The failed untouched-family test and unresolved measurement confounds shifted
the branch from architecture search to evidence repair. This anchor names
the 2026-07-27 audit, whose concrete findings were: several post-07-20
results were prose-only, with "preregistrations" committed minutes before
their verdicts; the same 20-case SHIFT pilot served as a development set for
successive hypotheses; exact configs and raw predictions were often absent;
the supposedly train-only gauge calibration iterated all 484 cases including
the held-out split (@sec-nb-gauge-calib); chained jobs replayed an
end-of-epoch scheduler step and reset fp16 scaler state on resume, so
chained trajectories were not the trajectories being compared (both defects
are since fixed in the recipe's checkpoint path); the recorded wall-shear
metric was a whole-field Frobenius norm while later prose described a
pointwise mean; and "random subsampling" named two different operators
(@sec-nb-hdi-summary). The audit's full text and per-claim relabeling are
preserved in the archived chronology
(`results/notebook_full_chronology_through_2026-07-29.qmd`) and in the
EDIT-annotated artifacts themselves
(`results/crossfamily_transfer_2026-07-22.json`); which defects justify
reruns is decided in @sec-nb-validity-triage.

### The replay campaign certified the canonical geometry path {#sec-nb-hqc-campaign}

The evidence-repair campaign (H-QC and the historical-k10000 replays,
2026-07-27..28) closed with three registered verdicts. The cast-once
canonical source-geometry API is byte-valid: 720 of 720 full-field tensor
comparisons across 36 cases, four resolutions, two precisions, and two
fields are raw-byte identical between the primary-center and fixed-center
paths
([adjudication](../results/hqc_canonical_geometry_validity_36x5_job306114_2026-07-28/artifacts/phase1_hqc_canonical_geometry_validity_adjudication_v1.json)).
On the frozen 36-case epoch-491 benchmark the canonical intervention is
noninferior on all four registered endpoints (cohort-mean ratios
0.99973--1.00132 against a 1.02 ceiling;
[terminal result](../results/phase1_historical_k10000_paired_accuracy_result_v1_job307260_2026-07-28.json)).
The H4 coverage hypothesis failed its common master gate: deterministic
normal-aware coverage improved the pressure substrate floor by a real
12--15% on both frozen cases but missed the pre-registered 20% on both, so
covering-style training was deprioritized as registered
([verdict](../results/phase1_h4_verdict_2026-07-27.json)).

## 2026-07-29 — Controlled reset sharpened what is actually known {#sec-nb-controlled-reset}

The reset produced three agenda-level conclusions:

| Finding | Scientific meaning | Limit |
|---|---|---|
| Licensed singular and limiting structure can reduce error substantially. | Known physics can simplify a controlled family. | Hard fixation was not consistently better, and operator extrapolation remained difficult. |
| Physical-order composition recovered responses constructed to be order-sensitive. | The computation must sometimes respect noncommuting spatial order. | This was shown on controlled layered systems, not broad geometry-bearing PDEs. |
| Several natural compact-state constructions failed to transfer across spectra. | After-the-fact low rank does not imply reusable low-dimensional dynamics. | The failures refute the tested constructions, not all compact representations. |

**EDIT:** the historical low-screening collapse was reproduced with a valid
operator and disappeared. Any conclusion that treated it as a physical
singularity of the learning problem is withdrawn.

Per-experiment verdicts behind the three rows, each linked to its registered
decision (five seeds unless noted):

- *Licensed structure.* The pure exact-propagation readout is sufficient on
  Laplace: the learned output gate and query contraction each earned zero
  qualifying splits and carried large residual penalties
  ([factorial](../results/laplace_readout_factorial_2026-07-29_job5688113/summary.json)).
  The remaining error ceiling is split-dependent: density inference
  dominates geometry stress; the 128-panel boundary representation
  dominates near-boundary and unseen-frequency error
  ([density ceiling](../results/laplace_solved_density_ceiling_2026-07-29_job5689064/summary.json)).
  On the drifted screened family, the learned singular coefficient
  converged to the analytic 1/(2*pi) within 0.12% and hard-fixing it was
  not earned
  ([principal part](../results/drifted_screened_principal_part_2026-07-29_job5689933/summary.json));
  neither supervision mix
  ([supervision](../results/drifted_screened_supervision_2026-07-29_job5690714/summary.json))
  nor exact similarity coordinates
  ([similarity](../results/drifted_screened_similarity_2026-07-29_job5691226/summary.json))
  was the principal factor; the one clear win was the fixed two-limit
  asymptotic carrier *with a learned transition*: every guard and every
  joint transfer criterion passed in all seeds, with field errors improved
  4--30x -- while the fixed carrier alone was 4.2x worse than raw
  ([asymptotic](../results/drifted_screened_asymptotic_2026-07-29_job5692029/summary.json)).
- *Physical-order composition.* Feed-forward coefficient context is not
  sufficient: no arm met the 80% layer-permutation recovery gate
  ([context](../results/layered_screened_context_2026-07-29_job5692619/summary.json)).
  A path-ordered local generator recovered 97.9--99.2% of the true contrast
  with 26x lower paired field error, though its local law did not transfer
  to high coefficients
  ([generator](../results/layered_screened_generator_2026-07-29_job5692915/summary.json));
  with coupled local modes the composition claim closed at full strength --
  98.3--99.5% contrast recovery, 17.7x over pooling, 44x/38x better on
  unseen twist rates and doubled layer counts
  ([coupled](../results/coupled_layered_composition_2026-07-29_job5693733/summary.json)).
- *Compact state.* A rank-4 correction ceiling exists and per-case bases
  beat any fixed subspace 2.6x
  ([census](../results/nonseparable_rank_census_2026-07-29_job5694242/summary.json)),
  and ordered compression was earned in-distribution -- but breadth
  refuted it (0/5 on faster variation,
  [latent composition](../results/nonseparable_latent_composition_2026-07-29_job5694690/summary.json)),
  continuum scaling fixed discretization transfer while frequency transfer
  still failed
  ([continuum flow](../results/nonseparable_continuum_flow_2026-07-29_job5695143/summary.json)),
  broader spectral training did not provide coverage
  ([coverage](../results/nonseparable_frequency_coverage_2026-07-29_job5695543/summary.json)),
  and a connection-aware moving subspace came within 1% of fixed
  truncation
  ([adaptive subspace](../results/nonseparable_adaptive_subspace_2026-07-29_job5695916/summary.json)).
  The registered decisions retire the learned rank-4 local-flow branch with
  fixed reduced propagation as the baseline.

The reset strengthened the case for conditional physical structure while
weakening confidence in a single fixed latent representation. It did not
justify specifying the final architecture.

## 2026-07-29 — Research questions replace component specifications {#sec-nb-agenda-altitude-reset}

The notebook had begun to turn candidate explanations into a detailed design
program before the evidence had established the central transfer effect.
That was the wrong altitude.

**EDIT (2026-07-29):** earlier entries described ports, modular domains,
carriers, latent ranks, and composition laws as though they were prerequisites
for the next result. They are possible explanations and diagnostic tools, not
established architecture requirements. Their detailed derivations have been
moved out of the active notebook and retained in the dated snapshot.

Five conclusions survive:

1. Boundary-aware structure can improve accuracy, fidelity, or efficiency on
   controlled PDE families.
2. More physical structure is not automatically better.
3. Within-family fit and even within-family OOD performance do not establish
   transfer to a new family.
4. The first untouched vehicle-family transfer failed decisively.
5. This program has not yet shown that source experience materially reduces
   the evidence needed on a causal geometry-family shift.

**EDIT (2026-07-29):** the earlier wording said that no experiment had shown
such a saving. That was false as a literature-wide claim. Recent work reports
substantial target-data savings from geometry and difficulty pretraining; the
unresolved issue is causal attribution and architectural increment, not bare
existence.

The program will therefore ask **whether reuse exists before designing how it
must work**. Candidate mechanisms remain dormant until an observed effect
requires explanation.

## 2026-07-29 — Literature favors adaptation over remote zero-shot claims {#sec-nb-literature-generality}

Broad pretrained PDE models make reusable representations plausible, and
several studies report strong gains after task-specific adaptation. The
literature does not establish reliable frozen transfer to remote geometry and
PDE families. This raises the prior for useful adaptation without licensing a
universal frozen model.

The program has strong evidence that representation choices matter inside

negative, but external evidence now makes useful adaptation substantially more
credible.

**EDIT (2026-07-29):** the first probability table assigned only 45% to useful
geometry-family adaptation and 30% to positive net program value. That estimate

Current subjective probabilities are:

|---|---:|---|

## 2026-07-29 — The first question becomes: what made transfer possible? {#sec-nb-geometry-transfer-claim-card}

**EDIT (2026-07-29):** the original claim card asked only whether related
geometry experience reduces target evidence. Existing literature now answers
that question positively in several scoped settings. Repeating bare transfer
existence would not be the highest-value contribution.

**Question.** When pretraining reduces target evidence, is the benefit caused
primarily by geometry similarity, by alignment with the downstream
propagation physics, by sheer source diversity, or by an architectural
inductive bias?

The discriminating patterns are conceptual:

| Pattern across prior work and future evidence | Belief update |
|---|---|
| Physics-aligned source tasks outperform equally informative static geometry. | Propagation alignment is essential. |
| Geometrically closer sources outperform broader alternatives. | Geometry relation is essential. |
| Broad diversity matches or beats the closer source. | Generic coverage dominates proximity. |
| Boundary-aware structure adds a reproducible gain after strong pretraining. | The architecture contributes beyond the data curriculum. |
| The ordering changes unpredictably by target. | Transfer remains task-specific; a universal rule is premature. |

**Decision.** Replace the transfer-existence claim with a causal map of source
relation and architectural increment. This is still a research question, not
an experiment specification. No mechanism is selected and no compute is
authorized by this entry.

The work was primarily a scientific audit, not an experiment campaign:

- invalid historical interpretations were separated from measurements that

  while untouched-family transfer remains a decisive failure;
- the first literature review increased confidence in adaptation but missed

No new model result was produced, no remote job was launched, and no compute
