## Forward research agenda {#sec-nb-forward-agenda}

The next block of work is governed by three questions:

1. **Cause:** which source relation—boundary-response compatibility, geometry,
   or diversity—predicts target-data savings?
2. **Architectural increment:** after strong generic pretraining, does
   boundary-aware structure still improve the transfer curve?
3. **Breadth and value:** does the winning rule recur across propagation
   classes, and do repeated savings repay its cost?

The first robust pattern determines the branch:

| Pattern | Program consequence |
|---|---|
| Boundary-response compatibility dominates | Test whether that causal ordering repeats on a second target before proposing a shared architecture. |
| Geometry alignment dominates | Favor geometry representation learning without claiming that PDE relation caused the saving. |
| Broad diversity dominates | Favor foundation pretraining; treat explicit physics as a possible fidelity or efficiency tool. |
| Boundary-aware structure adds an incremental gain | Pursue the minimum structural principle that works on a second propagation class. |
| No stable ordering emerges | Raise the probability of specialist families and stop claiming a universal transfer rule. |

This is the active research agenda. Engineering work begins only when one of
these questions requires a discriminating measurement.

## 2026-07-29 — Literature moves the gap from transfer existence to transfer cause {#sec-nb-literature-transfer-cause}

The corrected literature review finds that credible geometry transfer and
target-data savings already exist. The open problem is no longer whether
pretraining can ever help, but why one source helps one target and whether
physical architecture contributes beyond the source data.

| Primary evidence | What it establishes | What remains unresolved |
|---|---|---|
| [GINO](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.00583) predicts new vehicle geometries and inlet conditions from 500 labeled simulations. | Geometry-conditioned neural operators can generalize within a demanding vehicle family. | It does not separate family shift, pretraining relation, and architecture. |
| [Geo-NeW](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.02788) trains on circles in square domains and extrapolates to polygons, square obstacles, longer domains, and angled steps, outperforming generic baselines. | Structure-preserving learning can improve strong zero-shot geometry extrapolation. | It does not measure target-label savings or compare alternative pretraining sources. |
| [Choudhary et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.00564) mix easier flow data with hard multi-obstacle targets. Roughly 10% target examples recover most hard-only performance, and medium-difficulty data are often more cost-effective than easy data. | Related lower-cost data can materially reduce dependence on hard target simulations; source difficulty matters. | The study does not isolate geometry similarity from difficulty or compare an equally difficult unrelated family. |
| [Zhang et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.25788) pretrain geometry encoders without PDE labels and improve supervised prediction across four datasets and three operator backbones. | Geometry-only representation learning can improve label efficiency when source geometries come from the same or a similar distribution. | It does not test distant source families or distinguish source diversity from source similarity. |
| [GeoPT](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.20399) pretrains a generic simulator on dynamics-lifted ShapeNet geometry and reports 20%--60% fewer labeled examples across car, aircraft, ship, crash, and radiosity tasks. Static geometry pretraining can hurt; mixed geometry usually beats a single category, with one distant-geometry exception. | Useful adaptation across industrial geometry and physics is credible, and both dynamics alignment and diversity matter. | It does not isolate geometry proximity, dynamics alignment, and diversity at equal source cost, nor test whether boundary-aware structure adds an incremental gain. |

**Belief update.** Useful adaptation is now more likely than not. The
architecture-specific claim has become harder, not easier: a new structured
model must improve on strong generic pretraining rather than on training from
scratch.

**Decision.** Do not spend the next research block re-establishing that
geometry pretraining can help. Study the causal ordering of source relations
and the incremental value of boundary-aware structure. This conclusion changes
the agenda but does not select an implementation or launch computation.

## 2026-07-29 — Task relatedness passes the gate only as a causal question {#sec-nb-heilmeier-task-relation}

**EDIT:** “Develop a task-relation rule” could be read as a proposal for a
universal similarity score. That proposal is withdrawn. The useful question is
whether a physically interpretable ordering of source relations persists, and
the absence of such an ordering would itself be an important result.

The broader transfer-learning literature already provides computational task
maps and source-selection scores. [Taskonomy](https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content_cvpr_2018/html/Zamir_Taskonomy_Disentangling_Task_CVPR_2018_paper.html)
measures a graph of transfers among visual tasks;
[Task2Vec](https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content_ICCV_2019/html/Achille_Task2Vec_Task_Embedding_for_Meta-Learning_ICCV_2019_paper.html)
embeds labeled tasks through a probe network; and
[LEEP](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v119/nguyen20b.html) and
[LogME](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v139/you21b.html) rank pretrained
representations using target examples. These methods can predict which source
will work, but their answer depends on the chosen representation and target
data. They do not establish whether geometry relation, propagation physics, or
source diversity caused the transfer.

[Strategies for Pretraining Neural Operators](https://openreview.net/forum?id=9vEVeX9oIv)
likewise finds that PDE pretraining depends strongly on the model and dataset
and benefits especially near the pretraining distribution. That result makes
the causal question sharper; it does not answer it.

| Heilmeier gate | Judgment |
|---|---|
| Important? | Yes. Without causal source selection, expensive simulation data and architectural work are allocated largely by analogy. |
| Already solved? | Transfer ranking is well studied; physical causal attribution across geometry, propagation, and diversity is not established by the audited work. |
| New claim? | A stable *ordering* of physically meaningful source relations, not a universal scalar similarity metric. |
| Attackable? | Moderately. The rival hypotheses predict different orderings, and prior work shows that each candidate factor can matter. |
| Decisive failure? | If the ordering reverses across targets, target-data budgets, or reasonable model classes, relatedness is task- and representation-specific. |
| Scope control? | Source relation is the first question. Architectural increment is a separate second claim; breadth and economic value come later. |

**GO, but narrow.** The next research block should ask whether aligned physics,
nearby geometry, or broad diversity has a stable directional advantage. Do not
build a transferability metric, bundle an architecture claim into the same
conclusion, or pursue internal mechanisms first.

This question now ranks above architecture invention, cross-physics breadth,
and further component ablations because it decides whether a shared surrogate
program has a coherent source of reusable knowledge. No computation is
authorized until a measurement can distinguish the rival causal accounts.

## 2026-07-29 — The candidate transferable object is the boundary-response law {#sec-nb-boundary-response-hypothesis}

A boundary-driven task is not adequately described by a geometry label or a
PDE name. It is a physical map from boundary data to the requested field. For
a domain $\Omega$, differential operator $\mathcal L$, boundary operator
$\mathcal B$, and observable $\mathcal O$, call that map
$S_\tau:g\mapsto\mathcal O u$.

For a well-posed linear problem, this map can often be written

$$
S_\tau g(x)=\int_{\partial\Omega}P_\tau(x,s)g(s)\,\mathrm dS_s .
$$

The boundary influence kernel $P_\tau$ depends jointly on the geometry,
differential operator, boundary operator, and observable. For a nonlinear
problem, the local response also changes with the boundary drive. Thus the
distribution of drives determines which part of the response law is actually
identified.

This view is consistent with two recent results. Han et al. recast
[variable-geometry operator learning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.01498) as
learning geometry-dependent, potentially singular kernel operators. Shikhman
shows that a learned PDE surrogate is
[not identifiable outside its observed boundary-condition distribution](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.01406),
even when the differential operator is unchanged. Conversely,
[Poseidon](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2024/hash/84e1b1ec17bb11c57234e96433022a9a-Abstract-Conference.html)
shows that broad pretraining can help on unseen and apparently unrelated PDEs.
The literature therefore motivates the question but does not select its
answer.

The leading hypothesis is:

> **Boundary-response compatibility.** Target-data savings follow shared
> physical structure in the boundary-response law—its influence
> singularity and decay, boundary type, symmetry of the observable, and
> dependence on the drive—more strongly than they follow morphology alone.

The rival predictions are ordinal by design:

| Rival account | Deciding pattern |
|---|---|
| Boundary-response reuse | A physically aligned but geometrically dissimilar source is more valuable than a geometrically aligned source with a different response law. |
| Geometry-scaffold reuse | The reverse ordering holds. |
| Diversity-driven reuse | A broad source mixture beats both aligned sources without a stable pairwise relation. |
| Specialist families | Source rankings reverse across targets or no source dependably improves on target-only learning. |

The decisive evidence is a crossed comparison of geometry relation and
response-law relation, with source information and boundary-drive coverage
held comparable. The outcome is target-data saving, not zero-shot accuracy.
One target would be exploratory; the same ordering on a second different target is the minimum support for a reusable relation.

**Falsifier.** If the ordering reverses with target, target-data budget, or
reasonable model class, boundary-response compatibility is not an
architecture-independent transfer principle. The scientifically useful result
would then be that source selection is conditional, not a failed search for a
universal score.

**Decision.** Promote boundary-response compatibility to the first causal
hypothesis, while keeping geometry, diversity, and specialization fully live.
This is a claim card, not an architecture proposal. No computation is yet
justified.

## 2026-07-29 — Compatibility must be a relation vector, not a score {#sec-nb-prospective-relation-vector}

**EDIT to @sec-nb-boundary-response-hypothesis:** two statements were too
strong. First, “Shikhman shows” overstated the cited evidence. The paper argues
that empirical risk minimization does not identify behavior outside the
observed boundary-condition distribution and demonstrates the effect in one
steady Poisson/FNO study; it explicitly provides no formal guarantee. Second,
the four listed response features were not a sufficient prospective
definition. They omitted operating regime, topology, and the support of the
drives and observations. Boundary-response compatibility therefore remains a
candidate causal relation, not an established or scalar ordering principle.

Three analytic counterexamples make the omission decisive:

| Tasks that look compatible under the old description | What changes | Lesson |
|---|---|---|
| $u''+k^2u=0$ on $(0,1)$ with Dirichlet data | $u(x)=[g_0\sin k(1-x)+g_1\sin kx]/\sin k$ becomes arbitrarily sensitive near $k=n\pi$, and uniqueness fails at resonance. | The dimensionless operating regime and distance to loss of well-posedness matter even when PDE order, boundary type, symmetry, and drive linearity match. |
| Dirichlet Laplace problems on the unit disk | $g(\theta)=\sum_m g_m e^{im\theta}$ produces $u(r,\theta)=\sum_m r^{|m|}g_m e^{im\theta}$. Training drives confined to low $m$ do not identify response to high $m$. | The support and regularity of the excitation distribution are part of the learning task, not incidental dataset details. |
| Laplace problems on a disk and an annulus | The annulus admits a logarithmic harmonic mode excluded by regularity at the center of a disk. | Local propagation class does not determine global response; topology matters. |

The same issue appears in nonlinear problems near bifurcation: the label
“nonlinear” says little without the operating state. Equation-aware models
show that prospective description is feasible but not that it is sufficient.
[PDEformer](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.12652) encodes symbolic and numerical
PDE information as a computational graph, but its reported study is confined
to one-dimensional periodic problems.
[PROSE-PDE](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.12355) likewise benefits from symbolic
operator input across a scoped family of one-dimensional time-dependent PDEs.
Neither work defines or validates a source--target transfer ordering.

A task relation can nevertheless be specified before seeing transfer results,
provided it remains blockwise:

| Relation block | Prospective physical description |
|---|---|
| Task contract | Boundary and observable operators; field type; exact symmetries, invariances, and drive algebra. |
| Local propagation | PDE order and principal type; characteristic or influence structure; singularity, decay, dissipation, and dispersion. |
| Global regime | Dimensionless parameters, topology, and distance to resonance, bifurcation, or loss of well-posedness. |
| Excitation and observation support | Amplitude, spectral, and regularity range of boundary drives; parameter support; observed region and resolution. |
| Morphology distribution | Dimensionless shape family, feature scales, and geometric variability. |

This vector is non-circular only if it is frozen from the equations and task
distribution before training, reported without learned weights, and used to
name which block changes while the others are matched. A scalar “compatibility
score” would conceal value judgments and invite post-hoc relabeling.

The sharpened causal prediction is now conditional: **among sources matched
in task contract and excitation/observation support, matching local
propagation and global regime should yield more target-data saving than
matching morphology alone.** The geometry, diversity, and specialist
hypotheses predict the reverse, a mixture advantage, and unstable rankings,
respectively.

**Falsifier.** A stable physical ordering is refuted if source rankings reverse
across targets, target-data budgets, or reasonable model classes after the
relation blocks are fixed prospectively. The vector would then remain useful
for describing the failed contrasts, but it would not predict transfer.

**Decision.** Keep boundary-response compatibility as the leading hypothesis,
but demote any universal reading of it. The next scientific task is to find
the smallest problem family that crosses physical-response relation and
morphology relation without confounding excitation support. No computation is
justified until that contrast exists.

## 2026-07-29 — Two boundary modes are the minimum clean transfer test {#sec-nb-two-mode-transfer-test}

The smallest credible comparison is an exact two-mode screened problem on
rectangles. It is the first simple family in which geometry and physical
response can be varied separately without changing topology, boundary type,
drive support, or label fidelity.

**EDIT to @sec-nb-prospective-relation-vector:** its blocks are descriptive,
not generally independent. Geometry and PDE coefficients can enter a response
law only through coupled dimensionless groups. A factorial that labels one arm
“geometry” and another “physics” is circular unless the chosen observations
can identify both factors separately.

Consider the rectangle $\Omega_a=(0,a)\times(0,1)$ and

$$
(\Delta-\lambda^2)u=0,\qquad
u(0,y)=\sum_{m\in M}c_m\sin(m\pi y),
$$

with zero Dirichlet data on the other three sides. Here $a$ is aspect ratio,
$\lambda$ is dimensionless screening, and the coefficients $c_m$ are the
boundary drive. At normalized streamwise coordinate $\xi=x/a$, the exact
solution is

$$
u(\xi,y)=\sum_{m\in M}c_m
\frac{\sinh[d_m(1-\xi)]}{\sinh d_m}\sin(m\pi y),
\qquad
d_m=a\sqrt{(m\pi)^2+\lambda^2}.
$$

For a single mode, the entire response depends only on the optical depth
$d_m$. A change in aspect ratio can exactly imitate a change in screening, so
no one-mode experiment can say whether transfer followed morphology or
physics. Two modes are the minimum that removes this degeneracy. For
$M=\{1,2\}$,

$$
a^2=\frac{d_2^2-d_1^2}{3\pi^2},
\qquad
\lambda^2=\frac{d_1^2}{a^2}-\pi^2.
$$

Thus the response determines $a$ and $\lambda$ separately before any learned
representation is introduced.

| Candidate family | Verdict for this causal question |
|---|---|
| One-dimensional interval or one rectangle mode | Reject: geometry scale and screening collapse into one nondimensional response coordinate. |
| Disk versus annulus | Reject: morphology and topology change together. |
| Laplace versus Helmholtz | Reject initially: resonance and well-posedness introduce a second physical change. |
| Existing deformed screened-Laplace suite | Retain as solver evidence, but reject as this factorial: its boundary traces are restrictions of globally regular manufactured fields, so excitation support moves with geometry. |
| Two or more independent modes on rectangles | Accept: exact labels, fixed topology and contracts, independently sampled drives, and identifiable geometry and screening. |

The decisive comparison uses one target $T=(a_T,\lambda_T)$ and three
equal-information sources:

| Source | Relation to target | Interpretation |
|---|---|---|
| $P=(a_P,\lambda_T)$ | same screening, different aspect ratio | physical-regime aligned |
| $G=(a_T,\lambda_G)$ | same aspect ratio, different screening | morphology aligned |
| $N=(a_P,\lambda_G)$ | neither relation | interaction control |

All tasks use the same independently sampled coefficients $c_m$ and the same
normalized observation distribution. The non-target parameters $a_P$ and
$\lambda_G$ must be selected *before learning* so that $P$ and $G$ are equally
distant from $T$ under the exact response-operator norm induced by that common
drive distribution. This prevents a trivial “nearest operator wins”
explanation while leaving the direction of mismatch different.

The rival predictions are now sharper:

| Rival | Deciding source ordering |
|---|---|
| Physical-response reuse | $P$ requires fewer target examples than $G$ at matched operator distance. |
| Geometry-scaffold reuse | $G$ requires fewer than $P$. |
| Continuous response-spectrum proximity | $P$ and $G$ tie once their exact operator distances are matched. |
| Specialist or representation-dependent transfer | The ordering changes with target or reasonable model class. |
| Diversity-driven reuse | An equal-budget mixture of $P$ and $G$ beats both single sources; this is a secondary contrast, not part of the minimum factorial. |

The outcome is target examples required to reach a fixed held-out error, not
zero-shot accuracy. One target and one model class can only be exploratory.
An architecture-independent claim requires the same ordering on a second
target and on both a strong generic operator learner and a boundary-aware
learner. If the two-mode task is so easy that target-only learning saturates
immediately, the number of independently excited modes must increase without
changing the causal axes.

**Falsifier.** A stable source-relation principle is refuted by a rank reversal
across targets or model classes. A tie after exact-distance matching would
refute both categorical accounts and favor continuous response-spectrum
distance.

**Decision.** This family passes the conceptual gate, but not yet the launch
gate. The remaining pre-registration is to choose distance-matched source
parameters and an attainable target-error threshold without observing any
transfer result.

## 2026-07-29 — Equal total distance leaves a spectral crossover, not a tie {#sec-nb-spectral-crossover}

The scalar distance proposed in @sec-nb-two-mode-transfer-test is legitimate
only as a balancing control. It cannot stand in for task compatibility, and it
does not make the physics- and morphology-aligned sources equivalent.

For target $T=(a_T,\lambda_T)$, the modal optical depths of the two sources
obey

$$
\frac{d_m^P}{d_m^T}=\frac{a_P}{a_T},
\qquad
\frac{d_m^G}{d_m^T}
=
\sqrt{\frac{(m\pi)^2+\lambda_G^2}
{(m\pi)^2+\lambda_T^2}}.
$$

Changing aspect ratio therefore moves every mode by the same *fraction*.
Changing screening moves low modes most and becomes negligible relative to
$m\pi$ at high modes. The two mismatch vectors cannot agree on two distinct
modes unless $\lambda_G=\lambda_T$ and $a_P=a_T$—the trivial case in which
both sources are the target.

Let $f_d(\xi)=\sinh[d(1-\xi)]/\sinh d$ be a mode's normalized penetration
profile. The declared drive and observation distributions induce transparent
modewise distances

$$
D_m^2(S,T)
=
\int_0^1\!\left[f_{d_m^S}(\xi)-f_{d_m^T}(\xi)\right]^2\,\mathrm d\xi,
\qquad
D^2(S,T)=\sum_m w_mD_m^2(S,T),
$$

where the positive weights $w_m$ are fixed by the boundary-drive
distribution. Both source shifts must lie on the same side of the target—for
example, $a_P>a_T$ and $\lambda_G>\lambda_T$—so both increase attenuation.
On that one-sided comparison, $f_d$ decreases strictly with $d$, and identical
modewise distances would require identical optical depths, already ruled out
above. Matching $D(P,T)=D(G,T)$ therefore balances total displacement under
one declared task measure while necessarily leaving a crossover: at least one
mode is closer to $P$ and at least one is closer to $G$.

**EDIT to @sec-nb-two-mode-transfer-test:** the row predicting that
“continuous response-spectrum proximity” implies an overall tie was too
broad. Only an *isotropic scalar-distance* account predicts such a tie.
A modewise response account instead predicts that transfer benefit changes
sign with the mode whose response is closer.

The registered rivals should therefore be read mode by mode:

| Rival | Deciding pattern after total-distance matching |
|---|---|
| Categorical physical-regime reuse | $P$ transfers better than $G$ on both modes. |
| Categorical geometry-scaffold reuse | $G$ transfers better than $P$ on both modes. |
| Modewise response reuse | $P$ wins on the mode for which $D_m(P,T)<D_m(G,T)$, while $G$ wins on the other. |
| Isotropic scalar proximity | Aggregate transfer ties despite the modewise distance crossover. |
| Representation-dependent transfer | The modewise sign pattern changes across reasonable model classes. |
| No reusable knowledge | Neither source improves materially on target-only learning. |

The control is non-circular only under four restrictions: freeze $w_m$ and
the observation measure from the target task; use $D$ solely to balance total
displacement; publish the complete vector $(D_m)$ before learning; and make
mode-resolved target-data saving the primary outcome. Aggregate error is
secondary because it can cancel the very sign change that distinguishes the
rivals.

**Falsifier.** Modewise response reuse is refuted if the closer source does
not confer the larger data saving on either mode, or if the sign pattern
reverses across model classes. The categorical accounts are refuted by the
predicted crossover.

**Decision.** Retain the rectangle family, but withdraw the proposed overall
source ranking as the decisive result. The stronger experiment asks whether
transfer follows the *direction* of response mismatch mode by mode. The launch
gate still requires prospectively chosen source parameters with a clear
distance crossover and non-saturated modewise learning thresholds.

## 2026-07-29 — Two modes identify the cause but cannot measure useful transfer {#sec-nb-rich-transfer-task}

The two-mode rectangle is an identifiability proof, not yet a credible
transfer benchmark. Its exactness exposed a second confound before any
training was attempted.

**EDIT to @sec-nb-two-mode-transfer-test:** “minimum clean transfer test” was
too strong. With $M$ excited boundary modes, the target operator restricted to
that subspace is an $M$-dimensional linear map. At shared observation points,
$M$ linearly independent noiseless target excitations determine all $M$
response fields exactly. For $M=2$, any model that needs many target examples
is failing to exploit a known linear contract; a large apparent pretraining
gain would not by itself demonstrate reusable PDE knowledge.

**EDIT (2026-07-29):** the preceding argument supplied a sufficient
reconstruction count for an unrestricted linear map, then incorrectly treated
it as a necessary count for this separable PDE. Here one full target field
contains all modes at once. Sine projection in $y$ separates them, so the
number of energetic modes is not the number of target simulations. The
broadband launch criterion derived below is therefore withdrawn; see
@sec-nb-one-field-demixing.

The same exact solution provides a model-independent richness test. If
$w_m=\operatorname{Var}(c_m)$ and $\phi_m$ is the target field produced by a
unit boundary coefficient in mode $m$, its expected output energy is

$$
e_m
=
w_m\lVert\phi_m\rVert_{L^2([0,1]^2)}^2
=
\frac{w_m}{4}
\left[
\frac{\coth d_m^T}{d_m^T}
-\frac{1}{\sinh^2 d_m^T}
\right].
$$

The norm uses the normalized observation measure shared by all tasks. For a
declared relative root-mean-square error $\epsilon$, define the effective
response dimension $r_\epsilon$ as the smallest number of largest-energy modes
whose retention leaves at most $\epsilon^2$ of the total energy in the tail.
This quantity is fixed by the PDE, target geometry, and boundary-drive
distribution before a model exists.

The smallest statistically useful version is therefore not two individual
modes but two separated **mode bands**, each containing multiple independent
coefficients:

| Requirement | Scientific purpose |
|---|---|
| One low-frequency and one high-frequency band | Preserve the response-distance crossover derived in @sec-nb-spectral-crossover. |
| The same coefficient distribution in every source and target | Hold excitation support fixed. |
| Prospectively balanced target output energy across the two bands | Prevent aggregate error from hiding one side of the crossover. |
| $r_\epsilon$ larger than every target-data budget used for the low-data claim | Keep the target-only problem information-limited at the declared accuracy. |
| A linear reconstruction oracle that closes once enough independent target excitations span the effective subspace | Separate information reuse from optimization or representation failure. |

Within each band, a smooth spectral law can remain physically plausible; only
the total mass of the two bands is balanced. The source parameters are
admissible only if their total response distances match and their *bandwise*
distances have opposite orderings before training. The primary measurement is
then target-data saving within each band. Overall error remains secondary.

This creates three distinct outcomes. A physical or geometric category that
wins in both bands supports a categorical reuse mechanism. Opposite winners
across the two bands support modewise response reuse. An advantage that
appears only while the target-only learner remains far behind the linear
oracle is confounded with learner inefficiency and cannot by itself establish
source relatedness.

**Falsifier.** The proposed transfer instrument is invalid if its effective
dimension falls inside the target-data budget, either band contributes
negligible target variance, or the analytic distance crossover is absent.
Modewise response reuse is refuted if the closer source does not save more
target data in either band.

**Decision.** Do not launch the two-mode study. Retain it as the derivation
that proves causal identifiability, and promote a broadband two-band rectangle
family as the first admissible transfer instrument. The next gate is entirely
prospective: freeze the target spectrum, accuracy level, effective dimension,
and distance-matched source pair.

## 2026-07-29 — The broadband rectangle passes the analytic launch gates {#sec-nb-broadband-prereg}

The physical task, information regime, and source contrast are now frozen
without observing a learning result. This closes the prospective gate left by
@sec-nb-rich-transfer-task while keeping architecture and training choices
outside the claim.

The target is a square with dimensionless screening $\lambda_T=\pi$. The
physics-aligned source lengthens the rectangle by 25% at fixed screening; the
morphology-aligned source keeps the square and increases screening until its
total response distance matches:

| Task | Aspect ratio $a$ | Screening $\lambda$ | Relation to target |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Target $T$ | 1 | $\pi$ | — |
| Source $P$ | 1.25 | $\pi$ | same physical regime |
| Source $G$ | 1 | $2.24836\pi$ | same morphology |
| Source $N$ | 1.25 | $2.24836\pi$ | neither; interaction control |

The boundary drive contains two eight-mode bands: modes 1--8 and 17--24.
Coefficients are independent in every task. High-band coefficient variance is
$5.922$ times the low-band variance, the unique rescaling that makes the two
bands contribute 50% each of the target's output energy under the normalized
observation measure. This is a designed stress distribution, not a claim
about natural boundary spectra.

The closed-form response passes all four analytic gates:

| Gate fixed before learning | Value |
|---|---:|
| Target relative root-mean-square accuracy | 1% |
| Effective response dimension at that accuracy | 16 |
| Target-example budgets | 1, 2, 4, 8 |
| Total squared distance, $P$ and $G$ | equal by construction |
| Share of $P$ distance in low / high band | 49.77% / 50.23% |
| Share of $G$ distance in low / high band | 99.97% / 0.03% |

Thus every claimed low-data budget is below the target's effective dimension,
both bands are visible, and the distance crossover is large: $P$ is closer in
the low band, whereas $G$ is about fortyfold closer in distance in the high
band. The registered modewise-response hypothesis predicts that $P$ saves more
low-band target data and $G$ saves more high-band target data. A physical or
geometric category predicts the same winner in both bands.

The complete numerical preregistration, including the exact distance
definition and interpretation limits, is
[archived here](../results/rectangle_broadband_transfer_preregistration_2026-07-29.json).
The linear reconstruction oracle closes after 16 independent target
excitations; it remains the reference separating low-data reuse from
learner inefficiency.

**EDIT (2026-07-29):** that “oracle” was not the problem-specific oracle. It
was an unrestricted linear-operator reference that ignored the known
transverse eigenfunctions. A problem-specific oracle recovers all sixteen
modal profiles from one full field. Consequently, the claimed
information-content gate did not pass.

**Scope limit.** The spectrum emphasizes high-frequency boundary
content so that screening and morphology make opposing, observable
predictions. A positive result would establish a mechanism on a causal
instrument, not generality. It must later survive a naturally smooth spectrum
and a non-rectangular geometry.

**Decision.** The PDE family now passes its physical, identifiability, and
information-content gates. The remaining scientific gate is empirical:
determine whether the predicted bandwise crossover remains under substantially
different learning instruments.

**EDIT (2026-07-29):** that decision skipped a necessary scientific control.
The registered budgets of 1, 2, 4, and 8 target examples do not span the
registered 1% aggregate-error threshold under the exact neutral-adaptation
benchmark derived below. “Band-resolved 1% relative error” also failed to
specify whether each band or the full response supplied the denominator.
Because no learning result has been inspected, the physical contrast remains
frozen while the outcomes and budgets are amended prospectively.

**EDIT (2026-07-29):** the amendment above is itself superseded by
@sec-nb-one-field-demixing. Changing the budgets cannot repair an invalid
information unit.

## 2026-07-29 — An exact adaptation null precedes any architecture comparison {#sec-nb-adaptation-null}

The next question is not which model to build. It is what transfer should look
like if target learning merely preserves the source response wherever target
data provide no contrary information.

Write the whitened 16-mode source and target response operators as $B_S$ and
$B_T$. Among operators that fit $n$ noiseless target excitations, the smallest
change from the source is

$$
\widehat B
=
B_S+(B_T-B_S)P_n,
\qquad
\mathbb E\lVert\widehat B-B_T\rVert^2
=
\left(1-\frac{n}{16}\right)\lVert B_S-B_T\rVert^2,
$$

where $P_n$ projects onto the span of the observed target drives. The same
retention factor holds separately for each orthogonal mode band. This gives an
exact scientific null with no learned architecture.

**EDIT (2026-07-29):** “exact scientific null” means exact only for this
declared minimum-change update over an otherwise unrestricted linear operator.
It is neither an information-theoretic lower bound nor an
architecture-independent target-simulation curve. A learner that exploits the
known sine decomposition can use one full field to constrain all sixteen
directions simultaneously.

Three consequences follow:

1. The distance-matched sources $P$ and $G$ must tie in aggregate at every
   budget under this null.
2. $P$ must be better on the low band and $G$ on the high band, exactly as
   predicted by their response-distance crossover.
3. The original budgets do not span the 1% aggregate threshold. With consistent
   normalization, both sources remain above 3.7% at 15 target excitations and
   reach 1% only when all 16 directions are observed. Under per-band
   normalization, the high $G$ band is the lone exception: it is already below
   1% before target adaptation.

**EDIT (normalization correction):** the first calculation of this null mixed
response distances using drive weights normalized to sum one with target
energy using unnormalized relative variances. It therefore understated the
zero-target source error as 2.83% and placed threshold crossings at 14--15
examples. The consistently normalized error is 14.87%; the corrected values
above and in the amendment were checked before any learning result.

**EDIT:** “architecture-independent” was too strong. Transfer is necessarily
conditional on the adaptation rule. The defensible claim is
**architecture-robust**: a prospectively defined set of substantially
different learners either follows or departs from the same null pattern.

The rival hypotheses are now cleaner. A categorical physical effect requires
$P$ to beat $G$ in both bands, overturning the null's high-band winner; a
categorical geometry effect requires $G$ to beat $P$ in both, overturning its
low-band winner. Pure response reuse follows the aggregate tie and opposite
band winners; representation dependence appears as inconsistent departures
across learners.

The original preregistration remains unchanged as the historical record. Its
[pre-results analytic amendment](../results/rectangle_broadband_adaptation_null_2026-07-29.json)
adds the budgets 0, 12, 14, 15, and 16 and makes bandwise error relative to
this null the primary outcome.

**Decision.** Do not select or optimize architectures yet. First treat
learning systems as measurement instruments for deviations from this analytic
null. Their internal details matter only if such a deviation is reproducible
and scientifically diagnostic.

## 2026-07-29 — Smooth spectra collapse the rectangle's causal contrast {#sec-nb-response-tangent-metric}

The amplified high-frequency band is not merely a convenient stress test. It
is what makes aspect ratio and screening distinguishable in the observed
response.

**EDIT:** “morphology-aligned” and “physical-regime-aligned” were too broad
for this rectangle. The exact contrast is **aspect-ratio alignment versus
screening alignment**. General morphology and propagation-class reuse remain
untested.

To measure whether these two task directions are distinguishable before
learning, consider the local response metric at the target. Let $B$ be the
boundary-to-field operator and use coordinates
$\theta=(\log a,\log\lambda)$. The correlation

$$
\rho=
\frac{\langle\partial_{\log a}B,\partial_{\log\lambda}B\rangle}
{\lVert\partial_{\log a}B\rVert
 \lVert\partial_{\log\lambda}B\rVert}
$$

is one when the two changes are locally indistinguishable and zero when they
are orthogonal. Under the same mode support, the declared drive spectrum
changes this correlation dramatically:

| Boundary-coefficient variance | Direction correlation $\rho$ | Standardized metric condition number |
|---|---:|---:|
| Registered two-band stress spectrum | 0.524 | 3.20 |
| Flat across the selected modes | 0.681 | 5.27 |
| Smooth, proportional to $m^{-2}$ | 0.946 | 35.9 |
| Smoother, proportional to $m^{-4}$ | 0.990 | 202 |

The exact finite source displacements corroborate the local result: their
angle falls from $54.4^\circ$ under the stress spectrum to $9.1^\circ$ under
$m^{-4}$ weighting. The calculation is stable to twelve decimal places across
five quadrature orders;
the [calculation and scope](../results/rectangle_response_tangent_metric_2026-07-29.json)
are archived separately.

**EDIT to @sec-nb-broadband-prereg:** requiring the same result under a
“naturally smooth spectrum” would be an unfair falsifier. Such spectra nearly
collapse the two causal directions before a learner sees any data. A valid
follow-up must instead predict the loss of discriminating power from this
metric, or choose a different problem whose response tangents remain
separated.

This suggests a broader hypothesis: **source usefulness follows alignment in
the target's response-tangent space more reliably than it follows symbolic
labels such as “same geometry” or “same PDE coefficient.”** The rectangle is
now a clean first test of that hypothesis, not evidence for a universal
geometry-versus-physics taxonomy.

**Falsifier.** The response-tangent hypothesis fails if source ordering is
stable and categorical even as the tangent angle and exact modewise distances
are varied prospectively, or if closer response directions repeatedly transfer
worse across distinct learners.

**Decision.** The next scientific comparison should vary response-tangent
angle while keeping source cost and target support fixed. The scientific
object is the source-relatedness law; the learner is only its measuring
instrument.

## 2026-07-29 — Equal-information targets isolate response direction {#sec-nb-response-direction-sweep}

A three-target rectangle family can rotate the source-response directions
without changing their symbolic relations, total distance from target, or
target information content.

For each target, the same 16 boundary modes are retained and their coefficient
variances are chosen so that every mode contributes exactly the same target
output energy. The target therefore has effective dimension 16 in every
regime. The screening-aligned source and aspect-aligned source are each placed
at exactly 15% relative response error, so their neutral aggregate adaptation
curve is also identical.

Only the angle between their exact response displacements changes materially:

| Target screening | Response angle | Source--source chord / target radius | Low-band distance: screening-aligned / aspect-aligned |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| $\pi$ | $56.0^\circ$ | 0.938 | 49.9% / 99.9% |
| $8\pi$ | $32.2^\circ$ | 0.555 | 50.0% / 94.1% |
| $16\pi$ | $18.6^\circ$ | 0.323 | 50.0% / 79.3% |

Under the exact minimum-change null, the two sources tie in aggregate at every
target-data budget. The screening-aligned source wins the low band and the
aspect-aligned source wins the high band, but that contrast weakens as the
response directions converge. A categorical account instead predicts the same
source wins both bands despite the exact crossover.

The full [pre-results construction and rival predictions](../results/rectangle_response_direction_sweep_preregistration_2026-07-29.json)
were frozen before any learning result. Parameters and angles agree to twelve
decimal places across five quadrature orders.

**Main risk.** Increasing screening also thins the physical boundary layer.
Any later learner comparison must show equal observation fidelity before a
trend is attributed to response direction. A second, independent way of
rotating the response directions would be required before making a broad
causal claim.

**Decision.** This family passes the analytic gate for a prospective
response-direction test. The contribution would be a source-relatedness law,
not a new model component.

**EDIT (2026-07-29):** the analytic response-direction construction remains valid,
but its full-field target-example budgets do not. Any empirical reuse claim
must be moved to a task where one solution cannot be spectrally demixed into
all operator directions.

## 2026-07-29 — Two routes separate response direction from screening {#sec-nb-two-route-response-test}

The screening sweep in @sec-nb-response-direction-sweep had one unavoidable
ambiguity: increasing screening rotates the response directions but also thins
the physical boundary layer. A second route can now test the same angle trend
without changing the target PDE coefficient.

Changing the interior observation distribution was considered first and
rejected. It produced little clean rotation; a material change required drive
variances spanning roughly four orders of magnitude. That would replace the
screening confound with a worse excitation confound.

The cleaner route shifts the target's 16 boundary frequencies upward while
holding screening at $\lambda=\pi$. Every target mode is again weighted to
carry equal output energy, and both sources remain exactly 15% from target.
This spectral route nearly matches the three response angles from the
screening route:

| Response separation | Screening route | Spectral-support route |
|---|---:|---:|
| Separated | $56.0^\circ$ | $53.4^\circ$ |
| Intermediate | $32.2^\circ$ | $34.1^\circ$ |
| Nearly collinear | $18.6^\circ$ | $18.2^\circ$ |

The physical causes now differ while the proposed explanatory coordinate is
nearly matched. If band-resolved source contrast agrees across each pair and
weakens with angle, response direction is retained through the triangulation. A
systematic route-specific residual instead supports screening regime or
excitation support as an omitted causal variable. A categorical account still
predicts one source wins both mode halves.

The complete [paired preregistration](../results/rectangle_response_direction_two_route_preregistration_2026-07-29.json)
keeps the exact angles rather than treating the pairs as identical. Its
measurement is invalid if target-only or exact-linear-reference fidelity
differs enough across routes to explain the source contrast.

**Decision.** The response-direction hypothesis now has two independent
prospective manipulations and a direct falsifier. That is enough scientific
justification for an empirical test; it is not evidence for a new
architecture.

**EDIT (2026-07-29):** the two routes remain valid analytic manipulations of
response direction, but the proposed low-data learning test is withdrawn for
the same one-field demixing reason.

## 2026-07-29 — One target field defeats the rectangle's sample-complexity premise {#sec-nb-one-field-demixing}

The rectangle remains a clean way to separate aspect-ratio and screening
effects, but it cannot measure savings in the number of target simulations.
The mistake was equating response-energy dimension with simulation
complexity.

For one target boundary drive with nonzero coefficients in every selected
mode,

$$
u(\xi,y)=\sum_m c_m f_m(\xi)\sin(m\pi y).
$$

Orthogonality exposes every response profile from that same field:

$$
2\int_0^1 u(\xi,y)\sin(k\pi y)\,\mathrm dy
=c_k f_k(\xi).
$$

Thus one full-field solution recovers all $f_k$ by division by $c_k$. This is
not merely a continuous argument. On 64 equally spaced interior $y$ samples,
the discrete sine basis recovered all sixteen profiles on 65 streamwise
locations with relative error $2.06\times10^{-15}$. The largest absolute
profile error was $7.11\times10^{-15}$.

The [correction artifact](../results/rectangle_one_field_demixing_correction_2026-07-29.json)
records the derivation and numerical witness. No learning result was inspected
before this correction.

Three conclusions follow:

1. Sixteen equal-energy modes still describe the target's response-energy
   distribution, but they do not imply sixteen target simulations.
2. The minimum-change curve remains a legitimate conditional null for an
   unstructured operator update, not a lower bound on what a structured
   learner can infer.
3. The exact distances, spectral crossover, tangent angles, and two-route
   triangulation remain useful descriptions of task relation. Their proposed
   target-field-budget experiment does not.

**Decision.** Do not launch the rectangle learning study. Preserve it as an
analytic causal probe, and move the empirical source-relatedness question to
the smallest nonseparable boundary-driven family for which a single target
solution cannot expose all response directions by a known projection.

## 2026-07-29 — Nonseparable coupling preserves a measurable response-direction contrast {#sec-nb-nonseparable-response-gate}

The replacement keeps the useful causal axes while removing the rectangle's
exact modal diagonalization. It is a coercive elliptic strip with a positive
coefficient field that varies in both propagation and transverse directions.
Eight independent boundary modes are coupled in the interior. One source
changes propagation length; the other adds uniform screening. Both are placed
exactly 15% from the target response.

The frozen analytic gates all passed:

| Deciding quantity | Reference value |
|---|---:|
| Error of the old same-mode demixing strategy | 5.62% |
| Angle between the two source-response displacements | $35.73^\circ$ |
| Source closer on input modes | length: 0--2; screening: 3--7 |
| Drive-variance dynamic range | 3.10 |
| Maximum boundary-condition error | $9.81\times10^{-14}$ |

The result is stable under refinement. From the coarse to reference
calculation, the response angle changed by only $0.025^\circ$ and the
same-mode error by 0.036 percentage points; the source crossover never
changed. The [preregistration](../results/nonseparable_response_relation_preregistration_2026-07-29.json)
and [formal result](../results/nonseparable_response_relation_formal_2026-07-29.json)
contain the full gates and provenance.

This repairs only the known defect. A 5.62% mode-conversion penalty means the
rectangle's one-field sine projection is no longer an accurate oracle, but it
does not prove that several target simulations are necessary for every
learner.

**Decision.** The next experiment is a target-only saturation test. The
nonseparable family becomes a transfer instrument only if held-out error
continues to improve materially from one to several independently driven
target fields. If one field already saturates, reject it before measuring
source transfer.

## 2026-07-29 — The first learner fails the target-saturation gate {#sec-nb-target-saturation}

The nonseparable task passed its analytic gates, but its first learner is not a
valid transfer instrument. The learner represented the response as a smooth
coordinate-dependent kernel while enforcing exact linearity in the boundary
drive. Before asking whether either source helps, it had to show stable
capacity and a meaningful target-only learning curve.

**EDIT:** the first protocol used independent Gaussian target drives.
Inspection before the formal comparison found eight-field condition numbers
of 15.6, 30.7, and 2647. Field count therefore did not control directional
coverage. Those pilot results are excluded. The corrected comparison used
nested orthogonal drives, so each additional field added one equally
conditioned response direction.

The corrected three-seed result was:

| Target fields | Held-out relative error |
|---:|---:|
| 1 | 118.2% |
| 2 | 110.5% |
| 4 | 110.7% |
| 8 | 0.602% |

Full directional coverage solved the task, but partial coverage did not yield
a material or monotone improvement. The independent capacity control also
missed its 0.5% gate at 1.06%; a local signal check had reached 0.424%, so
final accuracy was not robust to the execution setting. The
[formal summary](../results/nonseparable_target_saturation_orthogonal_2026-07-29_job5700316/artifacts/summary.json)
was reproduced byte for byte by an independent reduction.

This is an instrument failure, not a transfer result. The model fits the
observed drive subspace while leaving unseen directions effectively arbitrary;
any source-trained advantage would therefore mostly measure the existence of a
prior, not which source relation is better.

**Decision.** Do not run source transfer with this learner. The next
measurement must test an explicit scientific prior that couples nearby
boundary-response directions and must pass the same capacity and saturation
gates before either source is revealed.

## 2026-07-29 — Spectral priors fail; the next exam moves to geometry {#sec-nb-spectral-priors-close}

Two explicit priors were tested to determine whether the nonseparable strip
could support a meaningful low-data transfer experiment. Neither passed its
prospective gate.

A smooth shared kernel over input and output frequency failed before any
low-data comparison: its best full-operator fit had 3.63% relative error
against a 0.5% capacity criterion. Supplying the exact uncoupled propagation
was much stronger. That carrier left a 5.66% mode-conversion residual, and the
learned correction fit the full operator to 0.099% geometric-mean error across
three seeds. Its held-out target-only curve was nevertheless

| Target fields | Relative error |
|---:|---:|
| 1 | 5.55% |
| 2 | 5.21% |
| 4 | 4.67% |
| 8 | 0.104% |

The curve was monotone, but four fields reduced the one-field error by only
15.9%, missing the registered 20% minimum. The formal verdict is therefore a
rejection, and no source-transfer result was run. The
[smooth-prior pilot](../results/nonseparable_spectral_prior_pilot_2026-07-29/capacity_seed17.json)
and [diagonal-carrier result](../results/nonseparable_diagonal_carrier_2026-07-29_job5700594/artifacts/summary.json)
remain the quantitative record.

The scientific reading is broader than the narrow threshold miss. Exact
uncoupled propagation removes nearly all aggregate error, but it does not
predict unseen mode-conversion directions; most of the remaining error
collapses only when the target drives span the full boundary space. This
matches the earlier conclusion that an after-the-fact compact correction does
not imply a transferable compact dynamics. Designing another prior for this
eight-mode instrument would now optimize the toy rather than test the
research program.

**Decision.** Close this spectral-instrument branch. The next exam is
geometry-bearing adaptation: does experience on DrivAerML reduce the number of
SHIFT-SUV simulations needed, and is any reduction larger for the
boundary-aware model than for a strong generic operator?

This exam can use fresh evidence. The full curated dataset contains
794/99/100 train/validation/test estate cases and 796/99/99 fastback cases.
All twenty previously inspected SHIFT-SUV cases belong to the estate test
split, leaving eighty fresh estate tests; no recorded experiment has used the
fastback test split. The [frozen manifest
inventory](../results/shift_suv_full_dataset_inventory_2026-07-29/inventory.json)
records the split hashes and exclusion policy.

The rival outcomes are now program-level:

| Prospective pattern | Interpretation |
|---|---|
| Pretraining halves the target-label requirement on both body styles. | Reusable source knowledge exists across the geometry-family shift. |
| Both models benefit similarly, or the generic operator benefits more. | Adaptation is real, but boundary-aware structure has not earned an incremental transfer claim. |
| The source advantage reverses between estate and fastback. | Reuse is geometry-conditional rather than a stable response-law principle. |
| Pretraining is neutral or harmful. | The present models remain specialist regressors despite sharing the governing flow problem. |

Only training and validation data may be used to choose an attainable error
level, optimization duration, and seed count. The eighty fresh estate tests
and all fastback tests remain sealed until those choices and the nested target
subsets are frozen.

## 2026-07-30 — The source shapes are closer to fastbacks than estates {#sec-nb-morphology-relation}

The active adaptation study has two live explanations: DrivAerML pretraining
may reuse external-flow knowledge, or it may simply provide a better geometric
starting point for similar vehicle shapes. Before revealing any adaptation
result, an independent geometry-only comparison made the second explanation
directional and falsifiable.

The comparison used the 435 DrivAerML training vehicles and the two frozen
128-case SHIFT-SUV training subsets. Each vehicle was represented by
scale-free, area-weighted spans and second moments of its surface position and
normal distributions. No flow field, validation case, or test case entered the
measurement. Two independent surface samples agreed well: median within-case
descriptor differences were 1.03%--1.14%, with 95th percentiles below 2.04%.

After standardizing the descriptor by the DrivAerML distribution, the
pre-registered energy distances were:

| Target family | Distance from DrivAerML |
|---|---:|
| Fastback | 3.106 |
| Estate | 3.757 |

The estate-minus-fastback contrast was 0.651, with a paired-bootstrap 95%
interval of [0.264, 1.037]. Estate was therefore 1.209 times farther from the
source than fastback, passing the declared 1.10 materiality threshold. An
[independent reduction](../results/shift_suv_morphology_relation_2026-07-30/formal_morphology_relation.json)
reproduced the result from the
[prospective protocol](../results/shift_suv_morphology_relation_preregistration_2026-07-30.json).

**Belief update.** Under this representation-independent morphology
description, DrivAerML is decisively closer to the fastback target family.
Geometry-scaffold reuse now predicts at least a 10% larger pretraining gain on
fastbacks than estates for both architectures. If the adaptation result instead
favors estates—or reverses by architecture—shape proximity is not a sufficient
explanation.

This is not evidence that transfer exists, nor is the descriptor necessarily
the geometry representation learned by either model. It isolates a prospective
direction for one rival explanation while the flow-regime shift remains
confounded.

**Decision.** Keep the adaptation result blinded. Once fixed validation is
complete, compare its family ordering with this frozen morphology ordering
before choosing any new source or architecture experiment.

## 2026-07-30 — Pretraining speeds adaptation but does not halve target labels {#sec-nb-adaptation-pilot-verdict}

DrivAerML initialization carries a reusable optimization signal into
SHIFT-SUV, but the pilot rejects the stronger claim that it halves the number
of target simulations needed. The comparison crossed two architectures,
estate and fastback bodies, nested target sets of 64 and 128 vehicles, and a
symmetric three-rate search. Checkpoints were selected on two common
validation-only surface samples across all 99 cases; the test sets remained
sealed.

The primary half-label ratio compares a pretrained model given 64 target
vehicles with a scratch model given 128. Values below 0.95 were required for a
material target-data saving; every observed ratio was above one:

| Architecture | Target family | Pressure ratio (95% paired-case interval) | WSS ratio |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| MeshTransformer | Estate | 1.294 [1.281, 1.307] | 1.135 |
| MeshTransformer | Fastback | 1.244 [1.229, 1.258] | 1.106 |
| GeoTransolver | Estate | 1.042 [1.021, 1.061] | 1.072 |
| GeoTransolver | Fastback | 1.030 [1.007, 1.068] | 1.029 |

Pretraining nevertheless reduced pressure error when the target-label budget
was held fixed. Geometric-mean scratch/pretrained gains across the 64- and
128-case budgets were 1.089 on estates and 1.075 on fastbacks for
MeshTransformer, versus 1.140 and 1.170 for GeoTransolver. Thus the generic
operator gained more from source initialization: the MeshTransformer/
GeoTransolver gain ratios were 0.955 [0.943, 0.967] on estates and 0.918
[0.909, 0.928] on fastbacks. Boundary-aware structure has not earned an
incremental transfer claim.

The prospective morphology explanation also failed its sufficiency test.
DrivAerML shapes are closer to fastbacks, yet MeshTransformer's fastback/
estate gain ratio was 0.987 [0.978, 0.997], in the opposite direction; its
descriptive interval lay below one. GeoTransolver followed the predicted
direction only weakly, at 1.027 [1.012, 1.042], below the declared 1.10
materiality threshold. Shape proximity alone therefore does not explain the
adaptation gain.

The narrow belief update is:

| Rival account | Verdict from this pilot |
|---|---|
| Reusable source knowledge | Supported only as same-budget optimization acceleration, not target-label saving. |
| Boundary-specific reuse | Refuted at the pilot gate; GeoTransolver benefited more on both families. |
| Geometry-scaffold reuse | Morphology proximity is not a sufficient predictor of source benefit. |
| Specialist regression | Too strong: both models retain some useful source signal, but neither demonstrated half-label efficiency. |

All sixteen selected models were still best at the final registered epoch, and
most selected rates lay on the upper search boundary. The measured gains may
therefore be transient warm-start effects rather than persistent differences
after fair convergence. The [complete formal reduction](../results/shift_suv_adaptation_pilot_2026-07-29/analysis/formal_validation_summary.json)
was reproduced independently; it contains no test result.

**EDIT (2026-07-30):** The paired-case intervals above condition on the
learning rate and epoch chosen on those same 99 validation cases. They are
descriptive sensitivity intervals, not nominal post-selection confidence
intervals. The earlier significance language is therefore withdrawn; the
point estimates and registered materiality verdicts are unchanged.

**Decision.** Do not open the test sets and do not add architectural components.
The next experiment must symmetrically extend the optimization horizon and
refine the learning-rate bracket for the half-label pairs. Source reuse
advances only if the pretrained-64/scratch-128 pressure ratio reaches 0.95 or
lower on both families without worsening wall-shear-stress error by more than
10%; otherwise close this branch as optimization-only transfer.

**EDIT (2026-07-30, before the convergence result):** The last clause
overstated what this experiment can identify. Its two arms are pretrained on
64 target cases and scratch-trained on 128; it can therefore close only the
claim that pretraining replaces *half* of the target labels. Even after both
arms plateau, failure of that gate cannot show that the source benefit is
merely transient, because a matched-update scratch-64 arm is absent. The
*optimization-only* interpretation is withdrawn. If the half-label claim
closes, the next question is whether the same-budget gain persists against
scratch-64 and, if so, how many labels it is actually worth. The
[prospective interpretation amendment](../results/shift_suv_convergence_extension_2026-07-30/prospective_interpretation_amendment.json)
records this boundary; no convergence result was inspected and the registered
numerical gate is unchanged.

## 2026-07-31 — One-step parity: the canonical and legacy paths are not operationally equivalent {#sec-nb-one-step-parity-verdict}

The repaired instrument (v3; the v2 producer had omitted one helper argument
and never measured anything) returned a valid adjudication with the
registered outcome `MATERIAL_PARITY_DIFFERENCE_FAIL`: all eight case/regime
cells fail their BF16 gates. The sharp part is the fresh-seed regime: the
legacy and canonical paths produce whole-model gradients whose cosine rounds
to 1.000000 -- passing the 0.999 gradient gate -- yet the
CombinedOptimizer update differs by 11--15% symmetric relative L2 (update
cosine 0.988--0.994 against a 0.9999 gate). At the trained epoch-491 state
the gradient cosine drops to 0.995--0.999 and the update difference grows to
22--25%. Per-module gradient cosines pass everywhere (>= 0.9976), so the
divergence is a whole-vector effect that the optimizer transform amplifies
from a sub-gate-level input difference, not a single broken module. Read
beside @sec-nb-hqc-campaign: cohort-level field accuracy is noninferior
while single-update equivalence fails. The pre-registered next step is one
fixed 16-step paired microtrajectory
(`studies/phase1_historical_k10000_microtrajectory_prereg_v1_2026-07-29.json`);
the truth table forbids launching a full same-cell retrain from this result.
[Adjudication](../results/historical_k10000_one_step_parity_v3_job332069_2026-07-31/historical_k10000_one_step_parity_adjudication.json);
the 326 MB gradient/update payload stays on AGA and this machine, recorded
by its committed sha256 sidecar.

## 2026-07-31 — Program decision: optimize the model, not the transfer eval {#sec-nb-model-quality-agenda}

Peter's directive, adopted as the governing agenda: the program had drifted
into designing ever-more-elaborate instruments whose purpose was to exhibit
cross-dataset transfer -- eval-first drift, the same failure the 07-29
altitude reset caught one level down. Each instrument was individually
pre-registered and constrained the conclusion (the gates ruled out a favorable half-label headline
hours before this entry), but the trajectory was motivated: iterating on
experiment design until a transfer effect appears is a garden of forking
paths at the meta level. The transfer question is a question about datasets;
this program is about the model. The falsification discipline also applies to the
refocus; its target changes.

**Thesis.** Build the simplest boundary-to-interior surrogate that is
accurate in-family, never catastrophic out-of-family, and indifferent to
discretization -- each property by construction where a mechanism is known
-- measured on one small frozen scorecard that never changes. Success is a
model configuration you would hand a stranger: fewer knobs than the
flagship, no failure mode that produces non-physical output, and a flat
resolution curve instead of a spike at the training resolution.

**The frozen scorecard** (all instruments already exist; no new evals will
be built under this agenda):

1. In-family accuracy: DrivAerML validation pressure + WSS, fixed protocol.
2. Resolution curve: the coverage sweep of @sec-nb-hcc-summary, reported as
   a curve, with the signed diagnostic `pred_rms/true_rms` primary at each
   resolution (the relative-L2 ratio conflates collapse with divergence and
   was retired by the five-seed verdict).
3. Foreign-family boundedness (smoke test, not a claim): zero-shot SHIFT-SUV
   pressure relative L2 finite and < 3.0 on every seed.
4. Seed band: 5 seeds, report min-max on 1-3.
5. Strong-form operator residual (the existing fidelity column).
6. Parameter and knob count.

**The measured defects this agenda attacks, in order:**

1. *Coverage-specific accuracy.* Error minimizes sharply at the training
   resolution; above it the prediction collapses toward zero RMS (4 of 5
   seeds) rather than diverging. Diagnosed root: random subsampling is a
   biased operator (far-field completeness), so training only ever sees one
   coverage (@sec-nb-hdi-summary, @sec-nb-hcc-summary).
2. *Unbounded out-of-family failure.* Checkpoints detonate to 1e3-1e13 on a
   foreign family while a generic baseline stays structured; the degree-1
   homogeneous mode improves the level ~6700x at the median but with a
   2491x seed band, so boundedness is not yet a property of the
   architecture (@sec-nb-wave-summary, @sec-nb-hseed-summary).
3. *Seed instability itself*, which couples to (2) and caps every claim.
4. *GeoTransolver's unexplained 2.34x matched-parameter efficiency* -- the
   one architectural question deferred all program: locate the mechanism of
   the learned soft-slice global exchange and absorb or refute it.
5. *Simplicity debt.* Consolidate to one canonical configuration whose
   every component cites the factorial that earned it; the eight learned
   kernel members are already evidence-orphaned at industrial scale, and
   the trace/self-identification channel (3.8x) stays.

**Closed and parked, with reasons.** The half-label/adaptation branch is
CLOSED with its verdict recorded and unbanked
(@sec-nb-convergence-extension-verdict): suggestive (0.9385 on fastbacks),
unresolved by its own plateau and grid-edge gates, and not pursued further
because the objective is retired -- extending it again would have been
instrument-tuning. The rectangle/nonseparable transfer-instrument line
remains closed. The replay/parity infrastructure line is parked at its
verdict (@sec-nb-one-step-parity-verdict); the staged microtrajectory
pre-registration stays on the shelf unless canonical-path training is
actually blocked. The SHIFT-SUV dataset copy to the second cluster
completes regardless; it serves the smoke test.

**Week one, pre-registered separately:** (a) measure-consistent training --
measure-weighted objectives and mixed-resolution sampling against defect 1,
using the quadrature-measure implementation was completed 2026-07-31; (b) held until
(a) reads out: the bounded-drive-path conjunction against defect 2. One
variable at a time; acceptance criteria on the frozen scorecard only.

## 2026-07-31 — Pre-registration: measure-consistent mixed-resolution training {#sec-nb-mixedres-prereg}

First experiment of the model-quality agenda, against defect 1
(coverage-specific collapse). Hypothesis: the collapse exists because
training only ever sees one coverage of a biased-sampled operator; training
on an unbiased effective measure (Horvitz--Thompson weights, the new target
quadrature measure) across mixed resolutions {2.5k, 5k, 10k, 20k} removes
it. The deciding gate is structural and uses the signed diagnostic that
replaced the retired ratio: at 40k -- a resolution never trained --
`pred_rms/true_rms` must fall in [0.7, 1.3] on all three seeds, against the
historical collapse to 0.055--0.355. One fresh fixed-10k control seed pins
code-epoch drift; every gate is within-experiment. Falsifier: if the
mixed-measure arm still collapses, the defect is architectural, not
sampling-statistical, and the next change must be to the model. Registered
prediction is a coin flip (p ~ 0.55).
[Preregistration](../results/mixedres_training_preregistration_2026-07-31.json)
(sha256 fb2d986a...); implementation: `RandomResolutionSubsampleMesh` (HT
measure unbiasedness unit-tested exact) and the mixedres dataset variant.

## 2026-08-01 — Rotation augmentation creates degenerate measures; amendment excludes it {#sec-nb-mixedres-amendment}

Both arms of the mixed-resolution experiment crashed deterministically: one
rank raised the model's finite-positive-measure validation and its peers
hung in the gradient collective -- the incident that produced the recipe's
new rank-synchronized step failure barrier and the audit of the whole
rank-divergence class. The diagnosis separated data from pipeline: all 484
raw surfaces are clean (per-case fp32 minimum areas 1.4e-11 to 2.3e-9, none
non-positive), while the z-rotation augmentation's fp32 area recomputation
erodes sliver areas by up to 5770x in a 16-angle probe (run_44: 1.38e-11 to
2.39e-15) -- continuous training-time angles make an exact-zero draw
inevitable. The strict validation caught a real numerical defect of the
augmentation, not bad data. Prospective amendment, no result inspected:
augmentation off for both arms (it was incidental to the registered
question and never part of the historical protocol -- this experiment was
the first to ever execute it), the resolution draw moves into the transform
chain, and all lanes restart from epoch 0 rather than mixing protocols
within a run. Every deciding gate is unchanged
([amendment](../results/mixedres_training_amendment_2026-08-01.json),
sha256 f3b284ae...).

## 2026-08-02 — Sliver degeneracy, not rotation, is the hazard {#sec-nb-mixedres-amendment2}

The rotation-removal amendment was refuted within a day: under
augment=false the identical measure-validation failure recurred, on one
lane at the very epoch where it had failed before. The revised mechanism is
sharper: ~1e-11-area sliver cells sit deep enough in fp32 cross-product
cancellation that *any* coordinate perturbation -- centering, rotation, or
device evaluation order -- can round their recomputed area to exact zero.
The new guard logic worked exactly as designed on its first outing:
the step failure barrier surfaced the true ValueError on every occurrence,
and the crash-loop guard stood both affected lanes down after two
identical fingerprints instead of burning the chain. Second prospective
amendment (no gate value inspected): a DropDegenerateCells transform ends
both pipelines, removing cells whose fp32 area is non-positive or
non-finite on exactly the points and device the model validates; lanes
resume from checkpoints because the dropped cells carry zero measure to
fp32 precision, unlike the augmentation change that required a restart
([amendment](../results/mixedres_training_amendment2_2026-08-02.json)).

## 2026-08-03 — All three mixed-resolution gates pass, and the control refutes its own prediction {#sec-nb-mixedres-verdict}

The experiment completed under its two amendments (all four lanes at 500
epochs; 20 sweep evaluations on the 49 held-out validation cases -- the
`id_reference` split named in the preregistration never existed in the
curated manifest, so the val split, disjoint from training, was declared
as the instrument before any value was read). Every registered gate
passes:

| Gate | mixedres s42 / s43 / s44 | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| G1: `pred_rms/true_rms` at 40k in [0.7, 1.3] | 0.979 / 0.977 / 0.973 | pass |
| G2: rel-L2 40k / 10k < 3 | 0.976 / 0.974 / 0.971 | pass |
| G3: in-family 10k cost <= 1.15x control | 1.024 / 1.029 / 1.119 | pass |

Error is now *lower* at 40k than at 10k -- against a historical ratio of
5.5--246 with RMS collapse to 0.055--0.355.

**The registered control prediction failed, and that is the finding.**
The fresh fixed-10k control was predicted to collapse at 40k (p ~ 0.85);
it did not (`pred_rms/true_rms` = 0.973, indistinguishable from the
mixed-resolution arms). The coverage cliff is gone for BOTH arms, so the
cure cannot be attributed to mixed-resolution sampling: it rode a bundled
component of the new code epoch -- most plausibly the measure-consistent
quadrature (Horvitz--Thompson weights and the target quadrature measure)
that the model and objective now consume, which both arms share and the
historical runs lacked. Mixed-resolution sampling is, on this evidence,
unnecessary for resolution transfer at a ~2--12% in-family cost.

**Attribution test, registered before its result:** sweep a historical
old-code-trained flagship checkpoint (the adaptation pilot's frozen
source model) through the identical new-code instrument. If the collapse
vanishes there too, the cure is inference-side measure handling alone and
no retraining was ever needed; if the collapse persists, the cure
required the measure-consistent objective during training.
[Gate reduction](../results/mixedres_training_2026-07-31/sweep/gate_reduction.json).

## 2026-08-03 — Measure-consistent training fixes resolution; old checkpoints differ {#sec-nb-mixedres-attribution}

The registered attribution fork resolves on its second branch. The
old-code-trained flagship, evaluated through the identical new-code
instrument (on the second cluster after the allocation cut; same
snapshot, same gates), outputs pure NaN -- 100% of points, all 48
validation cases, at every resolution, with targets clean. The mechanism
closes coherently: the new pipeline composes Horvitz--Thompson inclusion
weights into the quadrature the model consumes, making the effective
total measure resolution-invariant (the cure), but thereby scaling it by
up to ~1,770x relative to what unweighted-era checkpoints were calibrated
to -- far outside the norm-free drive stream's operating range, whose
measured dose-response NaN'd at 8x shifts. Three conclusions:

1. Defect 1 of the model-quality agenda (coverage-specific collapse) is
   SOLVED by training under the measure-consistent convention; error at
   40k is now slightly *below* 10k on every seed.
2. Mixed-resolution sampling contributed nothing detectable and its
   2--12% in-family cost is unearned: the fixed-resolution
   measure-consistent arm is the recommended default.
3. The convention is calibration-breaking both ways: old checkpoints
   NaN under new-code pipelines (they need a compatibility strip-weights
   path, and would then re-exhibit the collapse), so the fix cannot be
   deployed to historical models without retraining. This deserves a
   prominent compatibility note wherever the measure-weighted logic is upstreamed.

[Attribution reduction](../results/mixedres_training_2026-07-31/sweep/attrib_reduction.json).
Next per the agenda ladder: defect 2, the bounded drive path.

## 2026-08-04 — Stage 0: mixed-resolution training improves foreign-family boundedness {#sec-nb-bounded-stage0-verdict}

The registered gate fails as written -- the fixed-resolution linear

dip under 0.8 on both families -- noted, not banked; all arms remain at
