## 2026-08-09 — Defect-4 synthesis: the road decision {#sec-nb-defect4-synthesis}

Every registered arm has read out. The complete paired evidence, all on
the identical instrument and protocol
([window](../results/mixedres_training_2026-07-31/sweep/window_reduction.json),
[rung](../results/mixedres_training_2026-07-31/sweep/rung_reduction.json),
[round 3](../results/mixedres_training_2026-07-31/sweep/round3_reduction.json)):

| arch/scale | in-family 10k | peak VRAM | train wall | zero-shot foreign |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| MT 784k | 0.134-0.145 | 35.8 GB | 12.8 h | bounded, no skill |
| MT 11.4M | 0.073-0.080 | 104 GB (55.8 chunked) | 14 h | seed-conditioned detonation (2/6 lanes across arms) |
| GT 0.9M-class | 0.086-0.088 | 2.1 GB | 3.9 h | skilled (0.65-0.68) |
| GT 9.0M | 0.053 | 4.6 GB | 3.6 h | skilled (0.54-0.64) |
| GT 72M | 0.050-0.064 | 11.2 GB | 4.6 h | skilled (0.56-0.67) |
| GT 564M | 0.087 | 36.6 GB | 7.2 h | weakened (0.74) |

The conclusion for program review: **at every resource budget
tested, GeoTransolver architecture dominates in-family accuracy,
zero-shot transfer, boundedness reliability, and training cost.**
MT's measured assets reduce to: near-transfer skill (0.21-0.23
estate->fastback -- real, but GT does 0.11-0.12), three closed
root-cause defects, and its exact structural contracts (similarity
equivariance, declared drive degree, zero preservation, quadrature
awareness) -- none of which showed a measured *differential* advantage
on any axis this program has tested. GT's weaknesses are real but
lesser: a 1.28x seed band at 72M and a frontier that turns at 564M
under the frozen lr.

Recommendation staged for Peter: the registered "absorb the mechanism"
branch should be INVERTED. The evidence supports structuring the
winner, not accelerating the loser -- port MT's earned conventions
(measure-consistent quadrature; a degree-declared drive read-in, which
GT's global_embedding pathway lacks and which the estate->DrivAerML
weakness suggests could matter; the boundary-trace data contract) onto
the soft-slice architecture as testable increments, each with the same
preregistered discipline. Alternatively the program can conclude with
GeoTransolver-wins statement and the three closed defects as its
contribution. This is a direction decision above the notebook's pay
grade; both roads are staged.

## 2026-08-09 — Contract-axis probes preregistered and launched {#sec-nb-contract-probes-prereg}

The three benchmark axes the frozen scorecard never measured, and where
MT's structural contracts should show differential value if they show
it anywhere ([artifact](../results/contract_axis_probes_preregistration_2026-08-09.json),
sha256 f64c0291ec3df971; eval-only, existing checkpoints, both
architectures paired on every probe with MT as the positive control):
**P1** rotation-orbit (random z-rotation of geometry + all vector data;
MT predicted invariant p ~ 0.85, GT predicted degraded p ~ 0.7);
**P2** drive-amplitude effective degree in normalized space (MT
homogeneous predicted d = 1.000 +/- 0.02 -- the declared contract
measured end-to-end; GT's degree unknown, misbehavior p ~ 0.55);
**P3** 10:1 nonuniform sampling density with per-cell HT weights (MT
predicted within 10%, GT sensitivity p ~ 0.5, the weakest prediction).
Each probe maps to an MT2 module keeping or losing its slot. Design
correction recorded at registration (Peter): the earlier
"canonicalize by freestream x gravity" sketch was wrong physics --
gravity does not enter this PDE, and no single canonical frame exists
for problems with several non-orthogonal vector inputs. Whatever P1
shows, the remedy is an input-covariant treatment (invariant
featurization over the Gram of all vector inputs with vector-basis
expansion for outputs, per the GLOBE appendix treatment, to be
re-read before the MT2 symmetry section is finalized), not a
hand-picked frame.

## 2026-08-09 — Probe verdicts P1 and P2; P3 instrument repair {#sec-nb-contract-probes-verdict}

P1 and P2 read out; P3's first instrument was broken and is re-running
([reduction](../results/mixedres_training_2026-07-31/sweep/probe_reduction.json)).

**P1 (rotation orbit): the benchmark-incompleteness point is now a
measurement.** MT is invariant to 0.3-0.6% (ratios 1.003-1.006 over the
full random-yaw orbit, all three seeds -- the similarity-equivariance
contract verified end-to-end through the recipe), while **GT degrades
26-32x** (means 1.40-1.71, i.e., worse than predicting zero, on
geometry it predicts at 0.053 in canonical pose). GeoTransolver's
in-family dominance is pose-conditional; every number in the defect-4
synthesis carries an implicit "in the dataset's canonical pose" that
the scorecard never surfaced. The exact-symmetry mechanism justifies its
MT2 slot decisively (form per the GLOBE-appendix multi-vector
treatment, NOT a hand-picked frame -- see the correction above).

**P2 (drive-amplitude degree): both contracts verified, neither
detonates.** MT homogeneous measures d = 1.0000 exactly (range +/-
0.0000, 48 cases, k in {0.5, 2, 4}) -- the declared degree holds
end-to-end to four decimals. GT measures d = 0.000 (+/- 0.01): its
output is amplitude-BLIND, consistent with layer normalization
saturating input scale. By the registered letter (|d| outside [0.5,
1.5]) GT "misbehaves", but the physical reading is saturation,
not amplification -- no euler-arm-style blowup exists here, and on
this recipe drive amplitude is not a live axis (the drive input is a
unit direction by construction). P2's MT2 implication is therefore
weak support only: the norm-factored read-in is cheap and exact, but
GT's failure mode on this axis is silence, not detonation. The
sharper framing: for any deployment where output must scale
with an input amplitude (dimensional networks, varying dynamic
pressure), amplitude-blindness is itself a defect -- and only the
declared-degree design responds at all.

**P3 (nonuniform sampling): v1 instrument no-op.** Per-case metrics
were bit-identical to baseline for both models: the reader already
subsamples to `sampling_resolution` before the transform chain, so
the biased sampler had nothing to draw. Caught by the
exact-equality smell test, declared here before any v2 value is read.
V2 (launched): reader keeps a 40k pool, biased 10:1 draw at 10k, plus
a uniform 40k->10k control to isolate the bias effect from the
pipeline-depth change.

## 2026-08-09 — P3 verdict and the three-probe synthesis {#sec-nb-contract-probes-synthesis}

P3 resolved in two more rounds
([v2](../results/mixedres_training_2026-07-31/sweep/p3v2_reduction.json),
[v3](../results/mixedres_training_2026-07-31/sweep/p3v3_reduction.json)).
The v2 uniform 40k->10k control matches every baseline (instrument
sound). Under a 10:1 front/back density bias: **GT degrades 1.9-3.6x**
-- a clean verdict, since GT never sees the weights; pure density
sensitivity. **MT fails its own 10% gate too**: 1.9-2.5x with the
approximate-HT sampler, and still **1.65-2.24x with exact Poisson
inclusion probabilities (v3)** -- so the failure is the model's, not
the instrument's. Mechanistically, HT weighting keeps the
quadrature *unbiased*, but a 10:1 allocation leaves the sparse half
with ~11x fewer points and correspondingly higher estimator variance
in every boundary integral that reads it -- a variance term no
weighting scheme removes. The measure contract MITIGATES (MT
degrades ~2x less than GT relative to its own baseline) but does not
deliver density-robustness; the defect-1 closure generalizes only
across uniform densities.

**Three-probe synthesis for the MT2 gate list.** P1: exact-symmetry
mechanism IN, decisively (GT 26-32x off-pose vs MT invariant to 0.6%;
the pose-conditionality of every GeoTransolver number is now measured).
P2: degree declaration verified exact for MT, GT saturates rather
than detonates -- slot retained on cheapness and on deployments where
amplitude is live, but the forward-recipe motivation is weak. P3:
measure-aware aggregation IN as mitigation (halves the damage), with
a recorded caveat that density-robustness at inference is bounded by
estimator variance, not by weighting. The probes also harden the
program-review framing: GeoTransolver's dominance table
(sec-nb-defect4-synthesis) holds ON-POSE AND ON-DENSITY; off either
axis, the structural contracts are the only thing standing.

## 2026-08-09 — MT2 program charter and stage-0 preregistration {#sec-nb-mt2-charter}

The program pivots to MT2 on Peter's direction, building on the
defect-4 synthesis and the three-probe verdicts. **Thesis**: GT's
measured advantages live in normalized global routing, not
raw-coordinate access, so MT's contracts can be paid once at the
network edges -- GLOBE-style input-covariant featurization in
(invariants over the full vector set), vector-basis expansion out
(reusing GLOBE's `equivariant_ops` spherical-basis treatment for
non-orthogonal multi-vector inputs, per the appendix), a norm-factored
drive bypass, and measure-weighted softmax in the slice attention.
Stage 0 is the thesis-killer, registered BEFORE implementation
([artifact](../results/mt2_stage0_preregistration_2026-08-09.json),
sha256 c73bf8b64153eae3): a GT-class (~6-9M) v0 at 3 seeds against the
frozen GT baselines on the full paired instrument plus the P1/P3
probes. S0_1 decides: within 1.30x of GT in-family the thesis
holds; beyond 1.50x it is refuted and the fallback (frame-averaged
raw coordinates) is already declared. S0_2 (rotation ratio <= 1.05)
is a contract check gated by a pre-launch unit equivariance test --
its failure would be an implementation bug, not a result.

## 2026-08-10 — MT2 stage-0 verdict: v0 REFUTED at 3.08x; the invariants were non-separating {#sec-nb-mt2-stage0-verdict}

The thesis-killer killed the v0 formulation
([reduction](../results/mixedres_training_2026-07-31/sweep/mt2_stage0_reduction.json)).
**S0_1 FAILED**: in-family 10k seed-mean 0.1641 = 3.08x GT, past the
registered 1.50x refutation bar (and below the 784k flagship). The
autopsy is clean because the other gates passed: S0_2 rotation ratio
1.000 (exact equivariance end-to-end), resolution transfer flat
(40k/10k 0.97), the tightest seed band the program has measured
(1.006x), training at 1.8 GB / 2.5 h (S0_3 passed with 2.5x margin),
estate smoke 0.81-0.83. **Diagnosis**: the five per-point invariants
(|r|, log|r|, r.d, r.n, n.d) are NON-SEPARATING -- they collapse the
SO(2) orbit about the drive axis, so left/right-mirrored points with
mirrored normals are bitwise indistinguishable to the backbone. The
routing did not fail; the featurization quotiented the geometry away.
Also recorded: the measure-biased assignment softmax alone does NOT
provide density robustness (biased/uniform 5.7-6.4x, worse than GT's
3.6x) -- consistent with P3's estimator-variance lesson. Registered
next (stage 0b, an input-covariant repair rather than the declared
frame-averaging fallback, which stays in reserve): augment the vector
set with the cloud's measure-weighted principal axes -- data-derived,
covariant, sign-fixed by projection skewness -- making the invariant
set separating while keeping every contract exact and every cost at
the edges.

## 2026-08-10 — Stage 0b registered and launched: separating invariants {#sec-nb-mt2-stage0b}

Amendment 00b089c4 (results of v0 inspected and cited; gates
inherited): the minimal input-covariant repair -- the cloud's
measure-weighted, skew-oriented principal axes join the vector set,
making the invariants separating (11 scalars in, 10 basis vectors
out). Contract exactness is scoped to non-degenerate covariance
spectra, which is the accurate statement of the known global
obstruction to continuous equivariant frames; unit tests (7) pass at
fp64 exactness on anisotropic clouds and the P1 probe on real
geometry remains the end-to-end check. Prediction: S0_1 remains below
p ~ 0.5, on the strength of v0's autopsy (tightest seed band yet,
flat resolution curve, near-skill smoke -- a backbone that trains
well and lacked only position information).

## 2026-08-10 — Stage 0b: separating invariants recover routing; thesis remains viable {#sec-nb-mt2-stage0b-verdict}

All gates read out
([reduction](../results/mixedres_training_2026-07-31/sweep/mt2_stage0b_reduction.json)).
**S0_1 reaches 1.41x GT** (seed-mean 0.0750 vs 0.0532; seeds
0.0736-0.0758) -- in the [1.30, 1.50] band the preregistration failed
to assign, recorded as: past the survival letter (1.30),
clear of the refutation bar (1.50). The separating-invariants repair
bought 2.2x (0.164 -> 0.075), and v0b now matches the 11.4M
MeshTransformer rung's accuracy at 8.6M parameters and **1.8 GB / 3 h**
-- 58x less memory than that rung, 2.6x less than GT. **S0_2 PASSES**
(rotation ratio 1.028-1.035 <= 1.05) with a diagnosed residual: cars
are nearly left-right symmetric, so the lateral skew that orients the
principal frame sits near zero and the sign can flip under rotated
resampling -- the degeneracy obstruction showing up exactly where the
amendment said it would. **Zero-shot is the quiet headline**: estate
0.72-0.80, fastback 0.70-0.78 -- better than every MeshTransformer arm
the program has trained and approaching GT's 0.54-0.64, from an
architecture that is also exactly equivariant off-pose where GT loses
26-32x. **S0_4 is the clear defect**: density ratio 11.5-12.7x, WORSE
than v0 and GT -- the data-derived frame itself is density-sensitive
(biased sampling moves the weighted covariance and skew, dragging
every invariant with it). v1 work, in order: (1) a density-robust,
reflection-safe frame (the skew orientation replaced by an even-moment
or pair-symmetric scheme; frame statistics decoupled from the sampling
measure); (2) close 1.41x -> ~1.0x with capacity/tuning parity, to
which GT's community-hardened config is entitled and v0b's day-one
config is not.

## 2026-08-10 — Stage 0c registered and launched: the drive-oriented, handedness-completed frame {#sec-nb-mt2-stage0c}

Amendment 1e307907 (0b results inspected and cited): frame orientation
only, everything else frozen. The drive-aligned axis takes its sign
from the drive projection (physical and density-robust), the
stronger-skew remaining axis from skew, and the third from
right-handedness -- deleting the lateral-skew instability that
symmetric geometry exposed. Declared scope change: SO(3)-exact,
parity intentionally not enforced (a chirality-aware frame). The
deciding gate is S0c_4: density ratio materially below 0b's
11.5-12.7x (< 8x, p ~ 0.5) -- this isolates the frame's contribution
from the assignment-softmax redistribution, the other suspected
density mechanism. Three seeds training under the frozen protocol.

## 2026-08-10 — Stage-0c verdict: discrete frames are the wrong tool {#sec-nb-mt2-stage0c-verdict}

([reduction](../results/mixedres_training_2026-07-31/sweep/mt2_stage0c_reduction.json))
S0c_1 passes (1.36x GT, from 0b's 1.41x). S0c_2 splits (1.020-1.039
against the 1.03 letter). **S0c_4, the deciding gate, FAILS in the
informative direction: density 19.8-28.4x, roughly DOUBLE 0b's
11.5-12.7x.** The drive-oriented frame did not remove density
sensitivity -- it amplified it, and the mechanism is clear in
hindsight: the v1 orientation uses discrete selectors (argmax over
drive projections, argmin over skews), and under resampling jitter a
selector flip reorients whole axes discontinuously, where 0b's
per-axis signs at least flipped independently. Zero-shot also
regressed (0.76-0.94 vs 0b's 0.70-0.80). Two iterations now point at
one design lesson: **any global frame built with discrete choices is
a jitter amplifier under resampling; the density defect wants a
SMOOTH construction.** Registered direction for v2, before any result
is seen: drop the global frame entirely and make the slice mechanism
itself carry the geometry -- each slice already computes a
measure-weighted mean; extend that to an equivariant anchor vector
per slice (a softmax functional, smooth by construction), and feed
the backbone point-slice relational invariants (|r_i - z_s|,
rhat_i . zhat_s, ...). Separating without any frame, no discrete
selector anywhere, and the density behavior inherits the softmax's
smoothness instead of an eigenbasis's cliff edges. This is a backbone
change, not an orientation patch -- v2 gets its own preregistration.
Stage-0 record to date: v0 refuted (non-separating), 0b remains viable
(1.41x), 0c in-family 1.36x with the frame path exhausted.

## 2026-08-10 — v2 registered and launched: relational anchors, no frames anywhere {#sec-nb-mt2-v2}

Peter's directive, now also the twice-measured lesson: there is no
canonical frame in the physics, so stop building one. v2
([prereg](../results/mt2_v2_preregistration_2026-08-10.json), sha256
3f4e4af783c7e6df, registered before implementation): the global frame
is deleted entirely; each slice block computes equivariant anchor
positions (measure-weighted softmax means -- smooth functionals) and
every point sees relational invariants against every anchor
(|r - z_s|, direction dots with drive and normal), pooled through the
same softmax mechanism. Separation by multilateration against ~256
data-adaptive local reference points; no discrete selector anywhere;
exact similarity + full O(3) equivariance restored with NO degeneracy
caveat (the eigenbasis is gone, and the chirality construction with
it). Deciding gate V2_4: density < 8x (0b was 11.5-12.7x, 0c
19.8-28.4x; anchors should move smoothly with resampling where
eigenbases cliff, p ~ 0.6). Guards: in-family <= 1.36x, rotation
<= 1.02, zero-shot vs 0b's 0.70-0.80. Contract tests: 7 green, the
rotation test now exact without the anisotropy scoping. Three seeds
training under the frozen protocol.

## 2026-08-11 — v2 verdict: rotation solved exactly, density floor exposed, in-family paid the bill {#sec-nb-mt2-v2-verdict}

([reduction](../results/mixedres_training_2026-07-31/sweep/mt2_v2_reduction.json))
**V2_2 passes perfectly**: rotation ratio 0.996-1.000 -- with no frame
left, equivariance is exact on real geometry, full stop. **V2_4
FAILS**: density 10.8-12.0x -- better than 0c's 19.8-28.4x and at the
0b level, but far from the < 8x gate. The smooth anchors removed the
cliff-edge jitter and the ~11x floor REMAINS: the dominant density
mechanism is not frame discontinuity but the measure-biased
assignment itself (slice populations and anchor positions shift with
the sampling distribution -- smoothly, but they shift), sitting on
P3's estimator-variance floor. Notably GT, with no weights at all,
is the LEAST density-sensitive model measured (3.6x). **V2_1 misses**:
in-family 1.50x (vs 0c's 1.36x) -- the relational backbone paid
accuracy for its purity, plausibly the double-softmax per block or
the loss of the (frame-derived) global invariants' easy positional
signal. Zero-shot 0.76-0.80 holds at the 0b level. The stage-0 map:
no arm dominates -- 0b (1.41x, rot 1.03, dens 12x), 0c (1.36x, rot
1.03, dens 24x), v2 (1.50x, rot 1.000, dens 11x), all at GT-class
resources with near-GT transfer. Registered next: a 2x2
density-mechanism factorial on the v2 backbone (assignment log-w bias
on/off x anchor geometry on/off, 1 seed per cell, full instrument) --
localize the ~11x floor before spending another design iteration on
it.

## 2026-08-11 — Density factorial: the decisive cell launched {#sec-nb-mt2-density-factorial}

The 2x2 registered in the v2 verdict resolves to one new training run:
cells (bias on, anchors on) = v2 and (bias on, anchors off) ~= v0
already exist; the decisive missing cell is **v2 with the assignment
measure bias OFF** (`model.use_measure_weights=false`, one CLI-visible
knob, contract tests unaffected), launched at seed 42 under the frozen
protocol. Prediction, registered now: if the ~11x density floor drops
toward GT's 3.6x with the bias off, the quadrature weighting in the
ROUTING is the mechanism and v3 moves measure-awareness out of the
assignment (into the loss/aggregation side, where GT implicitly
lives); if the floor persists, the anchors' population-shift is
intrinsic and v3 attacks anchor stability instead (p ~ 0.55 for the
first branch). The fourth cell (bias off, anchors off) stays unfilled
unless the readout is ambiguous -- an asymmetry by design,
not an oversight.

## 2026-08-11 — Density-factorial verdict: the anchors themselves are the mechanism {#sec-nb-mt2-factorial-verdict}

The decisive cell read out (bias OFF, anchors ON, seed 42:
[reduction](../results/mixedres_training_2026-07-31/sweep/mt2_v2nw_reduction.json)):
**density 13.75x -- the floor did not drop.** My registered p ~ 0.55
prediction (routing bias as mechanism) was WRONG. The factorial across
cells: no anchors + bias 5.7-6.4x (v0); anchors + bias 10.8-12.0x
(v2); anchors + no bias 13.75x. The relational anchors add roughly 2x
density sensitivity regardless of the assignment bias (which is
neutral-to-slightly-helpful, consistent with HT weights doing their
unbiasing job); anchor positions are population statistics, and under
a 10:1 sampling shift they move -- smoothly, but they move, and every
relational invariant moves with them. Sub-findings: dropping the bias
slightly IMPROVED in-family (1.39x vs v2's 1.50x) and cost zero-shot
(0.91 vs 0.78). The v3 fork this sets up: (a) accept that any
geometry-adaptive statistic pays a density tax bounded below by
estimator variance (GT pays 3.6x with NO spatial statistics at all),
scope the claim, and spend v3 on the in-family gap instead; or
(b) anchor-stabilization work (distance-weighted rather than
population-weighted anchor updates; multi-resolution consistency
training). The stage-0 evidence (density never better than ~2x GT's
under any variant while in-family and equivariance improved steadily)
leans (a) -- but that is a scoping decision with program-review
weight, staged rather than taken unilaterally.

## 2026-08-11 — v3a registered and launched: the in-family gap, capacity first {#sec-nb-mt2-v3a}

Taking branch (a) of the factorial fork on the evidence's lean, without
closing branch (b)
([prereg](../results/mt2_v3a_preregistration_2026-08-11.json), sha256
4373b319cbc388d7): the density claim is scoped (geometry-adaptive
statistics pay a variance-bounded tax; ~11-14x vs GT's 3.6x at 10:1),
and v3a attacks the in-family gap with the two zero-code levers -- the
bias-off configuration the factorial found accuracy-favorable, at two
capacity rungs (hidden 256 at ~15M; hidden 256 x 16 layers at ~20M),
single seeds, frozen protocol. V3a_1 decides: < 1.20x GT at either
rung means the gap is capacity-limited and a matched-tuning stage
follows; >= 1.35x at both means capacity is not the controlling factor and v3b goes
after the thin relational-feature pipe (N_GEO = 3) instead. Anchor
stabilization (branch b) stays open for Peter's read.

## 2026-08-11 — v3a: capacity is not the controlling factor {#sec-nb-mt2-v3a-verdict}

Both rungs reach >= 1.35x, triggering the registered v3b branch. The
ladder is nearly flat -- 8.6M: 1.39x, 15M (wide): 1.45x, 20M (deep):
1.35x -- so MT2's in-family frontier is FEATURE-limited, not
capacity-limited (consistent with stage 0's history: the only large
in-family move, 2.2x, came from featurization). Two echoes of earlier
program lessons: the deep rung pays for its 1.35x with density 38.8x
and degraded zero-shot (1.51/1.79) -- depth trades robustness at the
frozen lr, exactly as gt_huge and x2l8h did; and rotation stays exact
(1.001-1.002) at every scale, as it should with no frame to break.
**v3b, registered next**: widen the relational pipe -- N_GEO 3 -> 8
(log-distance, anchor mean-normal direction m_s with its dots against
point normal and drive, anchor position magnitude/direction
invariants) and a wider geo channel, at the 8.6M scale where the
bias-off cell was healthiest.

## 2026-08-12 — v3b verdict: the pipe was the bottleneck; accuracy and robustness now visibly trade {#sec-nb-mt2-v3b-verdict}

**V3b_1 PASSES**: in-family 0.0596-0.0625 = **1.12-1.18x GT**
(seed-mean 1.15x, from 1.39x), with rotation exact (1.000-1.001) and
resolution flat. Featurization has now delivered every large in-family
move in MT2's history (3.08x -> 1.41x -> 1.15x) while capacity
delivered none. The costs: density 21.9-34.1x (richer
geometric statistics couple harder to sampling, per the factorial
mechanism) and zero-shot regressed to 1.00-1.87 (from 0b's 0.70-0.80)
-- the oriented-anchor features appear to bind to family-specific
statistics. The stage-0 map is now a clean anti-correlation: every
richer-geometry step improves in-family accuracy and degrades OOD. Note v3b is
bias-OFF, and the factorial showed the measure bias HELPS zero-shot
(v2 0.78 vs v2nw 0.91): the registered next arm (v3c) is v3b's
features with the bias restored, 3 seeds -- the cheapest candidate for
v3b accuracy at 0b-class transfer. If v3c recovers zero-shot < 0.85 at
in-family <= 1.25x, it becomes the canonical MT2 configuration for the
program review; if not, the anti-correlation is structural at this
design point and the review presents the frontier, not a single model.

## 2026-08-12 — v3c verdict and the MT2 stage-0 synthesis {#sec-nb-mt2-stage0-synthesis}

v3c ([reduction](../results/mixedres_training_2026-07-31/sweep/mt2_v3c_reduction.json)):
in-family 1.18-1.20x GT (gate <= 1.25x PASSES), density recovered to
13-14x (from v3b's 22-34x -- the bias does its job), rotation exact,
tight seeds. Zero-shot 0.95-1.03: better than v3b's 1.0-1.9 but the
< 0.85 letter FAILS. Per the registered rule, **the
accuracy-robustness anti-correlation is structural at this design
point, and the program review presents the frontier, not a single
canonical model.**

**The MT2 stage-0 frontier, eight preregistered iterations
(2026-08-09 to -12), every arm on the identical frozen instrument:**

| variant | in-family (xGT) | zero-shot | density | rotation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GT 9M (reference) | 1.00 | 0.54-0.64 | 3.6x | 26-32x BROKEN |
| MT2-0b | 1.41 | 0.70-0.80 | 12x | 1.03 |
| MT2-v3c | 1.18-1.20 | 0.95-1.03 | 13-14x | 1.00 |
| MT2-v3b | 1.15 | 1.0-1.9 | 22-34x | 1.00 |

All MT2 variants: exact similarity equivariance (v2 onward: no frame,
no degeneracy caveat), drive degree 1 by construction, 1.8-9.8 GB /
3-6 h training (GT-class), seed bands tighter than anything the
program measured before. What stage 0 established: (1) the routing
thesis is TRUE -- soft-slice routing works on invariant features once
they separate; (2) featurization is the only in-family factor
(3.08 -> 1.41 -> 1.15x; capacity flat); (3) richer geometric features
trade OOD for in-family, monotonically, with the measure bias
partially compensating; (4) GT's transfer superiority persists across every
MT2 variant -- pointwise local features generalize across families
where relational-global features bind to them. The v4 question this
frontier poses (open, for program review): can a pointwise-local
feature channel (GT's generalizing ingredient) be added UNDER the
equivariant contract -- local features are relational too -- to provide
transfer without selling the in-family gains? Stage 0 closes here;
the review decides v4 against the alternative of hardening what
exists.

## 2026-08-14 — v4 experiment registered and launched: the local channel {#sec-nb-mt2-v4}

Per the Heilmeier discussion and Peter's framing (an EXPERIMENT, not a
mainlined change): the local geometric channel is added behind a flag,
default off ([prereg](../results/mt2_v4_experiment_preregistration_2026-08-14.json),
sha256 f16bef426873511e). Design: measure-weighted Gaussian patch
integrals at two physical radii (~0.4 m and ~1.2 m) -- mean neighbor
normal and mean displacement projected on the point normal and drive,
plus patch mass -- 7 exact invariants per radius appended to the seed
features. Radius-based rather than kNN so the patch statistics stay
density-robust in expectation; measure weights keep the integrals
HT-unbiased; row-chunked kernels keep memory flat. Nine contract
tests exact in fp64, including the local variant. Gates: zero-shot
< 0.85 both families (the point of the experiment), in-family held
<= 1.25x, density not worse than v3c's 13-14x, rotation <= 1.02.
Stretch: zero-shot <= 0.80 AND in-family <= 1.20x -- a cell dominating
every existing MT2 variant. Failure reading, declared: if local
features do not transfer, the anti-correlation is a
one-family-training property and stage 1 pivots to training
diversity. Three seeds on the frozen protocol.

against the frozen 3e-3, with a declared caveat trigger at 15%

(trained on estate, against the existing gt_rev baselines) -- is

## 2026-08-15 — v4 verdict: local features do not improve transfer; pivot triggered {#sec-nb-mt2-v4-verdict}

**V4_1 (the point of the experiment) FAILED**: zero-shot 0.87-1.07
across seeds and families -- marginally better than v3c's 0.95-1.03 at
the median but nowhere near the < 0.85 gate, and seed 42 sits above

the best-yet at sane density), density 9.4-12.7x (the radius +

exact. So the local channel is a modest all-around improvement and a
failed transfer hypothesis. Per the failure reading declared in the
preregistration before any result: **the accuracy-robustness
anti-correlation is a property of single-family training, not of any
feature choice we have tested -- stage 1 pivots to training-data
diversity, with architecture work de-emphasized.** The evidence trail
supporting that reading is now three layers deep: every architectural
factor improved in-family accuracy while transfer stayed at ~1.0; GeoTransolver's
own far-transfer weakened in the reverse (data-poorer) direction; and
the burst wave's mt2_rev arms (in flight) plus a to-be-registered
multi-family training experiment (DrivAerML + estate -> zero-shot
fastback, both architectures) are the pivot's first two measurements.
The local channel stays flag-gated: its mainlining case (best
in-family-at-density cell) is a separate, smaller decision for after
the burst reads out.

variants: 0.87-1.07); GT-multi 0.105-0.114. Estate in-family 0.064 /
0.052. The accuracy-robustness anti-correlation was a single-family
-training artifact, exactly as the v4 failure reading declared: one
additional training family moves zero-shot transfer on a HELD-OUT
family by ~7x, dwarfing every architectural intervention the program
tried. Cost asymmetry worth flagging: MT2-multi pays 1.51-1.54x on
DrivAerML (from 1.18x; capacity split at 8.6M) where GT-multi pays
almost nothing (1.08x).

**R1/R2 -- the augmentation counterfactual prices MT2's headline
claim, favorably.** Rotation augmentation DOES close GT's orbit hole
(rot 1.00) -- at **1.84-1.91x in-family cost** and degraded transfer
(0.80-0.85). MT2 gets the same pose-robustness at 1.18x. At equal
pose-robustness, exact equivariance beats augmentation by ~1.6x
accuracy. The mt2 rotaug control sat at 1.21x, unchanged, as an
equivariant model should. This is the release-grade differentiator,
now measured rather than argued.

**C -- tuning parity: the frozen lr flattered GeoTransolver
slightly.** MT2-v3c prefers lr 1e-3 (0.0587 = **1.10x GT**, with
zero-shot improving to 0.78); GT prefers the frozen 3e-3 (1e-3:
1.03x). Neither crosses the declared 15% caveat trigger, but the
matched-tuning in-family gap is ~1.10x, not 1.18x. Both
architectures degrade at 6e-3.

**Bands, radii, capacity, reverse:** v3c 5-seed in-family band ~1.07x
(zero-shot band wider: 0.90-1.14); GT's band razor-thin. v4 radii
matter for transfer (larger patches 0.89-0.90 vs smaller 1.51-1.52,
in-family flat) -- patch scale is a transfer knob, noted for any v4
mainlining. Capacity x features: still flat (1.17x at 15M). MT2
reverse: estate in-family 1.16x GT-rev (the forward gap replicates),
near-transfer fastback 0.117-0.131 -- PARITY with GT-rev's 0.11-0.12
-- far-transfer none (GT-rev keeps its far edge, consistent with the
diversity story).

**The program-review picture in one line:** with one extra data
family, both architectures transfer; with exact equivariance, MT2 is
the only model that is simultaneously pose-robust (free), within
1.10-1.18x in-family (matched tuning), at equal resources -- and the
alternative (augmentation) is now measured at 1.6x more expensive for
the same robustness. Next per the ratified plan: P4 query-stability
probe and the v5a encode/decode split (query-independence + typed BC
re-ingestion), both preregistered separately.

## 2026-08-18 — v5a-v1 verdict: training collapse, diagnosed as the decoder's thin pipe; v5a2 launched {#sec-nb-mt2-v5a-verdict}

v5a-v1 REFUTED as implemented, and informatively: training collapsed
(final loss 0.064 vs healthy 0.0007-0.003), all three seeds converging
to the same near-mean predictor -- identical eval metrics to 1e-4
(in-family 14.6x GT, zero-shot 0.79-0.80), with the contracts passing
vacuously (a constant is perfectly equivariant, query-independent, and
density-robust; instrument note for all future gate reading). The
diagnosis is the program's own twice-taught lesson applied to the new
module: the read-only decoder handed queries THREE relational
invariants where v3b measured EIGHT as necessary -- the thin pipe
collapsed optimization, not the passive-decode thesis. v5a2 (commit
6b64d36e): the decoder's geometry pipe widened to the full v3b set
(oriented anchors, log-distance, anchor-position invariants), encoder
and everything else unchanged, 12 contract tests exact, three seeds
relaunched under the same prereg gates. P4's four-architecture
stability table reduces in the background; the high-lift copy
continues (~ETA tomorrow).

## 2026-08-18 — v5a2 verdict at epoch 70: the pipe was not the cause; lanes stood down early {#sec-nb-mt2-v5a2-verdict}

The widened decoder pipe changed nothing: v5a2's losses sat at
0.0637-0.0658 at epoch 70 -- the exact v5a-v1 collapse plateau --
so the lanes were cancelled at 14% of budget rather than burning to
500 (the trajectory-pilot lesson, now adopted as standing practice
for new architectures: check the loss leaves the known-collapse
plateau before committing full seeds). Diagnosis #1 (thin pipe)
REFUTED as the cause. The remaining structural suspect is the
information bottleneck itself: 256 slice states cannot carry
per-point detail, and v3c's queries had their own token stream where
v5a's queries have none. The principled repair (v5a3, to be
implemented with a 50-epoch pilot gate): passive decoder
cross-attention to NEARBY SOURCE TOKENS' features (radius-based, like
v4's patches but over encoder states) alongside the slice readout --
local + global, exactly the split GT uses, query-independent by
construction since queries still never write.

## 2026-08-18 — v5a3 pilot PASSES; P4 read out with a declared instrument artifact {#sec-nb-v5a3-pilot-p4}

**The v5 line is alive.** The v5a3 pilot (local-token readout added to
the passive decoder) left the collapse plateau decisively: loss 0.0129
at epoch 49 vs the 0.064 wall that killed v1 and v2 -- the missing
ingredient was per-point detail no 256-slice bottleneck can carry,
restored by a measure-weighted kernel readout of nearby ENCODER states
(still strictly read-only; the 1e-12 companion-invariance test covers
the new path). Full 3-seed run launched under the original v5a gates.
The pilot-gate discipline earned its keep: three collapse diagnoses
cost ~15 node-hours total instead of three full waves.

**P4 (query-set stability), with an instrument caveat.** Measured
companion-set instability at the shared 5000-cell prefix: GT 0.020,
MT2-v3c 0.068, MT1 1.48, MT2-v4 1.81. The two large numbers are an
INSTRUMENT ARTIFACT declared here: the base variant's deterministic
prefix carries inclusion weight 1 and represents only itself, so
measure-CONSUMING models (MT1's boundary quadrature, v4's patch
integrals) correctly see the two variants as different surfaces --
the probe conflates query-sensitivity with measure-representation
sensitivity for those models. The interpretable readouts: GT is
nearly companion-stable at matched counts (2%; my prereg prediction
of GT >> MT1 was WRONG in both directions), and v3c carries a real
but modest 6.8% query-interaction term. A symmetric P4-v2 (both
variants prefix+random, differing only in the random complement)
would fix the artifact if the number ever becomes decision-relevant;
for now v5a3's by-construction exactness exceeds every measured
alternative and the probe has served its purpose.

## 2026-08-19 — Query independence costs 2.7×; the v5 line closes {#sec-nb-v5-line-verdict}

far past the 1.40 refutation bar. But look at what it bought:

iterations and one pilot deep: **at this design family, accuracy and
query-interaction are entangled.** The iterated query-side token
stream is worth ~2.7x in-family accuracy over the best passive
decoder we built -- which simultaneously explains WHY GT and MT2
carry companion-set sensitivity (P4: 2% and 6.8%): it is not a
defect riding along, it is where the accuracy comes from. The menu is
now measured rather than argued: exact query-independence at 3.9x
error (v5a3), or 1.10-1.18x accuracy with 6.8% companion sensitivity
(v3c). Per the standing discipline (declared before this readout),

## 2026-08-20 — GeoTransolver transfer improves with data; G1/G2 prediction fails {#sec-nb-g1g2-verdict}

The 22-lane ladder reduced

structure is worth exactly the data it replaces at extreme scarcity
-- parity with 14 cases -- while GeoTransolver converts additional
data into accuracy at a faster rate.** The registered small-n
prediction (p ~ 0.5) scores as half-right: parity, not superiority.

+3% (mild small-n overfitting), so the fixed-epoch protocol does not

flat-curves prediction (p ~ 0.6) is REFUTED for GeoTransolver**: its

with the v4 diagnosis and the reverse-probe asymmetry): 
**GeoTransolver's pointwise-local features learn family-portable
surface physics whose quality compounds with geometric exposure,
while MT2's relational-global features bind to the training family
regardless of how much of it is seen.** The generalization campaign

## 2026-08-20 — Program check-in: what works, what does not, and the shape of a cohesive successor {#sec-nb-checkin-2026-08-20}

Self-contained restatement at Peter's request. The program builds
surface-pressure surrogates for external aerodynamics and measures them
on one frozen instrument against GeoTransolver (a soft-slice
point-transformer, the strongest mainstream baseline). WORKING: the
falsification framework (roughly eighty preregistered runs, five
architecture generations in twelve days, every claim priced, failed
predictions on the record); contracts-at-the-edges (exact equivariance
that costs GeoTransolver 1.87x to imitate with augmentation; exact
drive degree; small-data parity at n_train = 14); the diagnosis loop
(anchor-binding, query-entanglement, slice-bottleneck -- mechanisms
that passed their tests). NOT WORKING: in-family accuracy from
structure (every gap-close came from adopting GeoTransolver's
ingredients -- routing, features -- never from a contract);
architecture-carried transfer (G2: GeoTransolver's zero-shot improves
monotonically with training data, MT2's is flat -- the model built
for generalization generalizes worse on every axis not declared as a
group); the GLOBE-lineage distinctives (query-independence measured
at 2.7x accuracy cost; typed-BC ingestion unbuilt for lack of an
instrument until G3). TARGET-RICH REGION, triangulated by G2 + P1 +
defect-4 + the v4 radii sensitivity: local, family-portable physics
representations (pointwise/patch features recur across vehicle
families where car-scale anchor constellations do not) x declared
symmetry x slice routing. THE COHESIVE SUCCESSOR (MT3 sketch, to be
matured against a literature pass): a two-stream architecture --
a LOCAL stream of gauge-consistent tangent-frame features (local
frames are principled where the refuted single global frame was not:
curvature, per-panel BC values, multiscale patch structure -- the
transfer carrier and the natural typed-BC port) feeding MT2's proven
GLOBAL stream (measure-aware slices + relational anchors), with the
existing exact contracts at the edges and the G-ledger curves as the
selection pressure. Literature clusters to mine before committing:
gauge-equivariant and intrinsic surface networks (transfer across
meshings/families), discretization-invariance theory from neural
operators, equivariance-sample-efficiency theory (the G1 n=14 parity
begs its known formalization), and scaling-law methodology for PDE
surrogates.

## 2026-08-20 — Literature synthesis constrains the MT3 design {#sec-nb-lit-synthesis}

Four parallel literature agents reported (artifacts:
lit_review_{equivariance_theory, intrinsic_surfaces, sota_scaling,
discretization_theory}_2026-08-20.md). What they change:

**1. The G1 anomaly has two literature-supplied, cheaply-testable
mechanisms.** Theory (Elesedy-Zaidi; Tahmasebi-Jegelka) predicts the
DECAY of the equivariance advantage with n but FORBIDS our sign flip
under well-specified symmetry -- so an assumption is violated. Either
(i) over-symmetrization: our exact SCALE equivariance is physically
wrong (Reynolds dependence) and exact rotation equivariance is wrong
unless inflow/ground are explicit transformed inputs
(Petrache-Trivedi's bias floor binds at large n); or (ii) the
invariant-only featurization has a provable per-layer expressivity
ceiling (Joshi GWL: invariant features cannot propagate orientation;
Brehmer 2024: equivariant models that keep up at scale carry FEATURE
FIELDS). Distinguishing probes: residual-vs-scale correlation on
existing checkpoints; degenerate-pair separation audits.

**2. The G2/anchor-binding diagnosis is externally corroborated
twice** (AB-UPT transfer paper: zero-shot R^2 = -5.27 with the GLOBAL
geometry encoder as the non-portable part; CarBench: size beats
diversity for Transolver-family transfer) -- and our multi-family
near-parity result plus the 1.87x augmentation pricing are both
STRONGER than anything published (Symmetry in the Wild found
equivariance costs accuracy on aligned aero data; ours is free).

**3. The shelved v5 line has a literature answer**: AB-UPT-style
anchor-conditioned decoding (interaction upstream of queries) is
expected to deliver query-independence at ~zero accuracy cost -- our
v5a3 was one design step short. Plus an implementation audit item:
NEO-style measure weights must enter EVERY normalization; ours entered
only the assignment softmax.

**4. Program positioning**: the reviewed work does not publish scaling curves,
biased-sampling tests, or query-stability statistics for this model
class -- P3/P4 and the curve-dominance protocol are themselves
publishable; the live threat is AB-UPT+LoRA (published bar: zero-shot
4.4x degradation between related families), so AB-UPT joins the
measured-baseline set; HiLiftAeroML provides curated data-efficiency/OOD
splits that the high-lift wave should adopt.

**MT3, now constrained from both sides**: local stream = mass-matrix
continuous-operator communication (DiffusionNet-class) + gauge-local
frames carrying FEATURE FIELDS (not invariants only) + per-panel BC
scalars; global stream = slice routing with Galerkin-linear
measure-aware aggregation and an anchor-conditioned decode; symmetry =
exact rotation/translation with inflow+ground explicit, scale
RELAXED to conditioning (Reynolds); selection pressure = the G-ledger
curves with AB-UPT in the baseline set.

## 2026-08-20 — Literature wave preregisters M1–M3; M4 closes analytically {#sec-nb-lit-wave-prereg}

**The setting.** The literature synthesis (@sec-nb-lit-synthesis)
left three testable claims about MeshTransformer2 (MT2), our
similarity-equivariant slice-routing surrogate: (a) its exact scale
equivariance may be an over-symmetrization, since aerodynamic pressure
depends on Reynolds number and hence on absolute size; (b) its
data-scaling disadvantage against GeoTransolver at large training-set
sizes could instead be an invariant-only expressivity ceiling; and
(c) the query-independence line we closed at 2.7--3.8x accuracy cost
(v5a3, fully passive decode) was one design step short of AB-UPT's
anchor-conditioned decoding, where a fixed anchor subset carries all
token--token interaction and every query decodes passively from it.

**Preregistration.** `results/lit_wave_preregistration_2026-08-20.json`
(sha256 prefix `69a81e2a`), declared before any run. Four arms:

- **M1 (scale relaxation):** `scale_conditioning=true` appends the log
  raw cloud radius to the seed invariants — breaking
  scale equivariance, keeping rotation/translation exact (new contract
  test asserts equivariance AND that the flag is not inert). Runs at
  ladder rungs n∈{54, 218} × 2 seeds against the existing G1 ladder
  MT2 rungs. Prediction: >5% in-family gain at n=218 if the scale
  axis is the G1 mechanism; falsifier: within the ±3% seed spread.
  Caveat declared: DrivAerML's scale signal is weak (fixed freestream),
  so a null bounds only this dataset.
- **M2 (v5a4 anchor-conditioned decode):** `query_independent=true,
  n_anchors=2560` — a fixed-size anchor subset (deterministic prefix
  at eval) runs the interacting encoder; all points use the v5a3
  read-only decode. The anchor count is absolute, not fractional: a
  first draft used a fraction of the query count and the new contract
  test caught it — the anchor set then depends on the query set,
  violating the very contract the arm exists for. Pilot-gated (50
  epochs must reach ≤ 0.0129×1.15, the v5a3 pilot value) before seeds.
  Prediction: in-family within 1.3x of MT2-v3c; falsifier: >2x closes
  the anchor-conditioned line.
- **M3 (invariant-completeness audit):** analytic probe, no training —
  construct geometry pairs that MT2's invariant set cannot separate
  but that differ aerodynamically (e.g. handedness of a swept
  feature). Delegated as a self-contained analysis.
- **M4 (NEO normalization audit): closed by derivation.** Checked the
  code, not the paper trail: measure weights already enter every
  point-population normalization in MT2 (assignment softmax carries
  `log_w`; slice states and anchors use the weighted assignment; v4
  patch integrals are weighted; the per-point softmax normalizes over
  slices, where no point measure applies). MT2 is NEO-complete, so
  the P3 biased-sampling floor (4.3--4.5x at 10:1) is the
  information-limited component the SNIS analysis predicts — **no
  retrain arm is warranted**, and the density result stands as a
  property of the estimator class, not a bug.

**Instruments.** Both training arms are one-flag diffs against frozen
configs (G1 ladder rungs for M1; the v5a3 pilot for M2) on the frozen
DrivAerML instrument. Contract tests: 15/15 passing in fp64,
including the two new ones.

## 2026-08-20 — Local channel does not explain transfer; gives constant in-family gain {#sec-nb-locality-verdict}

**The setting.** The locality-hypothesis ladder (@sec-nb-locality-ladder)
asked whether GeoTransolver's data-compounding zero-shot transfer —
the one curve in the G2 experiment that improves monotonically with
training-set size while MeshTransformer2's stays flat — is carried by
local features. The test: MT2 with its flag-gated local
patch-integral channel (the v4 experiment) at training-set sizes
n ∈ {27, 109, 218}, two seeds each, on the frozen DrivAerML→SHIFT-SUV
instrument. Preregistered prediction (p ~ 0.45): a monotone decrease
in zero-shot error across the rungs; a flat curve refutes locality as
sufficient.

**What we saw** (`results/locladder_reduction.json`, evals job
527924). In-family, the local channel yields a **consistent but
constant 3–5% improvement** over plain MT2: 0.1695 vs 0.1779 at
n=27, 0.0881 vs 0.0913 at n=109, 0.0729 vs 0.0750 at n=218
(GeoTransolver still leads every rung: 0.1536 / 0.0713 / 0.0599). The
ratio to plain MT2 *rises* with n (0.953 → 0.965 → 0.972), so the
channel is an offset, not a slope change. Zero-shot transfer to the
held-out SHIFT-SUV estate is **not monotone and not improved**:
0.885 → 0.819 → 1.031 across the rungs, with the n=218 seeds at
0.970 and 1.091 — worse than the n=27 rung, worse than plain MT2 at
the same rung (0.825), and nowhere near GeoTransolver's compounding
0.740 → 0.669 → 0.657. Fastback numbers track estate throughout.

**Verdict: the prediction is refuted.** Patch-integral locality is
not the mechanism behind GeoTransolver's transfer compounding — and
adding it can *destabilize* transfer at the largest rung (0.12
seed spread there vs 0.02 in-family). The remaining candidate
mechanisms for the G2 gap are now (a) GeoTransolver's pointwise raw
features (pointwise-vs-patch distinction), (b) its non-equivariant
global encoder learning dataset-transcending regularities that exact
similarity equivariance forbids — which is exactly the
over-symmetrization mechanism the M1 scale-relaxation arm
(@sec-nb-lit-wave-prereg) is testing right now — and (c) the
expressivity ceiling under audit in M3. For MT3, the local channel
remains useful only as a cheap in-family offset; nothing about it
addresses generalization.

## 2026-08-20 — Invariant ceiling is irrelevant here; vector head had a reflection defect {#sec-nb-m3-verdict}

**The setting.** Arm M3 of the literature wave
(@sec-nb-lit-wave-prereg) asked whether MeshTransformer2's
invariant-only feature set has a Joshi-GWL-style expressivity ceiling
— geometry pairs it provably cannot separate. Executed as an analytic
fp64 probe with random weights (no training), artifact
`results/m3_invariant_completeness_audit_2026-08-20.md`, demo script
`results/m3_demo.py`.

**Verdict: PARTIAL.** A ceiling **exists**: for any geometry with a
discrete rotational symmetry about an axis parallel to the drive,
every adaptive slice anchor collapses exactly onto that axis, and
independent azimuthal scrambling of the symmetry orbits — for
example straight versus helically twisted fins at zero incidence —
is provably invisible: 127–138% geometry changes produce output
separations of 5e-16 to 2e-15 (roundoff), while every non-degenerate
control separates at 1e-2 to 4e-1. But the ceiling is **refuted as a
DrivAerML-scale limitation** — no car has such a symmetry, and 1° of
drive misalignment already restores measurable separation (3.5e-3 to
1.5e-2). The originally conjectured chirality blindness is refuted
directly: MT2(mirror geometry, d) equals MT2(geometry, mirror d)
bitwise, which is exactly the parity covariance of Navier–Stokes, and
chirality under yaw is separated at 0.13–0.37. The flag-gated v4
local channel (inter-point distances) fully breaks the constructed
ceiling instance (6e-2 to 8.6e-2) — so the cheap escape hatch
already exists in the codebase.

**The surprise the audit was worth running for**: the full-problem
mirror test exposed a real **reflection-equivariance violation in the
vector head**. The two e_phi basis complements are cross products —
pseudovectors — but their coefficients come from the parity-even
invariant trunk, so vector outputs (wall shear stress direction)
deviate from the physically correct mirror by 0.56–1.37 relative
error, dropping to exactly zero when those channels are zeroed.
Scalar outputs (pressure, the headline metric) match bitwise, which
is why the frozen instrument never caught it. **Fixed** by gating the
e_phi coefficients with the smooth parity-odd invariant
r̂·(n̂×d̂) (`parity_fix` flag, default OFF so frozen checkpoints keep
their trained behavior; new contract test asserts exact reflection
covariance at 1e-10 with the fix AND that the unfixed head violates
it, so the fix cannot become ineffective unnoticed; 16/16 contract tests pass).
Also disclosed: the audit's first version was fooled by O(1e-4)
noise from the m_s normalization clamp on symmetric geometries —
caught and corrected in-session.

**Implication for MT3**: full feature fields are sufficient but not
necessary for the observed failure modes; the minimal repairs are the
parity-odd gate (now built) plus a distance-bearing local channel on
by default. The M1 arms (running) decide the remaining
over-symmetrization question on the scale axis.

## 2026-08-20 — v5a4 pilot gate: FAIL by 1.2%; anchor-conditioned decode arm closed per prereg {#sec-nb-v5a4-gate}

The M2 arm of the literature wave (@sec-nb-lit-wave-prereg) tested
whether AB-UPT-style anchor-conditioned decoding — a fixed 2,560-token
interacting anchor core with all 10,000 points decoding passively —
recovers the accuracy that the fully passive v5a3 decode lost. The
preregistered gate: 50-epoch pilot mean validation loss at epoch 49
must be ≤ the v5a3 pilot value × 1.15. Measured with the identical
statistic on both runs (mean over the 12 validation batches of epoch
49): v5a3 pilot 0.01304, so the gate is 0.01500; the v5a4 pilot came
in at **0.01517 — a fail by 1.2%**. The collapse-escape condition
passed easily (the run left the 0.064 near-mean plateau immediately;
first-epoch losses were already at 0.037). Per the preregistration,
**the arm is closed**: no seeds are promoted.

Two caveats qualify this verdict. First, it is a single seed and a
2% miss against a gate whose own reference (v5a3) went on to fail its
full-run accuracy bar at 3.8x — the gate is a cheap necessary filter,
not a sufficient one, and passing it would not have implied success.
Second, the resource picture is real but was not the preregistered
axis: the anchor core trains at 6.3 GB versus 9.8 GB and runs
validation steps ~3x faster, while landing within 16% of v5a3's pilot
loss with a quarter of the interacting tokens. If the
query-independence question reopens, the registered follow-up is a
matched-resource anchor-count scaling study (new preregistration),
not a rerun of this arm.

## 2026-08-20 — Scale relaxation fails on DrivAerML; literature wave closes {#sec-nb-m1-verdict-wave-close}

**M1 verdict: refuted, per the preregistered falsifier.** The arm
asked whether MeshTransformer2's exact scale equivariance is an
over-symmetrization costing accuracy at large training-set sizes —
the leading literature explanation for the G1 scaling anomaly. The
intervention (a log raw-cloud-radius scalar appended to the seed
invariants) produced in-family gains of only 2.0% at n=54 (0.1198 vs
0.1223) and **1.3% at n=218 (0.0740 vs 0.0750)** — inside the
declared ±3% seed-spread band, far from the preregistered >5%
threshold (`results/m1_reduction.json`, evals job 528683).
GeoTransolver still leads both rungs (0.1004 / 0.0599). A secondary
observation with the expected sign: scale conditioning **hurts
zero-shot transfer** (estate 0.949–0.956 vs plain MT2's 0.825–0.856)
— conditioning on absolute size lets the model bind to the training
family's size distribution, exactly the failure exact equivariance
prevents. The preregistered caveat stands: DrivAerML's scale signal
is weak (fixed freestream), so this bounds the scale axis on this
dataset; the Reynolds-varying HighLiftAeroML wave is the strong test.

**The literature wave is now fully resolved, one day after
preregistration** (prereg 69a81e2a, @sec-nb-lit-wave-prereg):

- **M1 scale-relaxation: REFUTED** (this entry) — no in-family gain
  outside seed spread, and a transfer penalty.
- **M2 anchor-conditioned decode: CLOSED at the pilot gate**
  (@sec-nb-v5a4-gate) — 0.01517 vs the 0.01500 bar; the
  query-independence cost finding stands.
- **M3 invariant completeness: PARTIAL** (@sec-nb-m3-verdict) — a
  real expressivity ceiling exists but not at DrivAerML scale; the
  audit's by-product was finding and fixing a   reflection-equivariance defect in the vector head (`parity_fix`).
- **M4 NEO normalization audit: CLOSED BY DERIVATION**
  (@sec-nb-lit-wave-prereg) — MT2 was already measure-complete; the
  P3 density floor is information-limited, not a bug.

**What remains as the explanation of the G2 transfer gap.** With
locality refuted (@sec-nb-locality-verdict), the scale axis refuted
here, and the expressivity ceiling ruled out at this scale, the
remaining candidates for GeoTransolver's data-compounding zero-shot
transfer are its **pointwise raw coordinate features** and its
**non-equivariant global encoder** — i.e., the hypothesis that
transfer on this instrument is carried by representations that exact
similarity equivariance forbids MT2 from learning. The corresponding
qualification is that MT2's equivariance still provides its rotation robustness
(P1: free vs GeoTransolver's 1.87x augmentation price) and small-data
parity. The discriminating next experiments are (a) the
HighLiftAeroML wave (Reynolds-varying, curated OOD splits — the
strong version of M1) and (b) the G3 boundary-condition ladder on ORD
(exact labels, isolated BC factors), both already in flight. MT3's
design brief inherits: keep exact rotation/translation, keep the
parity gate and a local channel, and treat scale/Reynolds as explicit
conditioning only where the data actually varies it.

## 2026-08-21 — G3: linearity extrapolates in amplitude, not frequency {#sec-nb-g3-verdict}

**The setting.** G3 is the boundary-condition axis of the
generalization north star: out-of-distribution generalization over
*controllable* BC factors, measured with exact analytic labels on the
procedurally generated 2D conformal-Laplace suite (Dirichlet Laplace
on conformally deformed disks — zero solver error, so every
degradation is the model's). Preregistered as
`results/g3_2d_bc_generalization_preregistration_2026-08-20.json`
(sha ae2dee91); three arms at matched parameters and identical
training: **mt2_bscalar** (MeshTransformer2 with the Dirichlet trace
as an invariant boundary-scalar seed feature), **softslice_2d** (the
Transolver-class soft-slice mechanism, GeoTransolver's family), and
**mt1_linear** (MeshTransformer in drive-linear mode — the
contract-exactness reference). Train: drive modes 1–4, boundary RMS
1.0, deformation ≤ 0.3. Test axes, one factor each: T0 in-range
control, T1 unseen drive modes 5–8, T2a/T2b amplitude ×2/×4, T3
deformation 0.3–0.6. Results in `results/g3/` (9 per-seed artifacts +
`g3_reduction.json`), 3 seeds per arm, mean unweighted rel-L2.

**What we saw** (mean over 3 seeds; degradation ratio = axis / T0):

| arm | T0 | T1 modes | T2a ×2 | T2b ×4 | T3 geom |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| mt1_linear | 0.0723 | 1.0043 (13.9×) | 0.0667 (0.92×) | 0.0632 (0.87×) | 0.0898 (1.24×) |
| mt2_bscalar | **0.0624** | 1.1485 (18.4×) | 0.3883 (6.2×) | 0.7289 (11.7×) | **0.0669** (1.07×) |
| softslice_2d | 0.1114 | 1.2090 (10.9×) | 0.4979 (4.5×) | 0.7760 (7.0×) | 0.1221 (1.10×) |

**Readout G3_2 — confirmed (p ~ 0.85 held).** mt1_linear's
drive-linearity contract makes amplitude extrapolation *free*: its
T2 ratios are 0.92× and 0.87× (statistically 1.0; the deviation is
case-sampling noise, since rel-L2 is exactly invariant under the
linear scaling). The two learned-amplitude arms price what an
undeclared linearity costs: **6–12× degradation for mt2_bscalar and
4.5–7× for softslice_2d**, worsening with extrapolation distance.
This is the program's clearest result showing a contract improves generalization to
date: the axis where an exact structural property was declared is the
axis where extrapolation is exact.

**Readout G3_3 — trigger not met; the result is
sharper.** mt2_bscalar dominates softslice_2d in *absolute* error on
every axis (1.8× better at T0, 1.8× at T3), but the declared
readout demanded a better *degradation ratio at equal T0*, and T0 is
not equal — mt2_bscalar's fingerprint on the BC-amplitude axes is
actually the worst of the three (its boundary-scalar channel binds to
the training amplitude). Architecture-driven BC generalization, as
preregistered, was NOT observed: mt2's advantage is in-distribution
accuracy plus geometry robustness (T3 ratio 1.07×), not BC-axis
transfer.

**Readout G3_1 — the fingerprint's starkest row: no arm generalizes
across frequency content.** On T1 (drive modes never seen in
training) every arm reaches rel-L2 ≈ 1.0–1.2 — as bad as or worse
than predicting zero. Even the exactly-linear mt1 fails: linearity
constrains amplitude response but says nothing about basis
coverage — the model has simply never learned the harmonic response
to those modes. This is a *data/coverage* limit, not an architecture
gap, and no candidate mechanism in the program (equivariance,
measure-weighting, BC channels, locality) addresses it. For the
north star: spectrum coverage must be treated like training-set size
— an explicit axis of the data-scaling ledger, not something
structure can provide.

**Program consequence.** G3 delivers the first measured
generalization *fingerprint* decomposition: amplitude extrapolation
is purchasable by contract (declare linearity where the PDE has it —
for aerodynamics, the drive-degree-1 contract MT2 already carries is
exactly this and its value is now measured at 4.5–12×);
geometry extrapolation is mild and slightly favors the equivariant
slice router; frequency-content extrapolation is purchasable by
neither contract nor mechanism tested here. The 3D BC-varying
dataset question (whether to generate one) should be decided on the
axes where architecture can matter — amplitude and geometry — and
those G3 measures now exist.

## 2026-08-24 — GeoTransolver destabilizes; learning-rate parity amendment preregistered {#sec-nb-hl-lr-amendment}

**The setting.** The high-lift wave (prereg
`highlift_wave_preregistration_2026-08-17.json`) is training
GeoTransolver and MeshTransformer2 (v3c config) on the HiLiftAeroML
curated `full` split, 2 seeds each, under the frozen DrivAerML
protocol (lr 3e-3, 500 epochs). At mid-flight (~epoch 250 of 500),
the two architectures' health diverges in a way that must be handled
before results exist, not after.

**The symptom.** Both GeoTransolver seeds destabilize after roughly
epoch 130: seed 42 reaches val loss 0.016 at epoch 134 and then
*rises monotonically* to 0.070 by epoch 255 — training loss rising in
lockstep, so this is optimizer instability, not overfitting; seed 43
dips to 0.013 and re-plateaus at 0.021–0.024. MeshTransformer2
descends smoothly through the identical restart schedule (0.0039 at
epoch 248, still improving), which also rules out the checkpointing
training procedure as the cause. The mechanism is simple: the frozen lr 3e-3
was tuned on DrivAerML where an epoch is 54 optimizer steps; HiLift's
1,260-case training split makes an epoch 315 steps, ~6x more
optimizer steps at any given scheduler position.

**Amendment, preregistered before any lr-1e-3 result exists.** A
learning-rate parity grid, symmetric across architectures per the
steel-man rule: gt_hl_lr1_seed{42,43} and mt2_hl_lr1_seed{42,43} at
lr 1e-3, all else identical (jobs under name hl-lr). Declared
selection rule: for each architecture, the headline high-lift number
is its best val-metric configuration over the grid {3e-3, 1e-3},
with both configurations reported. The 3e-3 lanes run to completion
regardless (a cosine schedule can re-converge late; killing them
would bias against GeoTransolver). H1/H2 readouts of the original
prereg are unchanged — they now just take each architecture's best
lane. Precedent: the DrivAerML lr-parity treatment that produced
MT2's matched-tuning 1.10x (@sec-nb-lit-wave-prereg cites it).

**Also fixed this wave (recorded for reproducibility):** the
Sisyphus trap — the frozen save_interval=50 exceeded the ~35 epochs a
4-hour link covers cold, so early links restarted from epoch 1
(caught by a checkpoint-progress watcher, twice: the second catch was
Slurm snapshotting the batch script at submission, so the fix
required resubmitting the queue, not just editing the script).
save_interval=5 since; checkpoints now track epochs exactly.

## 2026-08-27 — MT2 leads one frozen-rate seed; learning-rate parity pending {#sec-nb-hl-interim}

**INTERIM readout — not the wave verdict.** The first two completed
lanes of the high-lift wave (seed 43 of each architecture, frozen
lr 3e-3, 500 epochs, curated `full` split, 180-case val set) have
been evaluated. Mean relative-L2 over the val set:

| field | GeoTransolver | MeshTransformer2 | ratio GT/MT2 |
|---|---|---|---|
| pressure | 0.1476 | **0.0490** | 3.0x |
| velocity | 0.1731 | 0.0704 | 2.5x |
| wall shear | 0.2709 | 0.1144 | 2.4x |
| temperature | 0.1181 | 0.0525 | 2.2x |
| density | 0.1967 | 0.0667 | 2.9x |

This *reverses* the DrivAerML ordering (GeoTransolver led by
1.10–1.18x there). Two observations, one caveat. **H2 (absolute
difficulty):** MT2's high-lift pressure error (0.049) is *lower* than
its DrivAerML error (0.0633) — the "harder" dataset is easier for
MT2 — while GeoTransolver got 2.8x worse (0.148 vs 0.053). **The
mandatory caveat:** this GeoTransolver lane trained at the frozen
lr 3e-3 where it demonstrably destabilizes on this dataset
(@sec-nb-hl-lr-amendment — best val loss 0.013 at epoch ~130,
plateau at 0.021–0.024 after), so this gap conflates architecture
with optimizer instability. Per the preregistered amendment, the H1
verdict takes each architecture's best over the lr grid {3e-3,
1e-3}; the 1e-3 lanes are at epoch ~240/500. No wave verdict is
declared until they complete, and the seed-42 frozen-lr lanes complete
(~30 epochs remaining each).

**2026-08-27 addendum (frozen-lr wave complete, both seeds).** Seed-42
evals: MeshTransformer2 pressure 0.0452 (2-seed mean **0.0471**,
spread 0.045–0.049 — tight); GeoTransolver pressure 0.3974 (2-seed
"mean" 0.27, spread 0.148–0.397 — the seed-42 lane is the one whose
optimizer visibly diverged, @sec-nb-hl-lr-amendment). At the frozen
lr, GeoTransolver on HiLift is not a usable baseline: the lr-parity
lanes are now fully essential for the H1 verdict.

## 2026-08-31 — Best-rate parity; DrivAerML gap does not transfer {#sec-nb-hl-verdict}

**The wave is complete**: GeoTransolver and MeshTransformer2 (v3c),
2 seeds x 2 learning rates each on the HiLiftAeroML curated `full`
split, evaluated on the sealed-protocol 180-case val set
(`results/highlift_wave_reduction.json`). Mean pressure rel-L2, all
eight lanes:

| arch / lr | 3e-3 (frozen) | 1e-3 (parity arm) |
|---|---|---|
| GeoTransolver | 0.148 / 0.397 (unstable) | **0.0408 / 0.0435** |
| MeshTransformer2 | 0.0452 / 0.0490 | **0.0401 / 0.0425** |

**H1 (the architecture gap on harder physics): the gap does not
transfer — it closes.** At each architecture's best configuration
(lr 1e-3 for both, per the preregistered selection rule), the 2-seed
means are GeoTransolver 0.0422 and MeshTransformer2 0.0413 — a
MT2/GT ratio of **0.98**, i.e. statistical parity with MT2 nominally
ahead, versus GeoTransolver's 1.10–1.18x lead on DrivAerML. MT2 is
also nominally ahead on every other field (velocity 0.059 vs 0.062,
wall shear 0.094 vs 0.101, temperature, density), all within
seed-spread-scale margins.

**H2 (absolute difficulty): HiLiftAeroML is more learnable, not
harder.** Both architectures beat their own DrivAerML pressure
levels (GeoTransolver 0.042 vs 0.053; MT2 0.041 vs 0.063). Combined
with H1 this supports the irreducible-error reading of the DrivAerML
gap that motivated this wave (Corey's suggestion): DrivAerML's
time-averaged transient labels carry a noise floor that the
architectures resolve differently, and on cleaner high-lift labels
both models go lower and the difference evaporates. The claim
"GeoTransolver is architecturally more accurate in-family" does not
survive the dataset change.

**The reproducible architecture difference on this dataset is
optimizer robustness.** MT2's eight lane-results span 0.040–0.049
across both learning rates and both seeds; GeoTransolver spans
0.041–0.397, destabilizing at the lr that its own frozen protocol
prescribed (@sec-nb-hl-lr-amendment). A concise summary for the
program: exact contracts cost MT2 nothing here, MT2 trains stably
where GeoTransolver requires tuning, and in-family accuracy at tuned
settings is a tie.

**Consequence.** The generalization ladder
(prereg `499bcfe8`) launches now with LR_GT = LR_MT2 = 1e-3 per its
declared gate rule. With in-family parity established, the ladder's
data-efficiency rungs (35/210/1260 cases) and OOD axes (AoA
extrapolation, pre-to-post-stall) are the deciding measurements for
the north-star question — whether MT2's structure improves
generalization that GeoTransolver's tuned pointwise attention does
not.

## 2026-09-01 — Campaign review: the month-one instrument was never characterized; agenda reset around measurement, robustness, and resource-normalized comparison {#sec-nb-campaign-review}

A full critical review of the campaign at Peter's request, recorded
here because the review itself reshaped the agenda.

**Central misconception.** The defect-4 to MeshTransformer2 arc
(eleven preregistered iterations) optimized against GeoTransolver's
1.10–1.18x DrivAerML lead without ever measuring DrivAerML's
label-noise floor. High-lift parity (@sec-nb-hl-verdict, MT2/GT =
0.98, both architectures *better* than their DrivAerML levels) says
that lead was substantially a property of the labels, not the
architectures. A second conflation rode along: "harder dataset" was
read as "harder for models"; HiLiftAeroML is harder physics with
cleaner labels.

**Aha moments that survive.** (1) G3 (@sec-nb-g3-verdict): structure
buys generalization exactly on the axes where it is the PDE's own
symmetry, and nothing tested generalizes across boundary-condition
frequency content — a coverage lever, not an architecture lever.
(2) Optimizer robustness is an architecture property: MT2 spanned
0.040–0.049 across the high-lift lr × seed grid, GeoTransolver
0.041–0.397. (3) The M3 audit's parity defect: contracts must be
enumerated from the symmetry group, not from encountered failures.
(4) Four literature hypotheses refuted in a day
(@sec-nb-m1-verdict-wave-close).

**Judgment errors.** The v5a4 anchor-decode arm was closed on an
accuracy-only pilot gate (1.2% miss, one seed) despite running at 65%
of the memory and 3x validation throughput — the resource frame Peter
had explicitly asked for was not applied (@sec-nb-v5a4-gate). M1
scale-relaxation was run on a dataset whose caveat predicted the
null. The "frozen protocol" froze an lr *value* across datasets with
6x different steps per epoch; protocols should freeze procedures (a
grid and a selection rule). The 3.0x interim high-lift headline
should not have been surfaced at all.

**Stones unturned → this wave.** Preregistered as
`results/instrument_wave_preregistration_2026-09-01.json`
(sha `1f6cb942`): **N1** measures the DrivAerML shared-residual
floor directly (cross-model disagreement vs error, per-case error
correlation, shared-residual fraction; HiLift as the cleaner-label
control) — eval-only, the highest-leverage unturned stone; **R1**
symmetric lr-robustness grid {1e-3, 3e-3, 1e-2} × 2 seeds × both
architectures on DrivAerML; **V6** re-opens anchor decode at
matched peak VRAM (v5a4 vs v3c at 6,500 tokens); **W1** trains the
parity fix and reads wall shear. Fourteen single-link DrivAerML lanes
(jobs 635238+, self-resubmitting) plus the eval-only N1 probe.
Still open after this wave: AB-UPT as a measured baseline; the G2
transfer result re-read in light of the noise floor (the running
HiLift ladder is the test); the mechanism of GeoTransolver's lr
instability; two-seed statistical power stated plainly in the book.

**Claims that survive for the book's hero framing:** exact contracts
cost nothing in-family on either dataset; MT2 trains stably where
GeoTransolver needs tuning; exact symmetries buy exact generalization
on their own axes; the measurement methodology is itself novel. The
claim to retire: "beat GeoTransolver in-family."

## 2026-09-01 — N1 verdict: the shared-residual probe does not discriminate; "DrivAerML gap = label noise" is unproven {#sec-nb-n1-verdict}

**The question.** Arm N1 of the instrument wave
(@sec-nb-campaign-review, prereg `1f6cb942`) tested the campaign
review's central reframing: that DrivAerML's 1.10–1.18x GeoTransolver
lead was a property of noisy time-averaged labels rather than of the
architectures. Method: dump per-point pressure predictions from two
GeoTransolver and two MeshTransformer2 checkpoints on bit-identical
val points (verified: max |Δpoints| = max |Δtargets| = 0), and
measure how much of each model's residual is shared across all four.
HiLiftAeroML (lr 1e-3 checkpoints) served as the cleaner-label
control. Results: `results/n1_noise_floor_2026-09-01.json`.

**What we saw** (measure-weighted, mean over cases):

| statistic | DrivAerML (48 cases) | HiLift (180 cases) |
|---|---|---|
| shared-residual fraction (4 models) | 0.713 | 0.703 |
| per-case error correlation GT vs MT2 | 0.887 | 0.968 |
| pointwise residual correlation, cross-arch / same-arch | 0.52 / 0.70 | 0.79 / 0.86 |
| cross-arch disagreement ratio D | 0.927 | 0.914 |
| same-arch seed-pair D (GT, MT2) | 0.66, 0.83 | 0.73, 0.84 |

**Verdict: the instrument does not discriminate, and the review's
attribution is unsupported.** DrivAerML shows the predicted shared
structure (71% of residual energy common to all four models), but the
cleaner-label control shows the *same or more* (70%, with higher
per-case and pointwise correlation). Whatever is shared is not
DrivAerML-specific label noise — or cannot be attributed to it with
this probe. The preregistered falsifier (D ≥ 0.8 with weak
correlation) did not fire; the prediction "D larger on HiLift" failed
on the mean. Two disclosures: (1) the preregistration's thresholds
were not mutually calibrated — for equal-norm residuals
D = √(2(1−ρ)), so D ≤ 0.5 demanded ρ ≥ 0.875 while shared fraction
≥ 0.5 needed only ρ ≥ 1/3; the measured ρ = 0.52 passes one and
fails the other by construction. (2) Shared residual is an *upper
bound* on label noise: the four models share training set, pipeline,
loss, and point subsample, so shared inductive bias is
indistinguishable from label noise here. Attribution needs a
model-free estimate (time-window splits of the DrivAerML averages, or
mesh-refinement pairs), which the shipped dataset does not contain.

**What stands, what falls.** The high-lift *parity* result
(@sec-nb-hl-verdict) is untouched: it is a measurement, not an
attribution. What falls is the review's explanatory story that the
DrivAerML gap "was noise." The honest statement is narrower: the gap
does not transfer across datasets, and the residuals on both datasets
are dominated by structure common to both architectures. **A new
observation worth its own follow-up:** MT2 has larger seed-to-seed
prediction spread than GeoTransolver on both datasets (same-arch D
0.83 vs 0.66–0.73), even though MT2 is far more robust to learning
rate. Hyperparameter robustness and seed variance are different
properties; the R1 arm now running should be read with both in view.
Measure-weighting caveat: unweighted HiLift D drops to 0.64 — the
architectures disagree most in large-area cells.

**2026-09-01 operational addendum (chain design).** The
"self-resubmitting tail" declared in the instrument-wave prereg does
not work: Slurm kills the entire batch script at walltime, so nothing
after `srun` is guaranteed to execute, and the eleven timed-out
first-generation links resubmitted nothing. Two further lessons from
the same day: singleton dependencies key on the job *name*, so array
links of one name serialize behind the slowest lane (the cause of
every "queue drained" wake in the high-lift waves), and Slurm
snapshots the script at submission, so edits never reach already
queued links. The pattern now in both wave scripts: **chain-ahead**
— each link, after its completed/blocked guards, immediately submits
its own successor under a per-lane singleton name
(`inst-wave-<lane>`, `hl-ladder-<lane>`), then trains. Lanes
progress independently, the chain self-terminates when the successor
hits the completed guard, and no human or agent tops up links.

## 2026-09-02 — Instrument wave verdicts: lr robustness confirmed (R1); anchor decode loses resource-normalized (V6); the parity fix costs accuracy (W1, refuted instructively) {#sec-nb-instrument-wave-verdict}

All fourteen DrivAerML lanes of the instrument wave
(@sec-nb-campaign-review, prereg `1f6cb942`) trained and evaluated on
the frozen val instrument (`results/instrument_wave_reduction_2026-09-01.json`).

**R1 — learning-rate robustness: confirmed, with one bound missed.**
Pressure rel-L2 across the symmetric grid (2 seeds at 1e-3 and 1e-2;
the 3e-3 rung is the existing 5-seed result):

| lr | GeoTransolver | MeshTransformer2 |
|---|---|---|
| 1e-3 | 0.0546 / 0.0550 | **0.0588 / 0.0567** |
| 3e-3 | **0.0532** | 0.0633 |
| 1e-2 | 0.739 / 0.221 | 0.0874 / 0.0914 |

GeoTransolver degrades 4–14x at lr 1e-2 (prediction: > 2x, held);
MT2 degrades 1.55x from its best (prediction: < 1.5x, **missed
narrowly**). The spreads differ by far more than the 20% falsifier
band, so robustness is a reproducible architecture property on both
datasets, not a HiLift step-count artifact. A by-product corrects the
DrivAerML ledger: **MT2's best learning rate on DrivAerML is 1e-3
(0.0577), not the frozen 3e-3 (0.0633)**, so the honest best-vs-best
in-family ratio there is 0.0577 / 0.0532 = **1.085x**, consistent
with the earlier single-seed lr-parity figure of 1.10x.

**V6 — anchor-conditioned decode at matched VRAM: the falsifier
fired.** Peak training memory: v5a4 6.35 GB, v3c at 6,500 tokens
6.56 GB (matched within 3%), v3c at 10,000 tokens 9.81 GB. Pressure:
v5a4 **0.209 / 0.221** vs the VRAM-matched control **0.0697 / 0.0671**
— 3.1x worse, far past the 1.3x closure bar. The v5a4 pilot's
near-miss did not reflect its asymptote; at 500 epochs the
anchor-conditioned decode lands where the fully passive v5a3 did
(3.3–3.8x). Also, on DrivAerML its validation step is *slower* than
v3c at 10,000 tokens (0.30 vs 0.21 s), so the throughput advantage
seen on HiLift does not generalize. **M2 stays closed, now for the
stronger reason.** Useful frontier point from the control: dropping
v3c from 10,000 to 6,500 training tokens costs 8% accuracy for 33%
less memory.

**W1 — the parity fix, trained: refuted instructively.** Prediction
was wall-shear improvement > 3% with pressure unchanged. Measured
(2 seeds vs the v3c seeds evaluated on identical points):

| | pressure | wall shear |
|---|---|---|
| v3c (3e-3) | 0.0636 / 0.0627 | 0.0916 / 0.0904 |
| v3c + parity_fix | 0.0706 / 0.0667 (**+8.6%**) | 0.1112 / 0.1049 (**+18.8%**) |

The physically correct head is *worse* on both fields, and pressure
moved even though the scalar path is untouched — the joint loss
routes the vector head's gradients into the shared trunk. Candidate
mechanism (a hypothesis, not a result): the raw pseudoscalar gate
p = r̂·(n̂×d̂) modulates *magnitude* as well as sign, and |p| ≈ 0
wherever r, n, d are near-coplanar — including the entire symmetry
plane of a mirror-symmetric car — so the two e_phi channels are
switched off exactly where the head had been using them. The
reflection-covariance defect is real (M3, @sec-nb-m3-verdict); the
*repair* removed capacity.

**W1' preregistered here, before any run.** Same fix with a
sign-preserving, unit-magnitude odd gate tanh(p / 0.1) — exact
reflection covariance retained (contract test updated to this
variant, 16/16 passing) with the magnitude restored away from p = 0.
Two seeds, same protocol. Prediction: wall shear within 3% of v3c
and pressure within seed spread — i.e., the covariance constraint
itself is free once capacity is restored. Falsifier: still > 10%
worse on wall shear → the e_phi pseudovector channels are
load-bearing in a non-covariant way, which would mean either the
labels are not reflection-covariant (worth checking directly on the
mirror-symmetric cases) or the head needs a different parity-odd
basis, not a gate.

## 2026-09-02 — W1' verdict: restoring gate magnitude halves the penalty but the falsifier fires (+12.6% wall shear); label covariance audit preregistered {#sec-nb-w1p-verdict}

**W1' result** (2 seeds, DrivAerML val, identical points; comparators
v3c seeds 42/43 at 0.0636/0.0627 pressure and 0.0916/0.0904 wall
shear). With the unit-magnitude odd gate tanh(p/0.1):

| | pressure | wall shear |
|---|---|---|
| v3c | 0.0632 | 0.0910 |
