| W1 raw gate p | 0.0686 (+8.6%) | 0.1081 (+18.8%) |
| **W1' tanh(p/0.1)** | **0.0671 (+6.2%)** | **0.1025 (+12.6%)** |

The magnitude hypothesis was *partly* right — restoring unit
magnitude recovers a third of the wall-shear penalty and a quarter of
the pressure penalty — but the preregistered falsifier (still > 10%
worse on wall shear) **fires**. The e_phi pseudovector channels are
load-bearing in a way no parity-odd gate restores. Two candidate
explanations remain, and they are distinguishable without training:

- **L1 (labels are not reflection-covariant).** DrivAerML's
  time-averaged fields on mirror-symmetric cars need not be
  mirror-symmetric (asymmetric wake modes, finite averaging windows,
  mesh asymmetry). If a material fraction of the wall-shear energy is
  mirror-antisymmetric, an exactly covariant head *cannot* fit it by
  construction and the "defect" the M3 audit found was, in effect,
  the head learning the labels' asymmetry. **Preregistered
  measurement:** on mirror-symmetric DrivAerML cases, pair each
  surface point with its mirror image (nearest neighbour after
  reflecting through the symmetry plane) and compute the
  antisymmetric energy fraction ||v(Mx) − M v(x)||² / ||v||² for wall
  shear and |p(Mx) − p(x)|² / |p|² for pressure. Prediction if L1
  explains W1/W1': wall-shear antisymmetric fraction ≳ 10%, larger
  than pressure's. Falsifier: both ≪ 5% → labels are covariant and
  the problem is the head's basis (L2 below).
- **L2 (basis, not parity).** With the e_phi channels gated, the
  true-vector basis is {d, n, r̂, e_θ,n, e_θ,d}; where r̂ is nearly
  parallel to n or d the θ-complements vanish and the basis is
  locally rank-deficient, so the pseudovectors may have been serving
  as a generic tangent completion. Test only if L1 is refuted.

**Program note.** Whatever L1 shows, the parity fix stays in the
codebase default-off: on this dataset a physically correct head is
measurably worse, and the honest statement is that exact
reflection covariance is a contract the *labels* may not honour.

## 2026-09-02 — L1 verdict: DrivAerML labels are mirror-covariant to <1%, but a miscalibrated threshold hides that this can still account for most of the parity penalty {#sec-nb-l1-verdict}

**Measurement** (`results/l1_label_covariance_2026-09-02.json`; 48
val cars at full resolution, 14.6–19.8M cells each, cell-area
weighted). DrivAerML geometry mirrors about y = 0 to 3e-6 m; the mesh
itself is mirror-conformal over the bulk of the surface (median
mirror-pair distance 0.003 cell lengths), and 95% of cells pair
within one cell length. The mirror-antisymmetric energy fractions
of the labels are tiny: **pressure A_p = 0.93%** (mean-subtracted),
**wall shear A_v = 0.67%**, unchanged by k=8 spatial smoothing (so it
is genuine smooth asymmetry, not pairing noise). The least symmetric
channel is the side-force component v_y at 1.9% of its own energy —
the expected weak asymmetric-wake signature — but it carries only
10% of wall-shear energy. Wall shear is *more* symmetric than
pressure.

**Preregistered verdict: the falsifier fires** (both ≪ 5%; the
prediction A_v ≳ 10% missed by 15x). **But the threshold was
miscalibrated**, and this is the second such error this week (N1,
@sec-nb-n1-verdict). I compared an *energy-fraction* statistic to a
*rel-L2 penalty* without converting. The A statistic is 4x the
antisymmetric-part energy, so the truly unfittable wall-shear energy
for an exactly covariant head is A_v/4 = 0.17%. Errors add in
quadrature on a small baseline: sqrt(0.0910² + 0.0017) = 0.0999, a
**+9.8% penalty** in the extreme case where the unconstrained head
fits that component perfectly. The observed W1' penalty is +12.6%
(@sec-nb-w1p-verdict). So label antisymmetry, though below 1% in
energy, can account for *most* of the covariant head's disadvantage.
The lesson for future preregistrations: state thresholds in the
units of the readout they must explain, and derive them.

**The discriminating follow-up (L1b, data-only, dispatched now).**
Compute the same antisymmetry statistic on the *predictions*: the
unconstrained v3c head's val wall-shear predictions, and the
parity-fix head's. If v3c's predictions are as antisymmetric as the
labels (A ≈ 0.67%), the head is exploiting the labels' asymmetry and
L1 accounts for the penalty; if its predictions are nearly symmetric
(A ≪ labels'), the unconstrained head is *not* fitting the
antisymmetric part and the penalty must come from the covariant
basis losing rank where r̂ aligns with n or d (L2). The parity-fix
head's predictions must show A ≈ 0 by construction — a deployment
check of the contract.

**Side result worth keeping.** Mirror pairing gives a *model-free*
handle on label structure that N1 lacked: the antisymmetric energy is
smooth, not point-iid, so DrivAerML's labels carry little white
noise at the cell level; whatever "shared residual" the four models
have in common (N1: 71%) is not iid label noise either.

## 2026-09-02 — L1b: the unconstrained head never exploited label asymmetry (L1 nil, L2 live); true-vector basis arms preregistered {#sec-nb-l1b-l2-prereg}

**L1b result** (`results/l1b_prediction_antisymmetry_2026-09-02.json`).
The mirror-antisymmetry statistic computed on *predictions* at the
10,000-point val subsample, on identical mirror pairs for every model
(pairing error dominates the absolute level, so the exactly covariant
parity heads define the floor and the per-case *excess* over it is
the informative quantity): unconstrained MT2-v3c excess
−0.002 ± 0.001 (i.e. zero), GeoTransolver +0.001, the labels on the
same pairs **+0.012 to +0.016**. The unconstrained head predicts
fields exactly as mirror-symmetric as the constrained ones and does
*not* reproduce the labels' 0.67% antisymmetry. **L1 is nil.** The
covariant head's +12.6% wall-shear penalty is therefore a
representation effect — the gate removes two of seven basis
directions (and where |p| is small, removes them precisely on the
symmetry plane) — not a labels effect.

**L2 preregistered here** (two arms, two seeds each, otherwise the
frozen v3c protocol; thresholds stated in the readout's own units per
the N1/L1 lesson):

- **true5** (capacity control): drop the two e_phi pseudovector
  channels outright, no gate — a 5-vector all-true basis
  {d̂, n̂, r̂, e_θ,n, e_θ,d}. Exactly reflection-covariant by
  construction (contract test added). Prediction: wall-shear rel-L2
  within the W1/W1' band (0.102–0.108, i.e. +12% to +19% over v3c's
  0.091) — the penalty is the lost channels, not the gate.
- **true7** (the fix): replace the two pseudovectors with the *true*
  vectors e_φ,n × d̂ and e_φ,d × n̂ (pseudovector × vector =
  vector), restoring seven directions with exact reflection
  covariance and no gating (contract test: reflection and rotation
  exact to 1e-10). Prediction: wall shear within 3% of v3c
  (≤ 0.094) and pressure within seed spread (≤ 0.066). Falsifier:
  wall shear > 0.100 (> 10% over v3c) → the specific pseudovector
  directions carry something no true-vector completion supplies,
  which would reopen the labels question at the *query-point* level
  (a model-in-the-loop covariance check at exactly mirrored points).

If true7 lands, MT2 gains exact O(3) covariance (rotations *and*
reflections) at no accuracy cost, and the parity_fix gate is
retired in its favour. 18/18 contract tests pass.

## 2026-09-02 — L2 verdict: dropping the pseudovector channels costs +23% wall shear, and the "true7" arm was a derivation error; the real constraint is coefficient parity (W2 preregistered) {#sec-nb-l2-verdict}

**Results** (DrivAerML val, 2 seeds; v3c reference 0.0632 pressure /
0.0910 wall shear):

| basis | pressure | wall shear |
|---|---|---|
| true5 (drop e_φ channels) | 0.0707 (+12%) | 0.1120 (+23%) |
| "true7" (e_φ,n×d̂, e_φ,d×n̂ added) | 0.0716 (+13%) | 0.1146 (+26%) |
| W1 raw gate / W1' tanh gate | +8.6% / +6.2% | +18.8% / +12.6% |

**true5 confirms the capacity reading**: removing the two
pseudovector channels costs about what gating them did (a little
more — the gates at least kept them alive away from the symmetry
plane). **true7 fails its falsifier (> 0.100) — but the arm was
invalid, and the reason is the finding.** e_φ,n × d̂ is perpendicular
to e_φ,n, hence lies in span{r̂, n̂}; likewise e_φ,d × n̂ ∈ span{r̂, d̂}.
The two "new" vectors added no direction, so true7 ≡ true5 within
seed noise, exactly as observed. My derivation error, disclosed.

**The correct statement of the problem.** {r̂, n̂, d̂} already span
R³, so *every* direction is available; what differs is the parity of
the coefficient needed. Components along true-vector directions take
even coefficients; the component along e_φ ∝ n̂ × r̂ (a
pseudovector direction) needs a **parity-odd coefficient**, and the
trunk emits only even invariants. The unconstrained head fakes it
with even coefficients (breaking covariance, M3), the gates supply
oddness through a single pseudoscalar p = r̂·(n̂×d̂) that vanishes
on the entire symmetry plane and wherever r̂, n̂, d̂ are coplanar
(W1, W1'), and the true-vector bases give up the direction (L2).
L1b's finding that the unconstrained head's predictions are already
mirror-symmetric fits: it learned an approximately covariant function
by *using* the e_φ directions off-plane; the exact versions took
those directions away.

**W2 preregistered here: the odd-coefficient head.** Build K = 7
pseudoscalars per point — the triple product of {r̂, n̂, d̂} plus six
triple products involving the point's soft slice anchor position ẑ
and anchor normal m̂ (true, equivariant vectors from a
measure-weighted assignment) — and set each e_φ coefficient to
Σ_k p_k g_k(h) with g even. Exactly O(3)-covariant (reflections and
rotations) and translation-invariant by construction (contract test,
19/19 passing, including a liveness check that the odd channels are
not silently zero); not extinguished where any single pseudoscalar
vanishes. Two seeds, frozen v3c protocol. **Prediction, in readout
units:** wall shear ≤ 0.094 (within 3% of v3c) and pressure ≤ 0.066.
**Falsifier:** wall shear > 0.100 → the even-coefficient pseudovector
head's advantage is not about parity at all but about optimization
(e.g. the two extra unconstrained channels acting as a
better-conditioned overparameterization), which would be tested next
by an unconstrained 9-channel head.

## 2026-09-02 — Independent critic review: two of MT2's stated contracts are not implemented; M4 closure retracted; program reframed {#sec-nb-critic-review}

At Peter's request a fresh-context critic reviewed the whole written
record with no framing from the program (report:
`results/critic_review_2026-09-02.md`, 17 graded claims). The two
most consequential findings were **verified in-session against the
code** before being accepted:

1. **MT2 is not scale-equivariant** (critic C4, confirmed). A
   geometric 2x rescale of the input (points ×2, areas ×4) changes
   the output by **63%** (fp64, random weights). `reference_length`
   is a constant 8.0, and the only "scale" contract test ever written
   (`test_measure_weight_scale_invariance`) checks measure-*weight*
   rescaling — exact to 1e-16 — not geometry. Every chapter that
   calls MT2 "similarity-equivariant" is wrong; the correct statement
   is SE(3)-equivariant (rotations + translations), with a fixed
   length gauge. **Consequence:** the M1 scale-relaxation arm
   (@sec-nb-m1-verdict-wave-close) tested nothing — it appended a
   log-size feature to a model that already saw absolute size — so
   its "refuted" verdict is void, and the literature synthesis's
   over-symmetrization hypothesis was never actually tested.
2. **MT2 is not measure-complete** (critic C6, confirmed). The
   centroid is an unweighted `points.mean`; under 10:1 biased density
   it shifts by **0.94 RMS radii**. The M4 "closed by derivation"
   verdict (@sec-nb-lit-wave-prereg) is **retracted** — the audit
   missed the very first line of the geometry reduction. The P3
   density floor (4.3–4.5x) therefore has an implementation
   component after all.
3. **The drive-degree-1 contract is vacuous in deployment** (C7): the
   recipe feeds a unit vector (`U_inf_dir`), so the output scaling by
   |drive| is identically 1; and physically pressure is degree 2 in
   speed, Cp degree 0. The contract test is exact and the contract is
   irrelevant.

Also accepted from the report: MT2's peak memory is 9.8 GB against
GeoTransolver's 4.6 GB on the same DrivAerML protocol (C16 — the
review chapter's cost table is wrong); the "DrivAerML gap was label
noise" framing survives in chapter 17 despite N1 retracting it
(C14); every 2026-08/09 verdict is two seeds without a paired
statistic; the HiLift dataset config lives only job-locally on AGA;
and the program has been optimizing a 48-case DrivAerML val ratio
rather than its stated boundary→interior generalization objective
(volume recipes exist in the tree and MT2 has never run on them).
Two claims I do not yet accept without checking: that the G3 MT1 arm
used the moment decoder with the proved m ≤ 2 ceiling rather than
the kernel decoder that chapter 6 reports at 0.075 on frequency-OOD
(being re-run, below), and the exact 3.7x density-sensitivity figure.

**Actions taken today, all preregistered before running:**

- **S1 — a real similarity gauge.** New flag `similarity_gauge`:
  measure-weighted centroid and measure-weighted RMS-radius
  normalization replace the unweighted mean and the constant
  reference length. Contract test added for *geometric* scale
  equivariance (points ×k, areas ×k² → identical output) alongside
  the existing weight-scale test. Arms: v3c + gauge, 2 seeds,
  DrivAerML frozen protocol, then the P3 biased-density probe and the
  SHIFT-SUV zero-shot pair on the new checkpoints. Predictions in
  readout units: in-family within seed spread of v3c (≤ 0.066); **P3
  density ratio drops from 4.3–4.5x to below 2x** (the unweighted
  centroid was the dominant density leak); zero-shot estate improves
  from 0.83–0.90 (a truly similarity-covariant model cannot bind to
  DrivAerML's absolute size). Falsifier for the last: estate
  unchanged within seed spread → absolute size was not the transfer
  leak and the G2 mechanism list is back to GeoTransolver's
  pointwise features.
- **P1' — GeoTransolver canonicalization control** (eval-only): align
  each input to a canonical frame from U_inf (and the geometry's
  principal axes for the remaining rotation), run the frozen GT
  checkpoint, rotate outputs back; re-read the P1 rotation orbit. If
  GT recovers its in-pose accuracy off-pose at zero training cost,
  the "equivariance is worth 1.6x" headline is void and MT2's
  rotation robustness is a convenience, not a capability.
- **G3' — rerun the G3 ladder's MT1 arm with the kernel decoder** to
  resolve the chapter-6-vs-G3 contradiction on frequency
  generalization (< 3 GPU-hours).

**Reframing accepted.** MT2 should be described as an SE(3)-equivariant
soft-slice transformer with a learned local geometry basis; the
differentiators that survive are exact rotation/translation
covariance (with the O(3) extension under test in W2), learning-rate
robustness, and the measurement methodology. "Similarity-equivariant",
"measure-complete", "equal-or-lower cost", "drive-degree contract",
and "the DrivAerML gap was noise" are retired from the book pending
the S1 result, and chapters 02 and 17 will be corrected in the same
pass that records S1.

## 2026-09-02 — G3 frequency verdict OVERTURNED: the kernel-decoder MeshTransformer generalizes across BC frequency content (T1 0.070 vs 1.00); the original arm measured a proved nullspace {#sec-nb-g3-kernel-rerun}

**The critic's confound was real.** G3's `mt1_linear` arm used the
*moment* query decoder (`make_model("mesh_transformer", "reference")`,
recorded in every artifact's config block), and chapter 3
(`#sec-ceiling`) *proves* that decoder can emit only angular orders
m ∈ {0, 1, 2} in linear scalar mode. G3's T1 test — drive modes 5–8
with the constant removed — is entirely m ≥ 3 content, so
rel-L2 ≈ 1.0 was structurally guaranteed. The notebook's sentence
"the model has simply never learned the harmonic response to those
modes … a data/coverage limit, not an architecture gap"
(@sec-nb-g3-verdict) was wrong for that arm: it *could not represent*
them. Chapter 6's kernel-decoder result (freq-OOD 0.0748) is on the
same suite and the same OOD axis, under a different training protocol.

**Rerun** (post-hoc decoder control, labelled as such, not
preregistered): arm `mt1_kernel` = the singular-only exact
double-layer kernel decoder, otherwise identical to `mt1_linear`
(linear field mode, explicit gauge, reference capacity; 104k vs 136k
parameters, inside the arm range). Same training set, seeds, epochs,
optimizer, evaluation; ORD job 33696718, 3 seeds. Artifacts
`results/g3/g3_partial_mt1_kernel_seed*.json`,
`results/g3/g3_reduction_with_kernel.json`.

| arm | T0 | T1 modes 5–8 | T2a ×2 | T2b ×4 | T3 geom |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **mt1_kernel** | **0.0158** | **0.0701** (4.4×) | 0.0163 (1.03×) | 0.0154 (0.97×) | **0.0232** (1.46×) |
| mt1_linear (moment) | 0.0723 | 1.0043 (13.9×) | 0.0667 (0.92×) | 0.0632 (0.87×) | 0.0898 (1.24×) |
| mt2_bscalar | 0.0624 | 1.1485 (18.4×) | 0.3883 (6.2×) | 0.7289 (11.7×) | 0.0669 (1.07×) |
| softslice_2d | 0.1114 | 1.2090 (10.9×) | 0.4979 (4.5×) | 0.7760 (7.0×) | 0.1221 (1.10×) |

**Verdict.** The kernel-decoder MeshTransformer **does generalize
across boundary-condition frequency content** (T1 0.070, 14× better
than the moment decoder's 1.00, reproducing chapter 6's 0.075 under
G3's protocol) and is the best arm on every axis: 4× lower
in-distribution error than the next best, exact amplitude
extrapolation from linearity, and the lowest geometry-OOD error. The
G3 "no architecture generalizes frequency content" line is
**retracted**; the correct statement is that the *soft-slice* family
(mt2_bscalar, softslice_2d) and the moment decoder fail on that axis,
while an exact-kernel decoder succeeds. The structural reading: an
exact Green's-function operator carries the PDE's spectral response
for free, whereas learned routing must have seen each mode.

**Why this matters for direction.** This is the strongest
generalization result the program owns, and it belongs to the
architecture line (MT1 / learned boundary-integral operators, chapters
3 and 6) that the program *pivoted away from* to chase DrivAerML
in-family accuracy with GT-class routing — the local hill the critic
identified. The open question is whether the mechanism transfers to
3D aerodynamics, where the exact kernel is the Laplace/potential-flow
double layer and viscous effects are corrections: a **3D
kernel-decoder arm on DrivAerML/HiLift** (the `learned_bie` line,
`results/learned_bie_2026-07-02.json`) is now the highest-value
unturned stone, to be preregistered against the G-ledger axes rather
than in-family accuracy alone.

## 2026-09-02 — P1' verdict: canonicalization gives GeoTransolver exact pose invariance at zero training cost, but a 1.15–1.7x in-pose penalty from sub-degree frame tilt; the "worth 1.6x" headline becomes "worth 1.15–1.2x, plus robustness to pose error" {#sec-nb-p1-canon-verdict}

**The control the critic asked for** (`results/p1_canonicalization_control_2026-09-02.json`;
eval-only, frozen GeoTransolver DrivAerML checkpoints, 2 seeds, 48 val
cases). Canonical frame: U_inf → +x, roll about it from the
area-weighted in-plane covariance (sign from the third moment;
0/48 cases within 5% of eigenvalue degeneracy), vector outputs rotated
back before the metric. Reproduction anchor held bit-for-bit (orbit
raw 32.2x / 30.1x). Incidental finding: the P1 probe's yaml says
"z-rotation" but the transform's default mode is uniform SO(3), so P1
has always been a full-orientation orbit (angles 44–179°) — a stronger
test than documented.

**Results** (pressure rel-L2; ratio to in-pose raw):

| pose | raw GT | canonicalized GT |
|---|---|---|
| in-pose | 0.0530 / 0.0533 (1.00x) | 0.0847 / 0.0918 (**1.60x / 1.72x**) |
| SO(3) orbit | 1.71 / 1.60 (32x / 30x) | 0.0847 / 0.0918 (same as in-pose) |
| yaw 90°, yaw 180°, roll 90° | 17–31x | identical to in-pose to 4 decimals |

Canonicalization makes GeoTransolver **exactly pose-invariant** at
zero training cost — but costs 1.6–1.7x in-pose. The follow-up
control explains why: **GeoTransolver is hypersensitive to sub-degree
frame tilt** — a fixed roll of 0.5° about U_inf costs 1.2–1.3x, 1°
costs 1.7–1.8x, 2° costs 3.2–3.4x, 5° costs 6.5–6.8x. The
canonical frame estimated from the 10,000-cell eval sample is off by
0.82° on average (max 2.2°); estimated from 1M cells it is off by
0.39°, and the canonicalization penalty falls to **1.15–1.19x**
(in-pose and orbit alike).

**Verdict.** The headline "exact equivariance is worth 1.6x" survives
only against rotation *augmentation* (1.84–1.91x). Against the
correct steel-man — canonicalized GeoTransolver with a well-estimated
frame — MT2's exact-equivariance advantage is **~1.15–1.2x**, not
1.6x, and the book's P1 framing must say so. What the control adds is
arguably more valuable than what it removes: a *quantified pose-error
sensitivity* for the non-equivariant baseline (1° → 1.7x) that MT2 is
immune to by construction. In any deployment where the freestream
direction or vehicle alignment carries even a degree of uncertainty,
that is the operative difference, and it is now a measured curve
rather than an argument.

**P1'' preregistered here** (the remaining steel-man step, launched
now): *train* GeoTransolver in the canonical frame (canonicalization
as a dataset transform, 2 seeds, frozen protocol otherwise), so the
model sees the estimator's sub-degree tilt noise during training.
Prediction: canonically trained GT lands within 1.05x of raw GT
in-pose and is pose-invariant; falsifier: penalty stays ≥ 1.15x → the
tilt sensitivity is intrinsic to GeoTransolver's coordinate features,
not an artefact of training in a single pose. Either outcome fixes
the honest exchange rate between exact equivariance and
canonicalization for the book.

## 2026-09-02 — 3D kernel arm scoped: the surface-to-surface kernel decoder already ran and was null; the right next step is a potential-flow oracle gate (K0), then a symmetric feature arm (K1) {#sec-nb-kernel3d-scoping}

**Scoping** (`results/kernel3d_arm_scoping_2026-09-02.md`), prompted
by the G3 kernel result (@sec-nb-g3-kernel-rerun). The naive plan —
"put the exact-kernel decoder on DrivAerML" — is already in the
record: `conf/model/mesh_transformer_surface_flagship.yaml` trained at
scale, and chapter 16's factorial (`#sec-drivaerml-factorial`) shows
its exact members buying 0–8% in-family and nothing zero-shot. The
document argues this null is *structural to the surface-to-surface
formulation* on a 0.1%-coverage point subsample (the exterior trace is
½I + compact K; exact panel integrals on a Monte Carlo sample carry a
~34% quadrature floor), not evidence against the 3D kernel mechanism.
The 2D result's leverage lives in boundary→interior — which is the
program's stated north-star objective, and the axis on which MT2 has
never been run (critic C-hill). Inventory: every piece that
*evaluates* a 3D Laplace kernel exists and is tested
(`kernel_decoder.py` triangle members, Barnes–Hut backend); every
piece that *solves* a learned BIE is 2D/complex-plane-bound.

**Preregistered, in readout units:**

- **K0 — potential-flow oracle gate (eval-only, zero parameters).**
  Exact 3D single/double-layer integrals on a closed coarse remesh per
  vehicle, Neumann data U_inf·n, Morino second-kind solve,
  Bernoulli Cp, compared to DrivAerML val pressure. **Gate: rel-L2
  < 0.90** (a viscous, separated car; prior 0.55–0.80). If the oracle
  is *worse* than that, "exact kernel = Laplace, viscous = learned
  correction" is refuted for this dataset and no learned kernel arm
  runs. Cost: eval-only, < 10 GPU-hours.
- **K1 — symmetric feature arm (conditional on K0 passing).** K0's
  field (Cp_pf and the tangential potential velocity, both exactly
  similarity-invariant with no reference length) as a declared input
  to *both* MeshTransformer2-v3c (lr 1e-3) and GeoTransolver (lr
  3e-3), 2 seeds each. Predictions: in-family unchanged (|Δ| ≤
  0.004); **SHIFT-SUV estate zero-shot improves** (MT2 0.997 → ≤ 0.85,
  GT 0.614 → ≤ 0.55); P3 density ratio ≤ 8x (from 13–14x for
  MT2-v3c on that instrument). Falsifier: neither architecture moves
  ≥ 0.10 on estate → the potential-flow prior does not carry
  transfer, K2 not launched.
- **K2 — mechanism arm (conditional on K1):** exact measure-weighted
  layer operators as a fixed exchange channel inside MT2's slice
  block.
- **K-alt (independent of K0–K2, admits the interior problem):** the
  existing kernel-decoder MeshTransformer, unchanged, on
  `drivaer_ml_volume.yaml` — boundary→interior, where the 2D
  mechanism's spectral leverage actually lives. Deferred until K0
  reads out, to keep the cluster share on S1/W2/P1''/ladder.

**Side facts from the scoping worth keeping:** the one G-ledger axis
the existing kernel-decoder arm already wins is P3 density bias
(1.7–2.1x vs GeoTransolver 3.6x vs MT2-v3c 13–14x on that probe
version); no watertightness check exists anywhere in the aero recipe
(K0 adds a Gauss-identity gate); degree 0, not MT2's degree 1, is the
correct drive law for pressure *coefficients*.

## 2026-09-02 — K0 gate FAILS: inviscid potential flow is not a usable prior for DrivAerML pressure (oracle rel-L2 4.8 vs 0.77 for the case mean); the 3D kernel line does not launch {#sec-nb-k0-verdict}

**Result** (`results/k0_potential_flow_oracle_2026-09-02.json`; 45 of
48 val cars passing the watertightness and Gauss-identity gates;
~6 GPU-hours). The zero-parameter exact potential-flow oracle —
Morino second-kind solve on a closed 4 cm marching-cubes remesh,
Bernoulli Cp, read at the recipe's exact 10,000 evaluation points —
scores a measure-weighted **rel-L2 of 4.79 (median 1.97, every case
> 1.6)** against the CFD pressure. On the same points, predicting
Cp = 0 scores 1.00 and Cp = case mean scores **0.774**. The
preregistered gate (< 0.90) **fails by a factor of five**, and no
numerical explanation survives the controls: clipping outliers gives
1.7; the oracle-optimal affine rescale reaches only 0.73; the remesh
resolution sweep (4/6/8 cm) shows no trend; the sphere validation is
exact (Cp error 0.07%, second-order convergence, Gauss identities to
1e-15). The physics is the failure: 69% of the surface has label Cp
in [−0.5, 0] — the separated-base pressure deficit — where inviscid
flow predicts ≈ 0 to +0.13, and inviscid suction peaks are 2–3× too
strong. **Verdict: for a bluff separated body, "exact kernel =
Laplace, viscous effects = correction" is refuted; K1 and K2 do not
launch on DrivAerML.**

**What this bounds.** The G3 kernel result (@sec-nb-g3-kernel-rerun)
stands: an exact Green's-function operator generalizes for free *when
it is the PDE's operator*. RANS aerodynamics of a car has no cheap
exact operator — the dominant physics is separation — so the
program's "structure buys generalization" thesis is bounded exactly
where the available structure stops matching the PDE. The remaining
kernel path is K-alt (a *learned* density through the exact 3D
double layer on the boundary→interior problem, where the operator is
at least the right *kind*), and it should be argued on that footing,
not on potential flow. Two repo findings for the recipe: the
DrivAerML `vehicle` patch is oriented inward (signed volume
−6.3 to −8.0 m³), and `physicsnemo.mesh.repair.fix_orientation`
propagates by normal dot-product, which fails across folds > 90°.

## 2026-09-02 — W2 collapsed in training (pressure 0.77, wall shear 0.74): an implementation failure, not a parity verdict; W2' (zero-init, bounded pseudoscalars) is the last rung of this thread {#sec-nb-w2-verdict}

The odd-coefficient head (@sec-nb-l2-verdict) trained to a
near-mean predictor on both fields — pressure 0.770 / 0.761, wall
shear 0.743 / 0.738 — so the shared trunk was wrecked, not just the
vector head. The preregistered falsifier fires trivially, but this is
**not** a scientific verdict on coefficient parity: the arm failed to
train. Likely causes, from the code: the odd gate was randomly
initialized (so from step 0 the head emitted large pseudovector-
direction outputs), and the anchor triple products were unbounded
(anchor positions are O(1) in the gauge, but the products enter
unnormalized). **W2'** (launched now, 2 seeds): the odd gate is
zero-initialized so training starts as the stable true5 head and the
odd channels grow from zero, and the anchors are unit-normalized so
every pseudoscalar lies in [−1, 1]; contract tests updated (O(3)
covariance verified with the gate perturbed to non-zero; 23/23).
Prediction unchanged: wall shear ≤ 0.094. **This is the final rung
of the parity thread**: five head variants have been trained
(W1, W1', true5, true7, W2); if W2' also fails to beat 0.100 the
program records "exact O(3) covariance of the vector head costs
≥ 10% wall shear on DrivAerML with every construction tried" and
moves on — the critic's hill-climbing warning applies here.

## 2026-09-03 — Parity thread CLOSED: W2' diverged to NaN at epoch 95; exact O(3) covariance of MT2's vector head costs ≥ 10% wall shear or fails to train under every construction tried {#sec-nb-parity-thread-closed}

W2' (zero-initialized odd gate, unit-normalized anchors, bounded
pseudoscalars) reached epoch 95 and produced `Train Loss: nan`
(both seeds; lanes cancelled at once). With the cap declared in
@sec-nb-w2-verdict, the thread closes. Ledger of the six
constructions, all on the frozen DrivAerML protocol (v3c reference:
pressure 0.0632 / wall shear 0.0910):

| head | reflection covariance | pressure | wall shear |
|---|---|---|---|
| v3c default (pseudovector channels, even coeffs) | violated (M3) | 0.0632 | **0.0910** |
| W1 raw gate p | exact | +8.6% | +18.8% |
| W1' tanh(p/0.1) | exact | +6.2% | +12.6% |
| true5 (channels dropped) | exact | +12% | +23% |
| true7 (invalid: replacements ∈ span{r̂,n̂}) | exact | +13% | +26% |
| W2 odd head (K=7 pseudoscalars) | exact | collapsed 0.77 | 0.74 |
| W2' zero-init, bounded | exact | **NaN @95** | — |

**Closing statement for the book.** MT2's vector head reaches the
e_φ (pseudovector) directions with parity-even coefficients, which
formally violates reflection covariance (M3). The labels are
mirror-covariant to < 1% energy (L1) and the trained head's
predictions are empirically as covariant as the exactly constrained
ones (L1b), so the violation is a *representation convenience* the
optimizer uses, not a physical error the model makes. Every exact
construction tried either removes needed capacity (gates, true
bases: ≥ 12% wall-shear penalty) or destabilizes training (odd
coefficient heads: collapse, NaN). The default head is retained;
`parity_fix`, `vector_basis`, and `odd_head` stay in the code as
documented negative results. The unexplored fix — parity-odd
*features in the trunk* rather than a bolt-on odd head — is left for
MT3's design and is not pursued further here, per the critic's
hill-climbing warning. Six trained variants on one head is where a
demanding reviewer would say stop; we stop.

## 2026-09-03 — P1'' verdict: GeoTransolver trained in the canonical frame is exactly pose-invariant at 1.01x cost; the exact-equivariance accuracy headline is gone {#sec-nb-p1pp-verdict}

**Result** (`results/p1pp_canonical_training_2026-09-03.json`;
2 seeds, DrivAerML val, metrics in the original frame). GeoTransolver
trained with the canonicalization transform in its pipeline (U_inf →
+x, principal-axis roll, the realistic 10,000-cell frame estimate):

| pose | canonically trained GT (s42 / s43) | raw GT reference |
|---|---|---|
| in-pose, no canon at eval | 0.0536 / 0.0535 | 0.0530 / 0.0533 |
| in-pose, canon at eval | 0.0535 / 0.0534 | 0.0847 (1.60x) |
| SO(3) orbit, canon at eval | **0.0536 / 0.0534** | 0.0847 |

**The preregistered prediction held (≤ 1.05x): the penalty is 1.01x.**
The sub-degree tilt hypersensitivity that cost the frozen raw
checkpoint 1.6–1.7x (@sec-nb-p1-canon-verdict) was an artefact of
training in one exact pose; a model that sees the estimator's tilt
noise during training simply learns to ignore it. Canonically trained
GeoTransolver is **exactly pose-invariant** (orbit = in-pose to four
decimals) at a **1% accuracy cost**, with zero architectural change.

**What this does to the program's claims.** The P1 headline —
"exact rotation equivariance is worth 1.6x" — is **retired**. Its
honest replacement: *given a known freestream direction and a
geometry with a resolvable principal frame (both true for every
vehicle dataset in this program; 0/48 degenerate cases),
canonicalization delivers the same pose invariance as exact
equivariance at ~1% cost and no architectural constraint.* The
augmentation baseline (1.84–1.91x) that made equivariance look
valuable was the wrong steel-man. MT2's exact equivariance remains a
genuine *contract* — it holds for any geometry, including ones whose
principal frame is degenerate or whose freestream is unknown — but on
the datasets this program measures, it is not an accuracy advantage.
Combined with high-lift parity (@sec-nb-hl-verdict) and the retired
scale/measure claims (@sec-nb-critic-review), the differentiators MT2
still holds on measured axes are: learning-rate robustness (R1) and
whatever the HiLift generalization ladder shows. This is the critic's
"single biggest risk" materializing, and it is better known than
assumed.

**Generality caveats, so the retirement is not over-read:**
canonicalization needs a known freestream (true in aerodynamics, not
in every PDE surrogate setting) and a sign-resolvable principal frame
(cars: skewness sign 48/48 consistent; a symmetric body would need
another disambiguator); the equivariant model needs neither.

## 2026-09-03 — S1 verdict: the real similarity gauge is free in-family and cuts MT2's biased-density penalty from 13–14.5x to 1.20x; zero-shot transfer unchanged {#sec-nb-s1-verdict}

**Result** (`results/s1_similarity_gauge_2026-09-03.json`; 2 seeds
each, seed-matched against v3c; configs differ only in
`similarity_gauge: true`):

| run | in-family p / wss | estate | fastback | P3 biased (10:1) | P3 ratio |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **v3c + gauge** s42 / s43 | 0.0638 / 0.0922 · 0.0629 / 0.0896 | 1.036 / 0.862 | 1.039 / 0.856 | 0.0766 / 0.0758 | **1.20x / 1.20x** |
| v3c s42 / s43 | 0.0636 / 0.0916 · 0.0627 / 0.0904 | 0.946 / 0.988 | 0.979 / 0.984 | 0.926 / 0.812 | 14.55x / 12.95x |

**Prediction 1 (in-family within seed spread): held.** The
measure-weighted centroid and RMS-radius gauge cost nothing on either
field. **Prediction 2 (P3 density ratio < 2x): held decisively** —
the 10:1 biased-sampling penalty falls from **13–14.5x to 1.20x** on
the p3v3 instrument (biased-sampling error 0.077 against a uniform
0.064). The unweighted centroid *was* the dominant density leak, and
the earlier "information-limited floor" reading (M4,
@sec-nb-lit-wave-prereg, already retracted in @sec-nb-critic-review)
is now positively refuted by measurement: the floor was an
implementation gap. With the gauge, MT2 is the most density-robust
architecture the program has measured on this instrument
(GeoTransolver 3.6x, kernel-decoder MeshTransformer 1.7–2.1x,
MT2-v3c 13–14.5x, **MT2-gauge 1.20x**) — and it is exactly the
property the SE(3) + measure contracts were supposed to deliver.
**Prediction 3 (zero-shot estate improves): falsifier fired.** Estate
0.949 mean vs 0.967, inside a two-seed spread of 0.17 and inside
v3c's own cross-seed range (0.90–1.12); fastback identical. Absolute
size was not the transfer leak; the G2 mechanism list reverts to
GeoTransolver's pointwise features. Disclosure: the preregistration
quoted a v3c estate baseline of "0.83–0.90" that matches no v3c run
(seeds 42–46 span 0.90–1.12) — a transcription error, the third
threshold/baseline slip this week, caught by the seed-matched
re-reduction.

**Adoption.** `similarity_gauge=true` becomes the reference MT2
configuration for all new runs (frozen checkpoints keep the constant
gauge; the flag stays default-off in code for that reason and the
book's MT2 description now states both). The HiLift ladder's MT2
lanes predate this and are recorded as v3c-constant-gauge. The honest
MT2 claim set after this week: exact SE(3) equivariance as a
contract (not an accuracy edge, P1''); learning-rate robustness
(R1); **biased-density robustness at 1.2x** (S1); in-family parity
with GeoTransolver on high-lift and a 1.085x deficit on DrivAerML at
best-vs-best learning rates.

## 2026-09-03 — G5 preregistration drafted (PRE-DATA): single-factor generalization on the forthcoming cfd-datagen corpus; dataset recommendations filed {#sec-nb-g5-prereg}

Peter is generating a new 3D RANS corpus (`~/gh/cfd-datagen`) designed
to isolate generalization factors. A forked session reviewed it and
filed two artifacts, archived here verbatim:
`results/cfd_datagen_feedback_2026-09-03.md` (recommendations to the
dataset run: counterfactual *twin* draws per random-number namespace —
pose, physics, scale, layout, mesh — so single-factor tests are exact
rather than marginal; multiple draws for the val/test geometry banks;
mesh-refinement twins for a per-stratum discretization-error floor;
`body_id` on the no-slip boundary; export of half-window
block-difference fields; realized-regime diagnostics) and
`results/g5_cfd_datagen_generalization_preregistration_2026-09-03.md`
(status PRE-DATA; kept as prose rather than converted to JSON so
nothing is lost in translation).

**G5 in one paragraph.** Six arms on the new corpus, every threshold
in readout units: **A1 pose twins** (exact SE(3) axis — MT2's twin
difference must sit at its own mesh-realization floor; raw
GeoTransolver fails by ≥ 5x on the two profiles without a freestream
frame; canonicalized GeoTransolver matches MT2 within 1.05x where a
frame exists); **A2 scale twins** — the *first real test of the
similarity gauge*, at fixed Reynolds number across 0.02–20 m
(GeoTransolver predicted to exceed 2x at a 10x scale change); **A3
Reynolds twins** (coverage axis — prediction from G2/G3: no
architecture transfers a decade of Re better than another); **A4 mesh
twins** (the label-noise floor that defines "resolvable" for every
other arm — a between-architecture difference smaller than the floor
is reported as not resolvable); **B1 bank-held-out geometry** (the
strong G2, at two training sizes to test the transfer-slope
hypothesis); **B2 profile-held-out boundary conditions** (do explicit
BC operators buy anything on realized 3D flows). Architectures:
GeoTransolver raw and canonicalized, MT2 with the gauge, the
kernel-decoder MeshTransformer as the GLOBE-lineage arm; surface task
first, then the boundary→interior volume task the program has never
run MT2 on. The A-arms are void unless the twin-draw recommendation is
adopted, which is why the preregistration exists before generation.
Tech tree: node **G5 PLANNED**, gated on the corpus launch.
